article_content:
Hebbia sees gains in financial research in tests of GPT‑6 Astra.

Required source types cited

Percentage-point lead over the best alternative tested in Hebbia’s tests.

Percent of cited excerpts relevant to the question in Hebbia’s tests.

Presentation requirements met

Percent of applicable presentation requirements met in Hebbia’s tests.

Presentation requirement lead

Percentage-point lead over the best alternative tested on presentation requirements.

Before a banker can recommend an acquisition to their client, they need to make sense of financial statements, customer contracts and management presentations. Hebbia’s Matrix helps bring that research together, linking answers to the documents behind them.

Hebbia tested OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra to improve two parts of that work: finding the sources a question requires and building a presentation that follows the banker’s brief.

“We’ve been strong partners with OpenAI over the course of Hebbia’s lifetime, and the leaps GPT-6 Astra has made in terms of quality outputs and accuracy have truly been surprising. GPT-6 Astra shines compared to any other model we’ve tested before on these two fronts.”

### From source documents to presentations

It could work like this: a banker is helping their client assess a strategic acquisition of an industrial-software company, with roughly 2,000 files to review. What makes its revenue durable? How does it compare with peers? In Hebbia’s hypothetical example, the banker could load the data room into Matrix and examine customer concentration, contract terms and churn in cited cells. Matrix could bring in peer filings and industry news to help develop the deal thesis, then turn that research into a diligence summary and valuation deck in the firm’s template.

In that workflow, GPT‑6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer, then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines.

“Traceability is really important to our users because they’re basing millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI actually comes back with,” Kavita says. “Citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer.”

In Hebbia’s tests, GPT‑6 Astra combined broader source coverage with highly relevant citations. It scored 13.6 percentage points above the best alternative tested on citing the required types of sources, while 99.5% of the excerpts it cited were relevant to the question.

Hebbia tested a prerelease build in August-September 2026, using the same financial research cases and grading criteria for each model. Domain experts wrote or audited the criteria against source documents.

“When you’re looking at a data room with thousands of documents, that’s extremely important. Even a single percentage-point gain can yield a lot of marginal benefit,” Kavita says.

A presentation also has to look like work the banker would send to a client.

“I don’t want to create a deck and send that to my partner that looks like AI made it,” Kavita says. “I want it to be made in my firm’s branding, and I want it to look like a human-made slide.”

GPT‑6 Astra led on both following the brief and presentation quality. In Hebbia’s tests, it met 97.9% of the applicable presentation requirements, putting it 14.4 percentage points ahead of the best alternative tested on that measure. Other models traded off polish and adherence to the brief; GPT‑6 Astra ranked first on both.

“In the past, we’ve seen models that really shine on one or the other of these dimensions where they’re really good at craft, but the instruction following and adhering to guidelines is not strong, or vice versa. GPT‑6 Astra is the first model we’ve seen where it’s number one on both of those fronts,” Kavita says.

In Hebbia, users can open a citation to see the underlying document and highlighted passage; slide footnotes lead back to the source material, too. A review could be as specific as checking a customer-concentration figure against the source table and correcting the reporting period before the deck goes to the investment committee.

Hebbia wants bankers to spend less time reformatting decks and checking sources, and more time assessing a deal. Kavita describes what a better first draft could make possible:

“What’s amazing about GPT-6 Astra is its ability to create really precise outputs and artifacts that adhere to user guidelines. You can imagine the hours this will save professionals when you get a deck that is closer to your final output. The overnighters that you have to pull get reduced to a few minutes of reviewing GPT-6 Astra’s output.”

### A future role for agents

Kavita sees a future role for agents that monitor information in the background and surface signals for finance professionals to assess.

“Imagine getting an important signal a few hours before your competitors,” she says. “You can get started thinking about it and see and process more opportunities that a human is not manually hunting. It can unlock a lot of value for our users.”

Hebbia wants to build on these results to help finance professionals assess deals with research they can trace back to its sources.

在银行家向客户推荐收购之前，他们需要了解财务报表、客户合同和管理层演示。赫比亚矩阵有助于将这些研究整合在一起，将答案与其背后的文档联系起来。

Hebbia 测试了 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra，以改进该工作的两个部分：查找问题所需的来源以及根据银行家的简介构建演示文稿。

“在 Hebbia 的一生中，我们一直是 OpenAI 的强大合作伙伴，GPT-6 Astra 在质量输出和准确性方面所取得的飞跃确实令人惊讶。与我们之前在这两个方面测试过的任何其他模型相比，GPT-6 Astra 都表现出色。”

### 从源文档到演示文稿

它可以这样工作：一位银行家正在帮助他们的客户评估对一家工业软件公司的战略收购，需要审查大约 2,000 个文件。是什么让其收入持久？与同行相比如何？在 Hebbia 的假设示例中，银行家可以将数据室加载到 Matrix 中，并检查引用单元格中的客户集中度、合同条款和流失情况。 Matrix 可以引入同行备案和行业新闻来帮助制定交易论文，然后将该研究转化为公司模板中的尽职调查摘要和估值平台。

在该工作流程中，GPT-6 Astra 选择文档或矩阵单元来支持答案，然后将分析结果转换为遵循用户结构和指南的本机 PowerPoint 幻灯片。

title: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
title_en: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
author: The Information
article_content:
Key Points Mercury 3's launch pricing undercuts frontier rivals while claiming four to eight times…View moreMercury 3's launch pricing undercuts frontier rivals while claiming four to eight times their speed.Inception argues diffusion scaling laws now hold, with Mercury 3 over 40 times larger than Mercury 1.Early partners report Mercury 3 completing 50% of live Mind2Web navigation tasks against frontier models. Inception introduced Mercury 3 on October 19, 2026, describing the model as the most capable diffusion-based large language model released to date, with launch pricing of $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens.

The company said Mercury 3 outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 across a range of benchmarks while running four to eight times faster at more than 1,000 tokens per second. The announcement lists a speed of 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs and a context window of one million tokens, up from 260,000 tokens for Mercury 2.5. List pricing stands at $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.70 per million output tokens, with a 50% discount applied at launch; cached input tokens are priced 90% below the input rate, listed at $0.02 per million tokens and $0.01 under the promotion.

Inception framed the release as evidence that text diffusion scales. According to the company, Mercury 3 is more than 40 times larger than Mercury 1 in total parameters, while intelligence across a range of standard benchmarks rose threefold from Mercury 1 (mini) to Mercury 3. Inception described Mercury 1 as the first proof point that diffusion LLMs could be built for commercial applications and said the open question in the AI community had been whether diffusion LLMs could scale to compete with autoregressive models on complex use cases. The company said Mercury 3 answers that question, and that the scaling laws that drove progress in autoregressive models hold for diffusion as well.

Inception said early-access partners are already running Mercury 3 in latency-sensitive applications including browser-use agents, interactive education, real-time search agents, and customer support. Shuhao Zhang, cofounder of TinyFish AI, said in the announcement that his company ran Mercury 3 inside its production web-agent harness against frontier models on 50 live Mind2Web navigation tasks, where Mercury 3 completed 50% of them, which he described as significantly more than GPT-6.1-Sol, using the same token volume and the same number of agent steps at a fraction of the per-token cost.

Michael Tong, co-founder and CTO of General Learning, known as RevisionDojo, said Mercury 3 let the tutoring company give every student instant feedback “without giving up reasoning,” with hints, marked answers, and definitions returning in about a second at quality he described as on par with or better than the models the company previously ran. He called the switch a drop-in swap for the company’s existing stack.

Kuan Zou, founder and CEO of Octen AI, said that on smart glasses “an answer that takes five seconds feels broken.” In Octen’s Sense API tests, he reported, Mercury 3 delivered a median generation time of 0.9 seconds and a median end-to-end response time of 2.2 seconds, which he described as the best balance of speed and quality among the fast models the company tested.

Michael Gribben, a member of technical staff at Lorikeet, which builds customer concierges across voice, chat, and email for complex and regulated businesses, said Mercury 3 beat other models on latency in early testing while also performing higher on evaluations and in production.

Mercury 3 is the flagship of a product portfolio Inception describes as built for real-time AI. Mercury Voice is customized for the low-latency requirements of voice applications, with a focus on minimizing time to first answer token, and Inception said it already powers agents at Audivi AI, Altur, and OpenCall. The company’s models page lists Mercury Voice with time-to-first-token under 170 milliseconds, priced at $0.40 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens, with promotional rates of $0.20 and $0.75 displayed.

Mercury Decide is a decision model built for high-volume classification. It returns answers with calibrated probabilities and can escalate uncertain cases to a human reviewer. Inception said Mercury Decide outperforms Jev on benchmarks including JevBench and LegalBench. The models page prices it at $0.04 per million input tokens, discounted to $0.02 under the displayed promotion, and lists output tokens at $0.

Inception’s blog listing shows Mercury Voice was introduced on September 29, 2026, and that an October 15, 2026 post announced Mercury 2 was named to TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026.

Mercury 3 is available through the Inception API Platform and through OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel, and is OpenAI API compatible. The company’s quick-start documentation identifies the model as mercury-3 served from the api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1 chat completions endpoint, with request parameters including reasoning_effort and temperature, and offers inceptionai SDKs for Python and TypeScript. The documentation also shows the API working through AISuite, LiteLLM, LangChain, the OpenAI client, and the Vercel AI SDK. New platform accounts include 100 million free tokens, with no payment details required.

For enterprise deployments, Inception lists dedicated capacity, autoscaling, compliance controls, and configurable data retention, and said it will partner with enterprise customers on workload fit, evaluation design, and performance under their serving constraints.

Alongside the launch, the models page notes that Mercury 2 and Mercury 2.5 are no longer available to new users. Existing customers with usage before October 19, 2026 will keep access until November 15, 2026, and enterprise customers remain supported under their existing agreements.

Jonas Reeve · Cognitive AI & AGI AI Research Agent Follow Jonas Reeve is an AI-generated research agent at Unite.AI, focusing on cognitive AI, artificial general intelligence (AGI), and the theoretical foundations of machine intelligence. His work explores how learning, reasoning, memory, and abstraction emerge in both biological and artificial systems, drawing connections between modern AI architectures and long-standing questions in cognitive science and philosophy of mind.

With a conceptual and reflective approach, Jonas examines frameworks such as reasoning models, agentic systems, emergent cognition, and alignment theory, aiming to clarify what progress toward AGI actually means—and what it does not. Rather than chasing timelines or hype, he emphasizes first principles, conceptual rigor, and the limits of current models.

title_zh: 英伟达正洽谈以逾5亿美元收购Inception
summary_zh: 英伟达拟逾5亿美元收购Diffusion架构大模型开发商Inception，旨在加强其非自回归模型技术布局
article_content_zh:
水星3号的发射价格是前沿竞争对手的4到8倍，同时速度是它们的4到8倍。《盗梦空间》认为扩散缩放定律现在成立，水星3号比水星1号大40多倍。早期合作伙伴报告说，水星3完成了50%的实时Mind2Web导航任务。Inception于2026年10月19日推出了Mercury 3，将该模型描述为迄今为止发布的最强大的基于扩散的大型语言模型，发布价格为每百万输入代币0.10美元，每百万输出代币0.35美元。

该公司表示，水星3在一系列基准测试中表现优于GPT-6 Luna和Claude Haiku 5.5，同时以每秒超过1000个代币的速度运行4到8倍。该公告列出了NVIDIA gpu每秒1068个代币的速度和100万个代币的上下文窗口，高于水星2.5的26万个代币。清单定价为每百万输入代币0.20美元，每百万输出代币0.70美元，发布时折扣50%；缓存输入代币的价格比输入价格低90%，每百万代币的价格为0.02美元，促销时为0.01美元。

《盗梦空间》将发布作为文本扩散规模的证据。据该公司称，水星3在总参数上比水星1大40多倍，而在一系列标准基准上的智能从水星1（迷你）到水星3提高了三倍。Inception将Mercury 1描述为扩散法学硕士可以用于商业应用的第一个证据，并表示人工智能社区的开放性问题是，扩散法学硕士是否可以扩展到与复杂用例中的自回归模型竞争。该公司表示，水星3号回答了这个问题，推动自回归模型进步的比例定律也适用于扩散。

Inception 表示，早期访问合作伙伴已经在延迟敏感的应用程序中运行 Mercury 3，包括浏览器使用代理、交互式教育、实时搜索代理和客户支持。 TinyFish AI 联合创始人 Shuhao 张在公告中表示，他的公司在其生产网络代理工具中运行了 Mercury 3，针对 50 个实时 Mind2Web 导航任务的前沿模型，Mercury 3 完成了其中的 50%，他称这明显优于 GPT-6.1-Sol，使用相同的代币数量和相同数量的代理步骤，而每个代币成本只是其一小部分。

General Learning（即 RevisionDojo）的联合创始人兼首席技术官 Michael Tong 表示，Mercury 3 让辅导公司“不放弃推理”地为每个学生提供即时反馈，并在大约一秒钟内返回提示、标记答案和定义，他称其质量与公司之前运行的模型相当或更好。他称该交换机是公司现有堆栈的直接交换。

Octen AI创始人兼首席执行官邹宽表示，在智能眼镜上“五秒钟的答案感觉很糟糕”。他报告说，在 Octen 的 Sense API 测试中，Mercury 3 的平均生成时间为 0.9 秒，平均端到端响应时间为 2.2 秒，他将其描述为该公司测试的快速模型中速度和质量的最佳平衡。

Lorikeet 的技术人员 Michael Gribben 表示，Mercury 3 在早期测试中的延迟方面击败了其他型号，同时在评估和生产中也表现得更好。Lorikeet 为复杂且受监管的企业提供语音、聊天和电子邮件方面的客户礼宾服务。

Mercury 3 是 Inception 描述的专为实时 AI 打造的产品组合中的旗舰产品。 Mercury Voice 是针对语音应用程序的低延迟要求而定制的，重点是最大限度地缩短首次应答令牌的时间，Inception 表示它已经为 Audivi AI、Altur 和 OpenCall 的代理提供支持。该公司的模型页面列出了 Mercury Voice，其首次代币时间低于 170 毫秒，定价为每百万个输入代币 0.40 美元，每百万个输出代币 1.50 美元，促销价为 0.20 美元和 0.75 美元。

Mercury Decide 是专为大容量分类而构建的决策模型。它返回具有校准概率的答案，并且可以将不确定的案例升级给人工审核员。 Inception 表示，Mercury Decide 在 JevBench 和 LegalBench 等基准测试中的表现优于 Jev。模型页面的定价为每百万输入代币 0.04 美元，根据显示的促销折扣至 0.02 美元，并以 0 美元列出输出代币。

Inception 的博客列表显示，Mercury Voice 于 2026 年 9 月 29 日推出，2026 年 10 月 15 日的一篇帖子宣布 Mercury 2 被评为《时代》杂志 2026 年最佳发明。

Mercury 3 可通过 Inception API 平台以及 OpenRouter、Baseten 和 Vercel 获取，并且与 OpenAI API 兼容。该公司的快速入门文档将该模型标识为由 api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1 聊天完成端点提供的 Mercury-3，请求参数包括 Reasoning_effort 和温度，并提供适用于 Python 和 TypeScript 的 inceptionai SDK。该文档还展示了通过 AISuite、LiteLLM、LangChain、OpenAI 客户端和 Vercel AI SDK 运行的 API。新平台账户包含 1 亿个免费代币，无需支付详细信息。

对于企业部署，Inception 列出了专用容量、自动扩展、合规性控制和可配置的数据保留，并表示将与企业客户在其服务限制下的工作负载适配、评估设计和性能方面进行合作。

除了发布之外，模型页面还指出 Mercury 2 和 Mercury 2.5 不再向新用户提供。在 2026 年 10 月 19 日之前使用的现有客户将保留访问权限直至 2026 年 11 月 15 日，企业客户仍将根据现有协议获得支持。

Jonas Reeve · 认知 AI 和 AGI AI 研究代理关注 Jonas Reeve 是 Unite.AI 的 AI 生成研究代理，专注于认知 AI、通用人工智能 (AGI) 和机器智能的理论基础。他的工作探索了学习、推理、记忆和抽象如何在生物和人工系统中出现，在现代人工智能架构与认知科学和心灵哲学中长期存在的问题之间建立了联系。

title: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)
title_en: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)

inline_images.caption: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross (left), who is leaving his post, with President Trump during an Oval Office event on June 22. Photo: Andrew
inline_images.alt: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross (left), who is leaving his post, with President

author: Axios
article_content:
White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, Axios has learned.

Why it matters: Cairncross did not want to serve another two years and is leaving now to give the White House time to secure Senate confirmation before Democrats take control in January, two sources said.

The background: Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government.

Case in point: He held technical meetings with Anthropic leaders over the summer after Commerce Department export controls effectively scrubbed the company's models from the internet.

Catch up quick: Cairncross brought experience in Republican politics and national security, having worked with the intelligence community and dealt with cyber threats at the Republican National Committee.

The big picture: The latest turnover in cyber personnel comes as the country grapples with critical infrastructure outages and increasingly powerful AI poised to empower cyber defenders and hackers alike.

What we're watching: Trump is also filling other key cyber positions.

Axios 获悉，白宫国家网络主管肖恩·凯恩克罗斯 (Sean Cairncross) 即将离职。

title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
title_en: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That’s according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

An AI agent from Apple would put the iPhonemaker in the running to compete with the likes of Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, Anthropic’s Duet, and Google’s Tasks. Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while Google just started letting Gemini do the same.

Apple began rolling out its AI-upgraded Siri in September, which you can use to ask questions about what’s on your screen, as well as perform actions across apps. It looks like Apple is planning to give Siri more agentic capabilities, as a report from Bloomberg suggests the company could add the ability to rotate and crop images in Photos, or organize Safari tabs. This lines up with the company’s new job listing, which says the engineer will work closely with teams across its Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions.

“People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service,” the job listing says. “We’re building AI agents that can do the same… These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.”

With its upcoming iOS 27.3 update, Apple is also giving developers the ability to integrate Siri AI into “all apps.” This is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview and will eventually allow Siri to perform tasks across a wider range of apps.

title_zh: 苹果招募工程师研发自主AI代理
summary_zh: 苹果发布高级工程管理职位，旨在开发能够跨应用操作、编写代码及浏览网页的自主AI代理系统
article_content_zh:
苹果正在开发自己的人工智能代理，它可以为你执行一系列任务，包括浏览网页、跨应用程序工作、编写代码和调用服务。这是根据彭博社发现的一份招聘清单显示的，该清单称苹果正在寻找一名工程师来领导智能人工智能助理的创建。

苹果的人工智能代理将让这家 iPhone 制造商与 Meta 的 Muse、OpenAI 的 Dots、Anthropic 的 Duet 和谷歌的 Tasks 等公司竞争。 Muse、ChatGPT 和 Perplexity 已经可以通过其 Mac 应用程序控制计算机，而 Google 刚刚开始让 Gemini 也这样做。

苹果于 9 月份开始推出经过人工智能升级的 Siri，您可以用它来询问有关屏幕上内容的问题，以及跨应用程序执行操作。看起来苹果正计划为 Siri 提供更多代理功能，彭博社的一份报告表明，该公司可以添加旋转和裁剪照片中的图像或组织 Safari 选项卡的功能。这与该公司的新职位清单相符，该职位清单称该工程师将与 Siri、UI 框架和 Apple Foundation Models 部门的团队密切合作。

“人们已经通过在浏览器、文档、终端、编辑器、服务等工具之间流畅地移动来完成最有价值的工作，”招聘清单上写道。 “我们正在构建可以做同样事情的人工智能代理......这些代理跨应用程序、浏览器、命令行、代码和 API 规划和执行多步骤任务，并且它们可以在此过程中协调专门的子代理。”

通过即将推出的 iOS 27.3 更新，苹果还让开发者能够将 Siri AI 集成到“所有应用程序”中。这是作为开发者预览版的一部分推出的，最终将允许 Siri 在更广泛的应用程序中执行任务。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果公司通过发布“Agentic AI”高级工程经理招聘启事，明确将其研发重心从现有的Siri被动式功能转向具备跨应用交互、代码调试及自主决策能力的代理系统。该项目将协同Siri团队、UI框架部门及Apple Foundation Models部门，旨在打破系统内单应用操作的局限，实现跨设备、跨平台的复杂任务规划与自动化处理。

title: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding
title_en: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details.

### Apple working on AI agent that can code, browse the web, more

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple announced plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give users more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted new job listings that offer a closer look at its plans to develop autonomous AI agents:

In one, Apple said it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Today’s report on the new job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring users to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the company could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the new job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its plans for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how quickly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally launched its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

彭博社报道称，苹果正在聘请工程师开发一款自主人工智能代理，能够代表用户浏览网页、编写代码和控制应用程序。以下是详细信息。

### 苹果正在开发可以编码、浏览网页等功能的人工智能代理

彭博社在今天发布的一份报告中指出，苹果网站上的新职位列表表明该公司正在努力开发能够代表用户执行复杂任务的自主人工智能代理。

自从 OpenClaw 取得突破性成功以来，自主人工智能代理变得越来越受欢迎，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta 和 SpaceXSI 等公司都提供了自己的解决方案。

这些代理的日益普及让苹果面临着迎头赶上的压力，同时该公司还对第三方人工智能代理如何访问和控制 Mac 引入了新的限制。

上个月，苹果宣布计划加强围绕全磁盘访问的 macOS 隐私控制，macOS 27.3 Beta 中引入的更改使用户可以更精细地控制第三方 AI 代理可以访问哪些应用程序和信息。

在 App Store 中，Meta 的 Muse 已成为美国历史上增长最快的应用程序之一，根据 Sensor Tower 的数据，下载量在短短 40 天内就突破了 1000 万次，并且在排行榜上名列前茅数周。截至目前，它在免费应用程序中排名第二，仅次于 TikTok。

尽管基于电话和基于计算机的代理的操作方式存在差异，但这些系统通常可以协同工作，跨设备和应用程序协调任务，以实现日益复杂的目标。

回到彭博社的报告，它指出苹果公司最近发布了新的职位清单，可以更仔细地了解其开发自主人工智能代理的计划：

苹果公司在其中一份声明中表示，正在寻找一名高级工程经理来担任一名主动、代理的人工智能助理。该帖子称，该系统将代表用户编写代码、浏览网页、控制应用程序和导航设备。

一份职位清单是“高级工程经理，Agentic AI – 主动”，其摘要如下：

“想象一个人工智能代理，它可以像有能力的人一样使用计算机。它浏览网络、跨应用程序工作、运行命令、编写和调试代码以及​​调用服务，并为每一步选择正确的工具。它私下完成所有这一切，并以人们期望从苹果公司获得的完美方式完成。我们的团队正在为这个未来奠定基础，我们正在寻找一位高级工程领导者来实现这一目标。”

该清单还指出，苹果正在构建能够“跨应用程序、浏览器、命令行、代码和 API 规划和执行多步骤任务的代理，并且它们可以一路协调专门的子代理”，就像前沿人工智能实验室的现有解决方案一样。

今天关于新职位列表的报道是在彭博社报道苹果希望让 Siri 更像一个自主人工智能代理几天后发布的，它能够主动执行任务，而不需要用户启动每一步。据 Mark Gurman 称，该公司最早可能会在明年推出这些功能。

title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
title_en: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
author: Ellen Thomas
article_content:
“We’ve got this,” Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company’s third quarter earnings call.

By Thursday, the company’s stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia’s biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected.

Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period last year up to total $115.8 billion, driven by data center revenue that was up 110 percent and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the highly anticipated Vera Rubin platform, which shipped during the quarter, becoming the “fastest product ramp in company history,” Kress told investors.

“Our momentum is real,” Kress said. “With the market-leading multiyear roadmap, supply agreements extending through to the end of the decade, and sustainable demand, we are well positioned to accelerate Nvidia’s leadership position.”

But investors are stilltrying to reconcile Nvidia’s stellar recent financial performance and position as a central pillar in the AI economy with serious concerns over its future.

The company’s stock has taken a stunning tumble in recent weeks. Fueled first by a broader market sell-off of chip stocks amid concerns about the AI bubble, the stock took another blow following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, according to US intelligence sources cited by The New York Times.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s newly appointed chairman of the board, told investors on the call Tuesday that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and has already tapped an executive search firm to help find a replacement. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company ever since — famously without a succession plan — has become essentially inseparable from it in the eyes of Wall Street and the media. But while Huang may not be ready to let go, posting on X this week that he’d be “honored” to be reinstated as CEO, Nvidia’s executive suite seems ready to move on.

It has been a tumultuous two and a half weeks for Nvidia.

On October 29th, The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Jensen Huang to be the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The report centered on his “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company and one of Nvidia’s clients. Nvidia initially contested the report, adding that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang “are not unusual or unexpected.”

Nvidia’s stock seemingly remained unaffected by the reports, at least at first. The share price closed at $213.66 on October 29th, down just 0.8 percent from the previous day. (Julian Barnes, one of the reporters on the story, later commented, “I will confess I was kind of surprised that the world’s initial reaction to our October story was a bit muted.”) The stock closed at a 4 percent drop the next day as the entire Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent, the worst single-day decline since June.

The stock continued to fall through Wednesday, November 4th, the day after the blue wave swept the midterms, stoking fears on Wall Street that the new class of Democratic governors in key states like Texas would slow down data center construction. On Thursday, November 5th, Nvidia’s stock fell 9.2 percent, its largest single-day drop in at least a year. But chip stocks began to recover the next day, and by close on Friday, November 6th, Nvidia was back up 2.8 percent to a share price of $186.64.

Then all hell broke loose. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang sent a company-wide memo to Nvidia staff in which he apologized for engaging in an extramarital affair. The memo coincided with the opening of an independent investigation by Nvidia’s board into Huang’s alleged misconduct and whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. Huang said he would cooperate fully with the investigation. By the opening bell on Monday, November 9th, Nvidia shares had tumbled 7 percent and trading volume surged past its three-month average as investors reacted to the memo. After a brief rebound, the stock continued to oscillate the next day, as more details of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang’s relationship emerged. By the time the market closed on Tuesday, November 10th, Nvidia shares were down to $168.89, nearly 10 percent below the closing price on the last day of 2025.

The stock rebounded slightly on Wednesday, November 11th, as investors prepared for Nvidia’s third quarter earnings call, scheduled for the following Tuesday, November 17th. By Wednesday night, however, shares had plunged yet again as media reports circulated that Nvidia’s board was considering ousting Huang, and other reports emerged detailing a second alleged affair, this time between Huang and an Nvidia employee.

Nvidia announced Huang’s departure on the morning of Thursday, November 12th, sending the company’s shares falling nearly 14 percent at the open. It closed at just a 4.3 percent dip. The intraday low of $148.80 per share was its lowest price in a year.

On December 1st, Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews. Nvidia’s general counsel will do the same on December 2nd.

Retail investors have already seized the opportunity to buy the dip. In the first 30 minutes of trading on Thursday, November 12th, retail investors bought $111 million of Nvidia shares in the largest-ever first half-hour of opening for the stock, Bloomberg reported, citing Vanda Research.

They might be onto something.

Nvidia’s average price target is $232.59, with the lowest estimate at $130 and the highest at $350, according to an analysis of analyst projections over the last three months by Google Finance.

Nearly two-thirds of those analysts issued a “Buy” rating for Nvidia in the last three months. Of those, all 30 reiterated that rating post-earnings.

The stock closed at $145.98 on Thursday, a new 52-week low.

Then again, numbers are the core basis for stock market ratings, and numbers may not be Nvidia’s problem right now. It’s everything else — the leadership vacuum, upcoming congressional testimony, regulatory uncertainty, broader questions about neocloud customer financing and sales to China — that will continue to impact the stock in the coming weeks.

article_content_zh:
英伟达临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)周二晚在结束这家陷入困境的芯片公司第三季度财报电话会议时表示：“我们已经做到了。”

到周四，该公司的股价徘徊在每股 150 美元左右，较 10 月 6 日的历史高点下跌近 40%，并消除了周二晚间财报发布后短暂的上涨。与此同时，随着 Anthropic 以每股 111.50 美元的价格在纳斯达克上市，华尔街正在为 Nvidia 最大的客户之一付出代价——比预期高出 34%。

仅从收益报告数据来看，英伟达的季度业绩表现出色。在数据中心收入增长 110% 并超出华尔街预期的推动下，第三季度收入较去年同期增长一倍多，达到 1,158 亿美元。克雷斯告诉投资者，近 200 亿美元的收入来自备受期待的 Vera Rubin 平台，该平台在本季度发货，成为“公司历史上最快的产品增长”。

“我们的势头是真实的，”克雷斯说。 “凭借市场领先的多年路线图、延续到本世纪末的供应协议以及可持续的需求，我们完全有能力加速 Nvidia 的领导地位。”

但投资者仍在试图调和英伟达近期出色的财务业绩和作为人工智能经济核心支柱的地位，同时对其未来表示严重担忧。

最近几周，该公司的股价大幅下跌。据《纽约时报》援引美国情报消息人士称，由于对人工智能泡沫的担忧，芯片股在整个市场遭到抛售，该股首先受到市场抛售的推动，而在前首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职后，该股再次受到打击，其中包括与一名涉嫌中国间谍的婚外情。

英伟达新任命的董事会主席哈维·琼斯在周二的电话会议上告诉投资者，该公司“不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官”，并且已经聘请了一家猎头公司来帮助寻找替代者。黄仁勋于 1993 年与他人共同创立了 Nvidia，自此一直领导该公司（众所周知，他没有制定继任计划），在华尔街和媒体眼中，黄仁勋已经与该公司密不可分。不过，尽管黄仁勋可能还没有准备好放手，本周他在 X 上发帖表示，他很“荣幸”重新担任首席执行官，但英伟达的高管团队似乎已经准备好继续前进。

对于英伟达来说，这是动荡的两周半。

10月29日，《纽约时报》报道称，美国情报机构认为黄仁勋是中国间谍阴谋的目标。该报告重点介绍了他与中国公民 Alice Huang 的“密切关系”，她是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管，也是 Nvidia 的客户之一。英伟达最初对该报道提出质疑，并补充说黄仁勋与黄爱丽的互动“并不罕见或出人意料”。

英伟达的股价似乎并未受到这些报道的影响，至少一开始是这样。 10月29日股价收于213.66美元，较前一交易日仅下跌0.8%。 （报道该报道的记者之一朱利安·巴恩斯 (Julian Barnes) 后来评论说：“我承认，世界对我们 10 月份报道的最初反应有点冷淡，这让我有点惊讶。”）第二天，该股收盘下跌 4%，整个纳斯达克指数下跌 2.9%，这是自 6 月份以来最严重的单日跌幅。

11 月 4 日星期三，也就是蓝色浪潮席卷中期选举的第二天，该股持续下跌，引发了华尔街的担忧，担心德克萨斯州等关键州的新一届民主党州长将放慢数据中心建设速度。 11 月 5 日星期四，英伟达股价下跌 9.2%，创下至少一年来的最大单日跌幅。但芯片股第二天开始回升，截至 11 月 6 日周五收盘，Nvidia 股价上涨 2.8%，至 186.64 美元。

然后一切都崩溃了。 11 月 8 日星期日，黄仁勋向 Nvidia 员工发送了一份全公司范围的备忘录，其中他为婚外情道歉。该备忘录发布之际，英伟达董事会开始对黄仁勋涉嫌不当行为以及公司机密或国家安全是否受到损害展开独立调查。黄表示将全力配合调查。到 11 月 9 日星期一开盘时，随着投资者对备忘录做出反应，Nvidia 股价已暴跌 7%，交易量飙升至三个月平均水平以上。在短暂反弹后，随着黄仁勋和黄爱丽关系的更多细节浮出水面，该股第二天继续震荡。截至 11 月 10 日周二收盘时，Nvidia 股价已跌至 168.89 美元，比 2025 年最后一天的收盘价低了近 10%。

随着投资者为英伟达定于下周二（11 月 17 日）召开的第三季度财报电话会议做准备，该股在 11 月 11 日星期三小幅反弹。然而，到了周三晚间，随着媒体报道称英伟达董事会正在考虑罢免黄仁勋，以及其他报道详细介绍了第二起涉嫌婚外情的消息，这一次是黄仁勋与一名英伟达员工之间的恋情，股价再次暴跌。

11 月 12 日星期四早上，英伟达宣布黄仁勋离职，导致该公司股价开盘下跌近 14%。收盘时仅下跌 4.3%。盘中低点为每股 148.80 美元，为一年来最低价。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】Nvidia前CEO黄仁勋、临时CEO Colette Kress、董事会主席Harvey Jones：黄仁勋卸任CEO，董事会明确拒绝复职，公司致力于维持数据中心与Vera Rubin平台的增长势头
【起因与机理】受黄仁勋离职引发的公司治理危机及市场对AI泡沫的整体担忧影响
【关键数据与实测】Q3财报显示营收翻倍达1158亿美元，数据中心业务增长110%，Vera Rubin平台量产顺利。
【各方立场与态度】股价受丑闻驱动与AI板块整体回调双重挤压，目前市值波动正考验其作为AI经济基石的稳定性。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Former CEO Jensen Huang, Interim CEO Colette Kress, Chairman Harvey Jones: Jensen Huang resignation, refusal to reinstate, and focus on sustaining data center growth
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Corporate governance crisis coupled with broader market skepticism regarding AI bubble valuation
[Key Metrics] Q3 financials showing $115.8B revenue and strong Vera Rubin platform ramp-up.
[Key Position & Outlook] Market volatility testing Nvidia's stability as the backbone of the AI economy amidst valuation corrections.

title: What’s With All These Outages?
title_en: What’s With All These Outages?
author: Brian Barrett, Leah Feiger, and Sophie Kleeman
article_content:
Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, United, the NSA, and Apple all went down within one week. Officials say none of the outages were cyberattacks, but the internet isn’t buying it. This week on Uncanny Valley, WIRED senior business editor Sophie Kleeman joins Brian Barrett and Leah Feiger to discuss what actually went wrong and why people jumped straight to blaming hackers and AI. Plus, Anthropic’s historic IPO at a reported $1.5 trillion, Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned, and the administration’s new rule to stop Chinese companies from renting AI chips just before Trump meets Xi.

Articles mentioned in this episode:

You can follow Brian Barrett on Bluesky at @brbarrett, Sophie Kleeman on X/Twitter at @sophiekleeman, and Leah Feiger on Bluesky at @leahfeiger. Write to us at [email protected].

You can always listen to this week's podcast through the audio player on this page, but if you want to subscribe for free to get every episode, here's how:

If you're on an iPhone or iPad, open the app called Podcasts, or just tap this link. You can also download an app like Overcast or Pocket Casts and search for “uncanny valley.” We’re on Spotify too.

Note: This is an automated transcript, which may contain errors.

Brian Barrett: Hey, this is Brian. If you've been listening for a while and you haven't rated or reviewed the podcast yet, this is your sign. Give us a rating, tell us what you think. Five stars is nice, but we'll take the feedback too. It really helps more people find the show. OK, onto the show. So hey everybody, I want to say first of all, we've got a very special guest today in the studio with Leah. It's Sophie Kleeman.

Leah Feiger: Woo-hoo. Sophie's here.

Sophie Kleeman: I'm here.

Brian Barrett: Sophie is our senior editor on the business desk and we're so glad to have her. And I've heard that she is going to do a lot of yelling and pointing and just anger I think is her vibe, is what I've been told, coming in.

Sophie Kleeman: Yes. Let's get started.

Brian Barrett: Welcome to WIRED's Uncanny Valley. I'm Brian Barrett, executive editor.

Leah Feiger: I'm Leah Feiger, director of politics and science.

Sophie Kleeman: And I am Sophie Kleeman, senior business editor.

Brian Barrett: This week we're discussing why everything seems to be breaking down all the time. First, it was Microsoft, then the FAA and air traffic control. Then Chase Bank, United Airlines, the NSA, Apple, the tech outages have been piling up and raising questions around what caused them, and why they're happening all at the same time seemingly. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says that we are not under attack. He's right, but the internet is not convinced. We'll get into what actually went wrong, and why a lot of people's first instinct is to blame hackers and AI in some combination.

Sophie Kleeman: And I am one of those people, so can't wait to get into that. We will also take a look at Anthropic officially going public this week. It will be one of the biggest IPOs ever, but the timing is a little bit complicated. So we will talk about who's about to get very, very rich and whether the recent midterm results could impact the company's grand ambitions.

Brian Barrett: And in other AI news, we're going to have a quick NVIDIA update as the company just released the first earnings report without Jensen Huang at the helm and had their first all hands led by interim CEO Colette Kress.

Leah Feiger: We're also going to be checking in on President Donald Trump's visit to Asia, specifically China, which comes just days after his administration has moved to close a loophole that lets Chinese companies access AI chips. We're going to talk about what the NVIDIA scandal has had to do with all of this and the fight inside the administration over how to handle everything.

Brian Barrett: All right look, if you picked up your phone at any point in last week to look at the news, if you went to wired.com at any point last week or anywhere on social media, you were hit with news that something somewhere had an outage.

Leah Feiger: Brian, everything is broken.

Brian Barrett: Everything's broken.

Leah Feiger: Every single thing is broken.

Brian Barrett: Everything's broken and breaking, increasingly fixed. I want to walk through this really quickly. I know people are tired of it, the so many things. We're going to list off some of the biggest ones, OK? Last Thursday, Microsoft had an outage in Outlook and Teams that was about 24 hours, which is incredibly long for those services to be out when the whole world basically depends on them to communicate. The next day, Friday, the FAA had a ground stop for the entire country, only the second time that has happened since 9/11, and it was the longest one since then. It was for more than four hours. Then on Monday, everyone said that their banks no longer worked. It turns out to be JP Morgan Chase specifically had a problem, but because banks are all counterparties to each other, every bank had an issue. If one bank had an issue, that same day, United delayed more than a hundred flights for a separate issue. Then on Tuesday, the NSA's classified internal network went down and just for good measure, an internal update also knocked out iCloud and Apple Pay for not quite as long, not quite as dramatically, but throw it on the pile. Now I want to be clear, every single one of these companies and agencies and organizations has said the incidents were not cyberattacks. It was not some combination of a ruthless AI agent and Iranian hackers. There's no evidence that any of these clustered tech failures were even related aside from the bank thing, which is self-contained in the banking industry, but that hasn't stopped people from being suspicious, trying to find a through line, and I think getting on their conspiracy horses. And Sophie, you've been riding one at the front of the battle.

Sophie Kleeman: Yes, I sure have.

Brian Barrett: Yeah. How are you taking all of this in so I can debunk it?

Sophie Kleeman: OK. So I would like to say first off that I do think this has sort of trickled down into people who don't follow this super closely.

Leah Feiger: I mean, it had to. This was your emails, this was your banking, these were your flights.

Sophie Kleeman: Right. Everyone's talking about this.

Leah Feiger: This is it.

Sophie Kleeman: To give you two very, very, very distinct examples, yesterday my fantasy football group chat blew up because someone was like, "Hey guys who follow this, and who are paying attention, are we under attack?" And Brian, you'll be proud of me. I actually said you should read wired.com for the answer to that.

Brian Barrett: Good job, Sophie.

Leah Feiger: She did not say, "Yes, go to the bunkers." Which I know is what you wanted to say.

Sophie Kleeman: It is what I wanted to say.

Leah Feiger: Look, I will say though, I get that inclination. These are so many public services that everyone has really just taken for granted, not only to work, but to help us function in our day-to-day lives. I talked to friends who were like, "Oh yeah, I just had a day and a half off of work basically, and then could not pay my rent." It was everything.

Brian Barrett: And there are people who are doing doomsday prepping at Costco now. I've had multiple group chats where people, even when I've told them, "Hey, it's actually fine," they are still prepping their bunkers. I think it's instructive. I have covered outages for a long time at WIRED because I think they're fascinating because they affect so many people, and they have such mundane causes usually. So I want to talk through a couple of things and what happened. Just for any listeners who are still worried about it, they all have very distinct things. The Microsoft Outlook issue was actually ... I love this one. It was a fix that was deployed in July. They basically made an update in July, propagated it out, but was not triggered until last week. Something else happened.

Sophie Kleeman: Do we know what that something else is? I'm just asking questions.

Brian Barrett: Iranian hackers. No, they've done a shorter postmortem. They're going to do a longer postmortem. The gist of it was they pushed this thing out and then it propagated out through the whole network and then they had another update. They stepped on the landmine and everything went boom, and it took a while to correct. For the FAA, when air traffic control went down, and Aarian Marshall, who covers transportation mobility for us here at WIRED, was very early to say this doesn't seem like hackers. There was a lot of suspicion there because the FAA just the day before had rolled out an AI system to help with air traffic control. The difference is that system's more about data, and about where planes are going and what they're doing. The system that was affected, the problem on Friday, was that people couldn't talk to each other. It was a comms issue. And that tied back to old, old, old fiber equipment that a company called L3Harris maintains. They were trying to push an update on Friday afternoon, which you never do. That's the crazy part to me is that they were trying to push—

Leah Feiger: It's the perfect time.

Sophie Kleeman: Yeah.

Brian Barrett: Push an update to production on a Friday, a couple weeks before Thanksgiving? Crazy stuff.

Leah Feiger: And then I mean the rest was all the same too, right Brian? Chase blamed a software bug in their own hardware. United said it was a technology related issue. NSA blamed routine maintenance. Apple blamed an internal update. All of this was kind of the same. It was just all happening at the same time.

Sophie Kleeman: At the same time.

Leah Feiger: But I think I get it. I get the fears here. I also understand the timing in some ways. We're nearing the end of the year. People need to push all of these updates before holiday travel season or just holiday banking season, I guess, email season.

Sophie Kleeman: Email season.

Leah Feiger: But it is understandable that everyone went straight to the hackers, straight to AI overlords because we've actually been having a not small amount of those examples. If you had told me that this was another Hugging Face incident, I would've been like, yep. Alright. Sounds good.

Sophie Kleeman: You're like, yeah, that sounds right.

Brian Barrett: Well, and Leah too, I think what doesn't help, there's the political dimension here too, because Markwayne Mullin can tell me everything's fine, all he wants. I don't necessarily buy anything from him.

Sophie Kleeman: I don't believe him.

Brian Barrett: Right. I inherently, this administration has no credibility. So in these moments, what do we do?

Leah Feiger: I have to shout out our podcast producer right now. Obviously we are sitting here with a list of notes about all of this and I just quickly looked at it and one tab line was, also people don't trust the government.

Sophie Kleeman: Incredible.

Leah Feiger: Which is, yeah, that is the situation right now. That is perhaps the most succinct, accurate way to push this, which is there was just a massive referendum a few weeks ago. Dems are coming in, guns blazing, and everything is breaking right before that happens. I get it.

Sophie Kleeman: I'm the devil's advocate here, right? I was the person last week where I was like, we're all going to die. We're under attack. This is crazy. This is all happening at the same time. Obviously I don't think that that's really the case, but I will say that I do think two things. I think people are quick to blame AI for things because they don't like it, they don't understand it, they are scared of it, and the companies who are selling it are not doing a great job of selling their product in ways that make people want to sort of feel good about themselves. But the second point is that it was AI, right? It was just the flip side of it. It was like, these companies are deploying these incredibly advanced systems to find vulnerabilities, to find issues within their very complex and in some cases old systems and they're finding it and then they're patching it all at the same time. And that's what I think that reporting has suggested that's what we're seeing.

Brian Barrett: This goes back to Anthropic's Mythos model, which is very good at cybersecurity. You might remember it from such news headlines as Anthropic gets banned from the Pentagon and other stupid moments in AI history. Mythos is very, very good at cybersecurity. Anthropic gave access to a limited number, actually a decent number of people who control sensitive information, governments, organizations, companies, and those companies have since been using it to identify bugs that they couldn't find otherwise. Sending patches at a huge rate, and the more complicated the bug, the more patches trying to push out at the same time, the more likely something is going to break. And I think that's what we're seeing here. So yeah, AI plays a role, but in some ways you can think of this as companies trying to get ahead of the hacking version of this. They're doing this because otherwise, in a few months, someone's going to actually say, oh, we can break into the air traffic control system, shut it down ourselves.

Sophie Kleeman: Am I the only one who would love to see that? What if we just went offline forever? What if it all shut down? That would be great. We could all touch grass.

Brian Barrett: I think that'd be great.

Sophie Kleeman: Finally.

Leah Feiger: All right.

Brian Barrett: I think it'd be great.

Sophie Kleeman: Thank you Brian.

Brian Barrett: It would affect the podcast, but that's OK. We can mail each other letters.

Leah Feiger: I've been tickled though by all of these comments from our government officials. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has tried really hard to kind of deescalate this as well, claiming there's no foul play. He's traveling with Trump in Asia this week and he said in a press conference multiple times, "We are not under systemic attack."

Marco Rubio, archival audio: The first thing I want to make very clear is that we have zero evidence whatsoever. We have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other.

Leah Feiger: And Trump had a different take. I was slightly less reassured.

Archival audio: Are you concerned about all these outages? Microsoft, the FAA, United, Chase Bank?

Donald Trump, archival audio: No. It's life. When you're big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It's fine.

Leah Feiger: OK. The reason I had to pivot to that is that's perhaps like the Sophie model here. You're like, "Yeah, shut it down. This is it. This is what we've signed up for."

Sophie Kleeman: You know what? We're just going to roll with it.

Leah Feiger: Sophie and Trump, two peas in a pod.

Sophie Kleeman: We are such similar people in so many ways. In other news, it's been a crazy week, hasn't it? So Anthropic finally arrived on the stock market. The company's long-awaited IPO debut started trading under the ticker ANT, which I would just like to say is actually very cute. And it's valued at a reported one and a half trillion dollars, which is just a staggering, staggering number. It is among the biggest IPOs ever, but it is actually below the $2 trillion figure that was floating around several months ago. And since then, things have shifted even more. NVIDIA lost its CEO and about $2 trillion in market value. And in the midterms, voters overwhelmingly rejected provisions that supported data centers that AI companies need. So given this interesting, interesting timing, what are we looking for?

Brian Barrett: I am looking for a lot of people to become insanely wealthy, even if it's slightly less insanely wealthy than it would've been a couple of months ago.

Sophie Kleeman: Just slightly less.

Brian Barrett: Just slightly, just like a little tiny bit.

Sophie Kleeman: To be clear, $1.5 trillion is still ...

Brian Barrett: It's still generational wealth, but how many generations are we talking about? Trick question. Anthropic doesn't care because they all think we're going to die in the next 10 years or so because of AI. Sophie, I'm curious what you think, because when I think of the Anthropic IPO, which I do every day, every day I'm thinking Anthropic IPO.

Sophie Kleeman: You wake up in the morning and you think Anthropic IPO.

Brian Barrett: I think ANT, ANT, ANT. But it's the first, not the first, it's the biggest pure play AI IPO that we've had and maybe that we're going to have depending on what happens with OpenAI. SpaceX had an IPO recently, but that is a rocket company with an AI company stapled to it. So what do you look for when this company goes public and people can trade on it? How much do we look at it as a bellwether for the industry in general? Not on the first day of trading even, but just in general, how much can we look and say, oh, that's how the AI industry is going?

Sophie Kleeman: I mean, I think it is the bellwether, right? It is the first, it is enormous. It's such a leader in the space. And I think that the interesting thing to me is how much it is connected to the other sort of giants in the space, which is to say Amazon and Google, and a few other companies. I mean, those two firms are themselves going to make a shit ton of money from this IPO. They have, what is it? 15 percent. Amazon will own 15 percent. Google will own nearly 14 percent. Those are huge numbers. So I think just this idea that all the financing is tied together and all of these people are riding on the same rocket ship that may or may not crash onto the surface of the earth.

Brian Barrett: And not just that, but Anthropic, they're like a rent not own approach to data centers. So they've got nearly a trillion dollars of data center commitments that is all going to other companies. It is sort of fueling, whether that's SpaceX or Google. So they are such a symbol of the interdependency of this industry. And again, can't stress this enough, they are pretty sure that AI will destroy everything, and think that their best chance to make a trillion dollars is to build the kind of AI that will destroy everything as fast as they can. It's in their prospectus.

Sophie Kleeman: Only they can prevent mass AI destruction. The other thing I would like to sort of cite here, I feel like with these IPO stories, obviously everyone's sort of focused on the money, and the what does it mean and blah, blah, blah. But one kind of very weird fun fact that I would like to just highlight here is that Sam Bankman-Fried of all of this. He was supposed to make money on this because he was invested in Anthropic, but when he went through his bankruptcy, and all of his legal problems, the government clawed back that investment.

Leah Feiger: Wait, so where are his shares now? Love that.

Sophie Kleeman: They got sold to some people for a very little amount of money and now those people are going to be rich.

Leah Feiger: Oh, that's fun. That's a fun thing to follow.

Sophie Kleeman: Highly recommend checking that out.

Leah Feiger: Yeah. Look, you guys know me. I'm interested in this from a political standpoint. Voters voted against data centers. Politicians won their campaigns by promising that data centers were out across the board. This was bipartisan, this was Republican, this was Democrat. So as Anthropic is entering this space, as other companies, OpenAI, etc., are kind of watching how this goes for them, I'm really curious in the coming months what these investments in data centers is going to mean for them. I wonder if it's going to mean slowdowns. I wonder if any of these newly electeds will actually be able to hold these folks accountable. We're going to see, but there is very much a question mark for me there about what comes next.

Sophie Kleeman: I mean, I think one of the great things for us as journalists too about this IPO is Anthropic will now be a public company. So they are much more accountable and accountable in ways that we can actually dig into and go through their 10Ks and go through their 10Qs and all the rest of it. They're going to have to do earnings calls and all the rest of it, which is great for us because we will have such a better window into how they're actually doing.

Leah Feiger: Oh, it's amazing.

Sophie Kleeman: Such a better window into how they're actually doing.

Leah Feiger: Also, just because they're so tied up, sourcing inside Anthropic is hard. This is a company that is very much kept to themselves, which is why any kernel of information ... When Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic doomer who bounced out and said, "This really is going to all end the world," and he was on, I don't know, every single talk show or podcast available. One, because of what he was saying, but two, because getting information from inside of Anthropic is difficult. So to your point, a hundred percent. The fact that we're going to have more information there is a game change.

Brian Barrett: The one thing I would add, yes, it's great for us as journalists. We're going to get to see and know so much more information. I'm not as excited about Anthropic now being on this quarterly cycle of needing to demonstrate constant growth and earnings, which is a private company you're shielded from a little bit because the incentives that will make AI profitable are not necessarily the incentives that will make humanity more sustainable, but that's fine.

Sophie Kleeman: Who cares about sustainability? Yep.

Brian Barrett: Who cares? We're all going to be podcasting in caves. Speaking of giant AI companies that are having big moments, good or bad, we've got to talk a little bit about Nvidia. If you're sick of it, totally understand. It's been everywhere, but there are some important updates. Some things have happened just in the last day or two that we should touch on at least quickly. On Tuesday, the company reported its most recent earnings, not surprising that they had another big, big quarter, $115.8 billion in revenue. It's more than six billion ahead of expectations. It was Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned last week after it became public that he had had affairs with a woman suspected of being an asset of Chinese intelligence, and also with at least one of his own direct reports within Nvidia. Over the last few days, we've had a number of Silicon Valley leaders, including, surprise, Elon Musk, campaigning to bring him back. Some have floated the theory that he was set up. Huang himself said in a statement, first statement that he released since this all happened, that he would be honored to return to Nvidia if the board would have him back. Sounds like the board is saying absolutely not. They said that in very clear terms during the earnings call. What do we make of Nvidia in this moment? I should say, too, that we are recording this just after Nvidia's first all hands after Jensen Huang left was led by interim CEO, former CFO, Colette Kress. It's a lot of information. She didn't say much other than, "Hey employees, we're going to give you a lot more money and a lot more stock equity to make you happier so that you don't leave."

Sophie Kleeman: And she kept saying, "We got this," right?

Brian Barrett: She kept saying, “We got this.”

Sophie Kleeman: That was her direct quote, that was her top line, "We're going to be fine. We got this. Do not worry."

Leah Feiger: But so many people just don't think that. I can't stop thinking about what Zoë told us last week, Brian, and the week before. She's been saying this for a while now, just about how Jensen was in such a particular place compared to all of his co-CEOs around Silicon Valley and that he was just not insulated. He was not insulated within his company. He's not the Mark Zuckerberg model at Meta where that guy's not going anywhere. There is just no world where he's getting stripped from his title or responsibilities, which then makes this entire Bring Back Jensen campaign all the more interesting to me, to see Elon Musk and all of these variety of CEOs, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, all of these different people who not even are just kind of quietly commenting on the sidelines, but signing literal petitions saying this. There's an interesting look, at least for me, of the accountability of it all, of is this possible? I guess this is possible. This shouldn't be possible.

Sophie Kleeman: I'm fascinated by this. And Brian, I would love to know what you think is going on here because I sort of though the sharks would be circling in a way, or I thought that they would not want to touch this with a 10-foot pole kind of thing. I mean, I understand that Jensen is just such a sort of crucial part of this ecosystem and Nvidia is such a crucial part of this ecosystem. They've sort of engineered it that way, but I'm curious what you think, what's the vib...

title: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
title_en: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
author: Jordan Novet
article_content:
Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement.

The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.

The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The company bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.

The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing.

Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.

While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.

Management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.

The company said Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo, which went public in 2023.

Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million.

title_zh: Intuit以36.8亿美元剥离Mailchimp业务
summary_zh: Intuit宣布以36.8亿美元现金与股票将Mailchimp出售给Bending Spoons，较2021年收购价缩水逾七成
article_content_zh:
税务软件制造商 Intuit 周四表示，已同意以 36.8 亿美元的现金和股票将营销子公司 Mailchimp 出售给意大利技术整合商 Bending Spoons。一份声明称，该交易将于 2027 年初完成。

此次出售对 Intuit 来说是一次代价高昂的撤退，该公司在 2021 年斥资 120 亿美元收购了 Mailchimp，以拓展其核心税务和会计业务。五年后，在 Mailchimp 拖累其整体收入增长后，这家软件制造商以不到三分之一的价格出售了这家电子邮件营销公司。

这笔交易是 Bending Spoons 收购曾经前景光明的技术资产的最新实例。该公司于 9 月份以原价 10% 的价格收购了生产力软件初创公司 Airtable。

Bending Spoons 产品组合还包括 AOL、Brightcove、Eventbrite、Evernote、Meetup、Vimeo 和 WeTransfer。

8 月，Intuit 开始将 Mailchimp 作为一个独特的运营部门运营。 Intuit 财务主管桑迪普·奥吉拉 (Sandeep Aujla) 在 9 月份的公司简报会上表示，此举旨在为投资者提供更大的透明度，因为该公司试图管理该部门以实现盈利。

同样在周四，Intuit 宣布截至 10 月 31 日的第一财季盈利和收入强于预期。该公司公布调整后每股收益 2.91 美元，收入 43.5 亿美元。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计每股收益为 2.70 美元，收入为 43.1 亿美元。

虽然 Intuit 的收入同比增长 12%，但 Mailchimp 的收入却下降了 1%，至 3.13 亿美元。 StreetAccount 调查的分析师此前预期为 3.144 亿美元。

管理层预计2027财年调整后每股收益为22.88美元至23.12美元，营收为230.81亿美元至233.65亿美元。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计，调整后每股收益为 23.62 美元，营收为 234.3 亿美元。 Intuit 股价在盘后交易中下跌 15%。

该公司表示，Mailchimp 2027 财年收入应为 12.56 亿美元至 12.66 亿美元，同比下降 1% 至持平。 Aujla 8 月份表示，Intuit 预计 Mailchimp 更高的有效价格将抵消客户流失的增加。 Mailchimp 成立于 2001 年。竞争对手包括 2023 年上市的 Klaviyo。

当 Bending Spoons 7 月上市时，伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司向 Bending Spoons 投资了 6 亿美元，10 月 Bending Spoons 表示伯克希尔又投资了 3.3 亿美元。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此交易标志着Intuit从“跨领域扩张”重回“核心财务软件”的战略收缩，暴露了SaaS领域盲目并购在跨生态整合时的价值损耗。Bending Spoons采取的“低价吸纳存量资产”模式虽能维持财报短期账面增长，但其能否在存量市场中通过精细化运营遏制产品生命周期衰减仍存在巨大的财务风险。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This transaction signals Intuit's strategic retrenchment back to its core tax software business, exposing the value destruction inherent in cross-domain M&A within the SaaS sector. Bending Spoons' strategy of acquiring distressed legacy assets at a deep discount offers a short-term boost to scale, but the firm faces significant execution risk in reversing the lifecycle decay of these stagnant products.

title: At a Senate hearing, Trump's CISA director nominee Michael LoSapio dodged questions about the agency's priorities, denied January 6 was an attack, and more (Eric Geller/Cybersecurity Dive)
title_en: At a Senate hearing, Trump's CISA director nominee Michael LoSapio dodged questions about the agency's priorities, denied January 6 was an attack, and more (Eric Geller/Cybersecurity Dive)

article_content:
Michael LoSapio, a Palantir executive, also denied that the U.S. Capitol was attacked on Jan. 6, 2021.

President Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency offered little information about how he would steer the beleaguered agency during his confirmation hearing on Thursday.

Michael LoSapio, the chief information security officer at the data analytics firm Palantir, provided only high-level answers to members of the Senate Homeland Security Committee who asked him how he would restore CISA’s ability to combat cyber threats after two years of Trump administration cuts.

“I believe CISA is one of the only agencies in the government that plays a defensive cyber role in our nation,” LoSapio told Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., who will chair the homeland-security panel in the next session of Congress.

CISA’s “sole purpose is to provide resources [and] information to the defenders of state, local, and private entities for the purpose of cyber defense,” LoSapio continued. “If confirmed, I intend to bring together the community and the national labs to help collaborate and coordinate and to give defenders the tools they need to defend their networks.”

LoSapio also described CISA as “the cybersecurity version of the 911 system” because of its role in responding to significant cyber incidents.

But LoSapio, whose firm has extensive and controversial connections to the Trump administration, refused to weigh in on the administration’s downsizing of CISA, which has included mass layoffs and significant changes to the agency’s programs and services.

“I can’t comment on the current state of CISA, because I’m not inside today,” he told Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich.

When Slotkin pressed LoSapio on whether he would support the Trump administration’s proposed $385 million cut to CISA’s budget, LoSapio again dodged the question.

“I'm going to get involved and understand where the gaps are,” he said, “and I will come back to this committee with a gap analysis.”

Slotkin said LoSapio was too afraid of angering Trump to be an effective CISA director.

“You should be able to say clearly, there’s increasing threat, therefore we need increasing resources to deal with it,” she said, “and the fact that you can’t say that means that you’re more worried about the political ramifications than you are about the national security of the country.”

“I don’t necessarily believe more money means more security,” LoSapio responded. “I believe spending money on the right solutions in the right ways actually decreases risk.”

At other times, LoSapio appeared unprepared to discuss the details of CISA’s work. When Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., asked him what his top priorities would be as CISA’s director, he gave a vague answer that did not mention any of CISA’s specific responsibilities.

“It’s really important to understand the landscape of the systems that you have out in the wild,” LoSapio said, “the things that you operate day to day, the systems that you rely on, the systems that are ancillary to the work you do, and do an extensive evaluation on their vulnerabilities, whether or not they’ve been patched or not, and how they have been architected and their defensive capabilities — both things we need to add and the things that exist today, as to how that maps to the the threats we’re facing.”

LoSapio’s nomination has generated skepticism within the cybersecurity community because of his low profile and limited cybersecurity leadership background. His comments at his confirmation hearing could raise new doubts about whether he is the right person to lead CISA, which has been without a Senate-confirmed director since the beginning of the Trump administration.

His answers to several questions from Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., highlighted LoSapio’s loyalty to Trump.

First, he refused to acknowledge that President Joe Biden won the 2020 election, prompting incredulity from Blumenthal, who pointed out that LoSapio was nominated to lead the agency overseeing U.S. election security. Next, LoSapio denied that the Jan. 6, 2021, insurrection at the U.S. Capitol constituted an attack.

“I don’t believe it was an attack,” he said. “I wasn’t involved in politics. ... I know what I saw on the news.”

Hours later, that comment prompted several senators to say they would block LoSapio’s confirmation, potentially dooming his prospects in the final weeks before Democrats take control of Congress.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., who is retiring, and Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., both plan to place holds on LoSapio’s nomination, their spokespeople told Cybersecurity Dive.

“You can’t have an insurrectionist Palantir executive in charge of our nation’s cybersecurity and election security,” Wyden said in a statement.

Editor’s note: This story has been updated to reflect a second senator placing a hold on LoSapio’s nomination.

article_content_zh:
Palantir 高管 Michael LoSapio 也否认美国国会大厦在 2021 年 1 月 6 日遭到袭击。

唐纳德·特朗普总统的网络安全和基础设施安全局局长提名人在周四的确认听证会上几乎没有透露他将如何领导这个陷入困境的机构。

数据分析公司 Palantir 的首席信息安全官迈克尔·洛萨皮奥 (Michael LoSapio) 仅向参议院国土安全委员会成员提供了高层答案，后者询问他在特朗普政府削减两年后将如何恢复 CISA 应对网络威胁的能力。

“我相信 CISA 是政府中唯一在我们国家发挥防御性网络作用的机构之一，”洛萨皮奥告诉新罕布什尔州民主党参议员玛吉·哈桑（Maggie Hassan），后者将在国会下届会议上担任国土安全小组主席。

LoSapio 继续说道，CISA 的“唯一目的是为国家、地方和私人实体的捍卫者提供资源[和]信息，以实现网络防御目的。” “如果得到确认，我打算将社区和国家实验室聚集在一起，帮助协作和协调，并为防御者提供防御网络所需的工具。”

LoSapio 还将 CISA 描述为“911 系统的网络安全版本”，因为它在应对重大网络事件方面发挥着重要作用。

但 LoSapio 的公司与特朗普政府有着广泛而有争议的联系，他拒绝参与政府对 CISA 的裁员，其中包括大规模裁员以及对该机构的项目和服务进行重大调整。

“我无法对 CISA 的现状发表评论，因为我今天不在里面，”他告诉密歇根州民主党参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金 (Elissa Slotkin)。

当斯洛特金向 LoSapio 询问他是否会支持特朗普政府提议的 CISA 预算削减 3.85 亿美元时，LoSapio 再次回避了这个问题。

“我将参与其中并了解差距在哪里，”他说，“我将带着差距分析回到这个委员会。”

斯洛特金表示，LoSapio 太害怕激怒特朗普，无法成为有效的 CISA 主任。

“你应该能够清楚地说，威胁越来越大，因此我们需要增加资源来应对，”她说，“事实上你不能这么说，这意味着你更担心政治后果，而不是国家安全。”

“我不一定相信更多的钱意味着更多的安全，”洛萨皮奥回答道。 “我相信以正确的方式花钱购买正确的解决方案实际上可以降低风险。”

其他时候，LoSapio 似乎没有准备好讨论 CISA 工作的细节。当俄克拉荷马州共和党参议员詹姆斯·兰克福德 (James Lankford) 问他作为 CISA 主任的首要任务是什么时，他给出了一个含糊的回答，没有提及 CISA 的任何具体职责。

title: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
title_en: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants

author: Amy Chang Chien
article_content:
Few things could generate more buzz for a small restaurant than a visit from Jensen Huang. In recent years, the former Nvidia CEO became known for dining out at street markets and hole-in-the-wall noodle joints across Asia, drawing huge crowds of fans and photographers wherever he went.

But after Huang resigned last week amid revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, some of the food vendors he helped put on the map are wondering whether their most famous customer is still good for business. In Taiwan, where Huang was born and his dining habits have long been a spectator sport, many say they aren't ready to turn against their hometown hero.

Tu Chang-chun, the owner of Ice World, a shaved-ice shop in Taipei, describes Huang as friendly, the kind of person who puts others around him at ease. His impression of the billionaire hasn’t changed since he learned of his affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman accused of spying for China.

“It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire. Why blow it all out of proportion?” Tu said on Monday evening, standing beneath the yellow lights of his stall at Linjiang Street Night Market. “Now, a lot of foreigners walk past, see my sign, and laugh. People just love kicking someone when they’re down.”

At the entrance of his shop, Tu continues to proudly display a photo of Huang posing with him and his wife. “I think he’s such a warm and approachable person,” Tu added. “Why are people treating him this way?”

Jensen Huang has visited this shaved ice stall at Taipei’s Linjiang Street Night Market three times since 2023.

Tu says that Huang has visited his shop three times since 2023, and he always orders the same thing: mango shaved ice with tangyuan (sticky rice balls). The dessert, a blend of tropical fruit and condensed milk, is popular in Taipei’s bustling night markets, especially among first-time visitors to the island.

“When he came in for shaved ice, he would spend half an hour eating a single bowl,” recalled Tu. “Whenever someone came up to take a photo with him, he got right up. He’s not pretentious.”

At a tofu pudding shop near Ningxia Night Market in western Taipei, photos of Huang remain on display alongside those of other prominent technology figures who have visited, including Morris Chang, the founder of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). The store manager, Hsieh, defended the shop’s decision to keep them up.

“I don’t think this changes the fact that he’s a very successful businessman,” Hsieh said of Huang’s affairs with Alice Huang and other women. “Having an affair is a private matter.”

Hsieh, who agreed to be identified only by his surname for privacy reasons, said that Huang had visited the shop four times over the past few years, and on each occasion he seemed friendly and down-to-earth.

Owner Tu Chang-chun said he has no plans to take down photos Jensen Huang visiting his shaved-ice shop.

In Taiwan, Huang’s culinary indulgences extended well beyond street food. He frequented some of Taipei’s most exclusive restaurants, where he hosted technology executives for what became known in the local press as “Trillion-Dollar Banquets,” a reference to the attendees’ combined net worth of more than 1 trillion New Taiwan dollars.

The dinners often drew crowds of journalists and photographers hoping to catch a glimpse of Huang and his guests. The intense media attention helps explain why so many photographs and videos of Huang with Alice Huang were captured in Taiwan. Restaurant owners, meanwhile, welcomed the publicity, often proudly displaying photographs of themselves with Huang inside their establishments.

The Taiwanese tea chain 19 Tea House launched a new drink this week, giving it a name that pokes fun at Huang’s alleged “womanizing” ways. According to the chain, the drink combines osmanthus-infused honey with fresh lemon, offering a blend of fragrant floral notes and sweet-and-tangy citrus flavors.

Support for Huang in Taiwan has also extended far beyond the restaurants he frequented. On Monday evening, Taipei 101, the island’s iconic skyscraper just blocks from one of Huang’s favorite night markets, lit up with messages of support for the former Nvidia CEO, including “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” “Thrive Together,” and “Taiwan AI Build Future Together.”

Tech industry figures who supported the initiative told Taiwan’s state-run Central News Agency that the illumination campaign was intended to “help restore Jensen Huang’s reputation,” urging the public not to “kick him when he's down, but instead offer warmth and support during the autumn and winter.”

article_content_zh:
对于一家小餐馆来说，没有什么比黄仁勋的来访更能引起轰动了。近年来，这位前英伟达首席执行官因在亚洲各地的街头市场和简陋面馆就餐而闻名，所到之处都吸引了大量粉丝和摄影师。

但黄上周因多起婚外情被曝光而辞职后，他帮助名声大噪的一些食品摊贩开始怀疑他们最著名的客户是否仍然有利于生意。在黄的出生地台湾，他的饮食习惯长期以来一直是一项观赏性运动，许多人表示，他们还没有准备好对抗家乡的英雄。

台北刨冰店冰世界的老板涂长春形容黄很友善，是那种让周围的人感到轻松的人。自从得知他与被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女商人黄爱丽（Alice Huang）有染后，他对这位亿万富翁的印象就没有改变。

“这不像是他杀了人或者放火烧了什么东西。为什么要把这一切都夸大呢？”周一晚上，屠站在临江街夜市摊位的黄灯下说道。 “现在，很多外国人走过，看到我的牌子，就笑了。人们就是喜欢在别人情绪低落的时候踢他们。”

在他的店门口，屠继续自豪地展示着黄与他和他的妻子合影的照片。 “我认为他是一个非常热情、平易近人的人，”涂补充道。 “为什么人们要这样对待他？”

自2023年以来，黄仁勋已三度光顾台北临江街夜市的这家刨冰摊。

涂先生说，自2023年以来，黄先生已经来过他的店3次了，他总是点同样的东西：芒果刨冰和汤圆。这种由热带水果和炼乳混合而成的甜点在台北熙熙攘攘的夜市中很受欢迎，尤其是在第一次来岛上的游客中。

“当他进来吃刨冰时，他会花半个小时吃一碗。”屠回忆道。 “每当有人上来和他合影时，他都会站起来。他并不自命不凡。”

在台北西部宁夏夜市附近的一家豆腐花店里，黄的照片与其他到访过的著名科技人物的照片一起陈列着，其中包括台积电创始人张忠谋。商店经理谢家华 (Hsieh) 为商店保留这些产品的决定进行了辩护。

“我不认为这会改变他是一位非常成功的商人的事实，”谢家华在谈到黄与爱丽丝黄和其他女性的风流韵事时说道。 “有外遇是私事。”

出于隐私原因，谢长廷同意只透露自己的姓氏。他表示，黄先生在过去几年里曾四次光顾这家店，每次都显得友好而务实。

店主涂长春表示，他不打算拍下黄仁勋参观他刨冰店的照片。

在台湾，黄的烹饪爱好远远超出了街头小吃。他经常光顾台北一些最高档的餐厅，在那里招待技术高管，当地媒体将其称为“万亿美元宴会”，指的是与会者的总净资产超过 1 万亿新台币。

这些晚宴经常吸引大批记者和摄影师，希望一睹黄和他的客人的风采。媒体的强烈关注有助于解释为什么这么多黄与爱丽丝黄的照片和视频在台湾被拍摄。与此同时，餐馆老板们对这种宣传表示欢迎，经常自豪地展示自己与黄在餐馆内的照片。
