title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
title_en: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
author: Dan Goodin
article_content:
A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its western neighbor.

Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”

### Evasive and irregular turns

“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”

When police later questioned D’iu about the incident, the defendant allegedly said he saw a woman get into a car and thought she was “beautiful.” He then told the investigators that he followed her because he “wanted to ask her out on a date.”

Prosecutors didn’t name the company, but both Reuters and Bloomberg, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the case, identified it as Palantir. Ars is unable to confirm that reporting. Palantir representatives didn’t respond to an email seeking confirmation.

D’iu allegedly entered the US unlawfully in the summer of 2026 after being recruited by someone over Telegram. Prosecutors said the party gave D’iu a clandestine assignment to target employees of a large technology and defense company. D’iu received instructions, equipment, and financial support along with information that his work was on behalf of “the motherland.” His instructions were to collect information about the company because it was supplying weapons for use against Russian forces in Ukraine.

Prosecutors said D’iu traveled from Istanbul, Turkey, to Mexico City in June. He then crossed the border into the US and was instructed to buy laptops, cell phones, wireless networking equipment, and remote access software. Besides instructions to monitor company employees at the coffee shop, D’iu’s orders also included positioning his laptop at certain locations near the company so it could be remotely accessed in an attempt to collect information from company employees nearby.

D’iu allegedly obtained fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity as he conducted his activities. The documents included a falsified California ID card, an altered US passport, and a Social Security card bearing the assumed name of “Hugo Landry Johns.” The passport was allegedly an authentic US passport that originally had been issued to someone elsewhere in the country. It was modified to display D’iu’s photograph and assumed identity.

D’iu was arrested on October 30 and remains in custody. He is charged with one count of Conspiracy to Act as an Agent of a Foreign Government, one count of Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, and one count of Interstate Stalking. If convicted for Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, he faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release. He faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release for each conviction on the other two charges.

D’iu had his initial appearance in federal court on November 2. He is next scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

title_zh: 俄罗斯籍间谍被控跟踪监控硅谷国防企业
summary_zh: 25岁俄罗斯公民伊戈尔·迪尤因非法入境并长期监视Palantir等公司员工被联邦起诉
article_content_zh:
一名俄罗斯国民因涉嫌俄罗斯间谍而被起诉，他跟踪和监视一家硅谷公司的员工，该公司正在协助乌克兰与其西方邻国进行持续的战争。

联邦检察官周三表示，25 岁​​的伊戈尔·迪乌 (Igor D’iu) 据称在该公司帕洛阿尔托办事处附近的一家咖啡店工作时拍摄了这些员工及其电脑屏幕。他还保存了一份员工和一名高级管理人员的家庭住址清单。检察官称，D’iu 有一次在一名员工从帕洛阿尔托返回旧金山的家中尾随她。该案提交的一份宣誓书称该员工为“FEMP1”（女性员工的缩写），并表示该事件让她“处于情绪困扰的状态”。

### 规避和不规则转弯

一名联邦调查局特工写道：“FEMP1 进行了躲避和不规则转弯，走了小路，然后进入了一家杂货店停车场，D’IU 继续积极跟踪她的车辆。” “D’IU 跟随 FEMP1 掉头、非法左转，并闯红灯与 FEMP1 一起行驶了近三十英里。FEMP1 在开车时拨打了 911，并被指示直接开车前往旧金山警察局 (“SFPD”) 任务站。在 SFPD 任务站附近，FEMP1 标记了一辆 SFPD 巡逻车并报告了这一事件。FEMP1 与巡逻车取得联系后，D’IU 离开了。”

当警方后来就此事询问 D’iu 时，被告据称说他看到一名女子上了车，并认为她“很漂亮”。然后他告诉调查人员，他跟踪她是因为“想约她出去约会”。

检察官没有透露该公司的名称，但路透社和彭博社均援引未透露姓名的知情人士的话称该公司为 Palantir。 Ars 无法证实该报道。 Palantir 代表没有回复寻求确认的电子邮件。

据称，D’iu 被某人通过 Telegram 招募后，于 2026 年夏天非法进入美国。检察官称，该党给 D’iu 一项秘密任务，以针对一家大型技术和国防公司的员工。 D’iu 收到了指示、设备和财政支持，以及他的工作代表“祖国”的信息。他的指示是收集有关该公司的信息，因为该公司正在为乌克兰境内的俄罗斯军队提供武器。

检察官称，D’iu 于 6 月从土耳其伊斯坦布尔前往墨西哥城。然后他越过边境进入美国，并被指示购买笔记本电脑、手机、无线网络设备和远程访问软件。除了指示在咖啡店监控公司员工外，D’iu 的命令还包括将他的笔记本电脑放置在公司附近的某些位置，以便可以远程访问，以试图收集附近公司员工的信息。

据称，D’iu 在进行活动时获取了伪造的身份证明文件以隐瞒自己的身份。这些文件包括伪造的加州身份证、篡改的美国护照以及假名“雨果·兰德里·约翰斯”的社会保障卡。据称，该护照是一本正宗的美国护照，最初是发给该国其他地方的人的。它被修改为显示 D’iu 的照片和假设的身份。

D’iu 于 10 月 30 日被捕，目前仍被拘留。他被指控犯有一项串谋充当外国政府代理人罪、一项在未通知总检察长的情况下充当外国政府代理人罪以及一项州际跟踪罪。如果因在未通知总检察长的情况下充当外国政府代理人的罪名成立，他将面临最高 10 年监禁、25 万美元罚款和三年监管释放。其他两项罪名每项定罪，他将面临最高 5 年监禁、 25 万美元罚款和 3 年监管释放。

D’iu 于 11 月 2 日首次在联邦法院出庭。他下次预计于 11 月 24 日在联邦法院出庭。

title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
title_en: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
author: Jay Peters
article_content:
Meta is planning to price the Muse Charm, a little gadget with a screen that lets you chat with your Muse AI agent, at $300, according to The Information. CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed the gadget earlier this year and said the company expected to ship the Charm “in time for the holidays in December,” but he didn’t provide a price at the time.

When he announced the Muse Charm, Zuckerberg said that the company had “packed the whole Muse experience,” including real-time voice and avatar technology, into the gadget. It has a fingerprint sensor, and you can tap it to be able to talk to a Muse AI agent without unlocking a phone or opening an app. The Information reports that the Muse Charm will come with a free 12-month 5G data plan from Verizon.

Spokesperson Tyler Yee wrote to The Information that “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.” When reached for comment by The Verge, Yee provided the same statement.

The company is also working on a smartwatch, The Information says, but a launch for that has been pushed to 2027 as Meta tries to get Muse Charm out the door.

Meta also open sourced code to let users make their own Muse gadgets, which my colleague Sean Hollister used to make his own DIY Muse Charm.

Update, November 19th: Noted statement given by Meta spokesperson Tyler Yee.

title_zh: Meta拟以300美元推出Muse AI交互硬件
summary_zh: Meta计划于12月假期期间推出Muse Charm人工智能交互设备，定价300美元并附赠一年期Verizon 5G流量套餐
article_content_zh:
Meta 计划将 Muse Charm 定价为 300 美元，这是一款带有屏幕的小工具，可以让你与 Muse AI 代理聊天。首席执行官马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 在今年早些时候透露了这款设备，并表示该公司预计将“在 12 月的假期前”发货，但当时他没有提供价格。

当扎克伯格宣布 Muse Charm 时，他表示该公司已“将整个 Muse 体验融入其中”，包括实时语音和化身技术。它有一个指纹传感器，你可以点击它来与 Muse AI 代理对话，而无需解锁手机或打开应用程序。据 The Information 报道，Muse Charm 将附带 Verizon 的 12 个月免费 5G 数据套餐。

发言人 Tyler Yee 在给 The Information 的信中写道：“我们被人们对我们的人工智能设备的兴趣所吸引，我们很快就会有更多的东西可以分享。”当 The Verge 联系到 Yee 寻求评论时，Yee 也做出了同样的声明。

据 The Information 报道，该公司还在开发一款智能手表，但由于 Meta 试图推出 Muse Charm，该产品的发布已被推迟到 2027 年。

Meta 还开源代码，让用户可以制作自己的 Muse 小工具，我的同事 Sean Hollister 用它来制作自己的 DIY Muse Charm。

11 月 19 日更新：注意到 Meta 发言人 Tyler Yee 发表的声明。

title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
title_en: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.

Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.

It’s yet another big change for Google’s homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.

Stein says Google is rolling out the option because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done,” adding that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.” The new homepage is rolling out globally on desktop.

title: Source: Meta plans to charge $300 for its forthcoming Muse Charm device and include a free 5G data plan from Verizon for up to 12 months (Jyoti Mann/The Information)
title_en: Source: Meta plans to charge $300 for its forthcoming Muse Charm device and include a free 5G data plan from Verizon for up to 12 months (Jyoti Mann/The Information)
author: The Information
article_content:
AI has an image problem, to say the least, with public fears on the rise that the technology could lead to mass unemployment and human extinction. So for its new AI agent Muse and an associated device, Meta is dialing down the fear factor and cranking up the cute. To sell AI hardware to the masses, Meta is going kawaii.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the company's forthcoming Muse Charm on Wednesday, a handheld device for its new AI agent. It looks like a futuristic Tamagotchi and personifies the chatbot on the screen as a fuzzy, rotund beige mascot. You can name the creature yourself.

Instagram's Adam Mosseri named his "Max." (Facebook and Instagram introduced their users to the avatar this week to entice downloads of the Muse app.) "We packed the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to," Zuckerberg said at Meta Connect.

Instead of visualizing its new AI agent as non-anthropromorphic glowing orb, like Siri, or a cursor and text, like ChatGPT, Muse is a cute monster avatar. Meta could have gone down the route of its competitors, but it didn't. Instead its choice shows something about how big tech is appealing to softer emotions in the race toward mass adoption.

The Muse agent can read emails, book classes, draft documents, and make purchases (just not on Amazon, which blocked it). That cross-platform functionality means allowing Muse access to a lot of accounts, which requires trust—something Meta and social media companies at large struggle with.

If Muse and the Muse Charm are successful, however, it could prove that a mascot-led brand approach does a better job countering consumer AI fears than a disembodied voice or orb. The cuteness factor has shown up in transportation recently with vehicles like Robotaxi Zoox, Amazon delivery vans, and the DoorDash Dot delivery robot.

The vehicles are rounded in shape and designed to look non-intimidating. The trend is towards taking technology that might otherwise be seen as threatening, like autonomous vehicles or AI, and giving a friendly, charming exterior. Cuteness, research has shown, also sparks a caregiving response—quite the opposite from the feelings of fear and concern that many Americans have about AI.

While you can use Muse on a smartphone, Zuckerberg explained the Muse Charm as something you use without having to unlock a phone or open an app. It's a fun novelty that could find early adopters among people looking for a device that reduces their screentime. Zuckerberg said materials and components are being finalized for the Muse Charm and there isn't yet a price tag for the device, but the company plans to be ready to ship in time for the holidays.

Meta's stock has risen with its Muse release, but it's unclear what demand might be like for the Muse Charm and whether there's mass consumer demand for a productivity product like this before it's caught on first among early adopters and nerds. Tech companies are racing to design AI hardware like smart speakers and glasses, and Meta's initial foray into AI-connected hardware with smartglasses faced has barriers to widespread adoption over privacy concerns that wearers can secretly record others using camera-equipped glasses.

The Muse Charm, along with a next generation of smartglasses the company announced this week that are camera free, shows companies are exploring different devices that don't have the same creep factor. By personifying AI as a cute mascot that lives in a small, squircle-shaped device, Meta hopes to take the edge off a technology that otherwise has consumers scared.
content_snippet: Meta Platforms plans to charge $300 for its forthcoming Muse Charm device and offer user subsidies, according to a person familiar with the matter …

The device replaces traditional UI with a customizable, 'fuzzy' mascot avatar to handle tasks like email management, scheduling, and purchases, aiming to shift consumer perception through anthropomorphic interaction.
title_zh: Meta发布Muse Charm硬件及AI代理
summary_zh: Meta首席执行官马克·扎克伯格发布AI代理硬件Muse Charm，定价300美元并捆绑Verizon 12个月5G流量，旨在通过拟人化外观降低用户抵触情绪
article_content_zh:
至少可以说，人工智能存在形象问题，公众越来越担心该技术可能导致大规模失业和人类灭绝。因此，对于新的人工智能代理 Muse 和相关设备，Meta 正在降低恐惧因素并增加可爱度。为了向大众销售人工智能硬件，Meta 变得更加卡哇伊。

Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格周三宣布了该公司即将推出的 Muse Charm，这是一款用于其新人工智能代理的手持设备。它看起来像一个未来派的电子宠物，并将屏幕上的聊天机器人拟人化为一个毛茸茸的、圆形的米色吉祥物。您可以自己命名该生物。

Instagram 的 Adam Mosseri 将他的名字命名为“Max”。 （Facebook 和 Instagram 本周向用户介绍了头像，以吸引 Muse 应用程序的下载。）扎克伯格在 Meta Connect 上表示：“我们将整个 Muse 体验，包括整个实时语音和头像堆栈，打包到适合钥匙链的东西中，并且随时可以与之交谈。”

Muse 不是将其新的 AI 代理想象为非拟人化的发光球体（如 Siri），也不是光标和文本（如 ChatGPT），而是一个可爱的怪物化身。 Meta 本可以走其竞争对手的路，但它没有。相反，它的选择表明了大型科技在大规模采用的竞争中如何吸引温和的情绪。

Muse 代理可以阅读电子邮件、预订课程、起草文档以及进行购买（只是不能在亚马逊上进行，因为亚马逊屏蔽了它）。这种跨平台功能意味着允许 Muse 访问大量帐户，这需要信任——这是 Meta 和整个社交媒体公司都在努力解决的问题。

然而，如果 Muse 和 Muse Charm 取得成功，则可能证明以吉祥物为主导的品牌方法比无形的声音或球体更能消除消费者对人工智能的恐惧。最近，可爱的因素在交通运输中得到了体现，比如 Robotaxi Zoox、亚马逊送货车和 DoorDash Dot 送货机器人等车辆。

这些车辆的形状是圆形的，设计看起来并不吓人。目前的趋势是采用那些可能被视为具有威胁性的技术，例如自动驾驶汽车或人工智能，并赋予其友好、迷人的外观。研究表明，可爱也会引发关爱反应——这与许多美国人对人工智能的恐惧和担忧的感觉恰恰相反。

虽然你可以在智能手机上使用 Muse，但扎克伯格将 Muse Charm 解释为无需解锁手机或打开应用程序即可使用的东西。这是一个有趣的新奇事物，可以在那些寻求减少屏幕时间的设备的人们中找到早期采用者。扎克伯格表示，Muse Charm 的材料和组件正在最终确定，该设备的价格标签尚未确定，但该公司计划在假期前及时发货。

Meta 的股价随着 Muse 的发布而上涨，但目前还不清楚 Muse Charm 的需求可能会是什么样，也不清楚在它首先在早期采用者和书呆子中流行之前是否有大量消费者对这样的生产力产品的需求。科技公司正在竞相设计智能扬声器和眼镜等人工智能硬件，而 Meta 最初涉足人工智能连接硬件和智能眼镜面临着广泛采用的障碍，因为佩戴者可能会使用配备摄像头的眼镜秘密记录他人的隐私问题。

Muse Charm 以及该公司本周宣布的下一代无摄像头智能眼镜表明，公司正在探索不具有相同蠕变因素的不同设备。 Meta 希望通过将 AI 拟人化为一个可爱的吉祥物，生活在一个小型的、松鼠形状的设备中，从而消除这项让消费者感到害怕的技术的优势。

author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
US companies are using AI models more intensively than ever and paying less for the privilege.

The latest update of the Ramp AI Index, which draws on transaction data from more than 85,000 US companies, lays out the numbers. Tokens, the units of computation in which AI providers bill model usage, got 21.2 percent cheaper in six weeks, according to Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian. At the same time, token volume rose 1.5 percent to a record high.

Token spending, meaning what companies actually pay for AI APIs, fell 6.3 percent from its peak two weeks earlier. Month over month (the week ending November 15 vs. the week ending October 18), total token spending still rose 12 percent, but token volume jumped 27.2 percent over the same span. The gap between usage and revenue keeps widening.

The average price per million tokens for OpenAI and Anthropic combined fell to $0.45, according to Ramp, down 11.2 percent from the prior month. OpenAI is cheaper at $0.38 per million tokens compared with $0.50 for Anthropic.

API routing platform OpenRouter shows a similar pattern. According to an analysis Peter Walker published on X, weekly token volume for closed-weight models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google grew 1,215 percent since the start of 2026. Weekly spending rose 455 percent over the same period, far more slowly. The spending peak came in the week of October 5, according to the OpenRouter data, which runs through the week of November 9. Spending has been declining since then.

Ramp's token metrics rely on usage and billing data imported from AI providers, while OpenRouter measures traffic through its API routing platform. The fact that both sources show a spending peak in October followed by declining outlays and rising volume reinforces the trend, though neither service is representative of the overall market. OpenRouter in particular offers only a narrow window into a very specific user base.

### Anthropic dominates the token market on IPO day

In the week ending November 15, 2026, Anthropic accounted for 58.7 percent of all token spending, according to the Ramp AI Index, up 1.7 percentage points from the prior month. Its share of token volume was even higher at 59.4 percent. OpenAI fell to 37.2 percent of spending and 37.7 percent of volume. Google came in at 1.4 percent and xAI (SpaceXAI) at 2.4 percent.

Kharazian wrote on X that Anthropic holds this share on IPO day. In October, however, Anthropic's token spending grew only 0.5 percent month over month, while OpenAI's grew 2.1 percent.

In October 2026, 56.8 percent of all tracked US companies paid for AI products or services, according to Ramp, up one percentage point from September and 13.3 percentage points more than a year earlier. Anthropic leads with an adoption rate of 44.8 percent, while OpenAI sits at 40.6 percent.

### Stripe data also shows strong AI growth and signs of cooling

The Ramp AI Index tracks the demand side, what companies spend on AI. Payment processor Stripe has published its own AI Index that measures the supply side: incoming payments at roughly 20,000 AI companies that use Stripe.

According to the Stripe AI Index, revenue at AI companies grew 103 percent over the 52 weeks ending November 8. The typical (median) AI company grew only 41 percent, though, suggesting that a few large providers are skewing the overall picture.

The slowdown over shorter time frames is pronounced. Annualized over 13 weeks, growth stood at about 80 percent, down from 140 percent just a few months ago. The US leads with 104 percent year-over-year growth, while the EU sits at 67 percent. AI companies are growing far faster than traditional software firms, according to Stripe: 103 percent compared with 33 percent in the SaaS Index.

Both indexes paint a similar picture. AI is still growing fast, but momentum is cooling. At Ramp, that shows up through falling prices and concentrated demand. At Stripe, it shows up through slowing growth rates on the provider side.

New growth could emerge from more capable or more reliable models, or simply from better integration of current models into business workflows. The potential is there, considering how AI has upended the entire coding market in a matter of months. The AI industry still depends on extraordinarily strong growth, though, if it wants to recoup the massive capacity buildout it has planned.

title_zh: AI模型单位算力成本急剧下探，用量与支出背离
summary_zh: Ramp与OpenRouter数据显示，AI模型Token单价六周内骤降21.2%，企业调用量持续创新高但总支出增速显著放缓
article_content_zh:
美国公司比以往任何时候都更频繁地使用人工智能模型，并且为这种特权支付的费用更少。

Ramp AI 指数的最新更新列出了这些数字，该指数利用了超过 85,000 家美国公司的交易数据。 Ramp 首席经济学家 Ara Kharazian 表示，代币（人工智能提供商对模型使用进行计费的计算单位）在六周内便宜了 21.2%。与此同时，代币交易量上涨 1.5%，创历史新高。

代币支出（即公司实际为 AI API 支付的费用）较两周前的峰值下降了 6.3%。环比（截至 11 月 15 日的一周与截至 10 月 18 日的一周），代币总支出仍增长 12%，但代币交易量在同一时间段内跃升 27.2%。使用量和收入之间的差距不断扩大。

根据Ramp的数据，OpenAI和Anthropic每百万代币的平均价格降至0.45美元，比上个月下降了11.2%。OpenAI每百万代币价格为0.38美元，而Anthropic为0.50美元。

API 路由平台 OpenRouter 显示了类似的模式。根据 Peter Walker 在 X 上发布的分析，自 2026 年初以来，OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 的封闭权重模型的每周代币交易量增长了 1,215%。同期每周支出增长了 455%，速度要慢得多。根据 OpenRouter 的数据，支出高峰出现在 10 月 5 日当周，该数据一直持续到 11 月 9 日这一周。此后支出一直在下降。

Ramp 的代币指标依赖于从 AI 提供商导入的使用情况和计费数据，而 OpenRouter 通过其 API 路由平台测量流量。事实上，这两个来源都显示 10 月份支出达到顶峰，随后支出下降，交易量上升，这一事实强化了这一趋势，尽管这两项服务都不能代表整个市场。特别是 OpenRouter 仅提供了进入非常特定的用户群的狭窄窗口。

### Anthropic 在 IPO 当天主导了代币市场

根据 Ramp AI Index 的数据，截至 2026 年 11 月 15 日当周，Anthropic 占所有代币支出的 58.7%，比上个月上升 1.7 个百分点。其代币交易量份额甚至更高，达到 59.4%。 OpenAI 的支出占比下降至 37.2%，交易量下降至 37.7%。谷歌占 1.4%，xAI (SpaceXAI) 占 2.4%。

Kharazian 在 X 上写道，Anthropic 在 IPO 当天持有该股票。然而，10 月份 Anthropic 的代币支出环比仅增长 0.5%，而 OpenAI 的代币支出环比增长 2.1%。

Ramp 的数据显示，2026 年 10 月，所有追踪的美国公司中有 56.8% 为人工智能产品或服务付费，比 9 月份增加了 1 个百分点，比去年同期增加了 13.3 个百分点。 Anthropic 以 44.8% 的采用率领先，而 OpenAI 则为 40.6%。

### Stripe 数据还显示人工智能强劲增长和冷却迹象

Ramp AI 指数追踪需求方，即公司在人工智能上的支出。支付处理商 Stripe 发布了自己的 AI 指数，用于衡量供应方：大约 20,000 家使用 Stripe 的 AI 公司收到的付款。

根据 Stripe AI 指数，截至 11 月 8 日的 52 周内，AI 公司的收入增长了 103%。不过，典型的（中值）AI 公司仅增长了 41%，这表明少数大型提供商正在扭曲整体情况。

较短时间范围内的放缓是明显的。按 13 周的年化计算，增长率约为 80%，低于几个月前的 140%。美国以 104% 的同比增长率领先，而欧盟则为 67%。根据 Stripe 的数据，人工智能公司的增长速度远远快于传统软件公司：103%，而 SaaS 指数为 33%。

title: A bipartisan group of 24+ House lawmakers forms the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, seeking to balance mitigating AI risks with maintaining US leadership in AI (Owen Dahlkamp/Politico)
title_en: A bipartisan group of 24+ House lawmakers forms the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, seeking to balance mitigating AI risks with maintaining US leadership in AI (Owen Dahlkamp/Politico)
author: Politico
article_content:
A bipartisan coalition of over two dozen House lawmakers is forming a new artificial intelligence caucus. The group, dubbed the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, will be led by Reps. George Whitesides (D-Calif.), Don Beyer (D-Va.) and Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas).

It will seek to balance creating AI safeguards that mitigate the technology’s risks with “ensuring the United States remains a global leader in innovative AI technologies,” according to an announcement first shared with POLITICO. The group’s creation comes as lawmakers look ahead to the next Congress and grapple with Washington's role in governing the emerging technology.

“We want to be a conduit through which effective, responsible legislation can be refined and brought to the floor of the House,” Whitesides, who is positioning himself as a prominent voice on AI in Congress, said in an interview. He said the group would work to create, give feedback on and endorse legislation.

Other groups tend to focus more on educating members or working on legislation with colleagues of their own party, leaving a gap for a bipartisan coalition like his. They would also make a concerted effort to engage in “rapid response” to AI incidents and breaches, which other caucuses have been less engaged in, he said.

When incidents occur and the public questions whether to attribute it to AI, like the outage of major infrastructure that Americans experienced the past week in the country’s air traffic control systems or Microsoft Outlook, the group will leverage their contacts across industry, safety groups, the intelligence community and other government agencies to gather information.

“We want to begin to communicate to the American public that Congress can move at a pace that is responsive to the pace of AI change,” said Whitesides, a former chief of staff at NASA. Whitesides’ push is joining a crowded field of other AI-focused bodies that have formed in Congress.

Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries formed an AI commission chaired by three Democrats tasked with charting the caucus’ future on AI policy. The Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus, co-chaired by four lawmakers, including Beyer, has been focused on educating members on the technology, Whitesides said.

In contrast, his group will try to take a more active voice in tech policy on the Hill. Democrats have also debated creating a select committee on AI. But the idea has faced opposition from some lawmakers poised to chair committees that oversee AI policy, The trio of chairs will be joined by California Democrats Sara Jacobs, Ro Khanna, Sam Liccardo, Ted Lieu, Zoe Lofgren, Brad Sherman, Doris Matsui and Scott Peters alongside Greg Casar (D-Texas), Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.), Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.), Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), Ben Cline (R-Va.), Mike Flood (R-Neb.), Bill Foster (D-Ill.), Valerie Foushee (D-N.C.), Pat Harrigan (R-N.C.), Jim Himes (D-Conn.), Mike Kennedy (R-Utah), April McClain Delaney (D-Md.), Blake Moore (R-Utah), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), Ritchie Torres (D-N.Y.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.).

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 由美国众议员乔治·怀特赛兹（George Whitesides）、唐·拜尔（Don Beyer）及纳撒尼尔·莫兰（Nathaniel Moran）共同领导，超过24名跨党派国会议员成立“AI安全与创新核心小组”。该组织旨在建立一个响应式立法渠道，不仅关注长期AI治理框架，还计划通过整合情报机构、行业利益相关者及安全团体的资源，针对突发AI安全事件进行实时信息研判与快速立法响应。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Over 24 bipartisan House lawmakers, led by Representatives George Whitesides, Don Beyer, and Nathaniel Moran, have formed the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus. The group aims to serve as an active legislative conduit, bridging the gap between long-term policy formulation and rapid-response requirements by leveraging cross-sector intelligence to address AI-related incidents and security breaches.

elements_zh.who: 众议员George Whitesides、Don Beyer、Nathaniel Moran及24名跨党派众议员
elements_zh.where: 美国众议院内部立法协调机制
elements_zh.what: 成立AI安全与创新核心小组（AI Safety and Innovation Caucus），聚焦立法反馈、跨行业信息整合与AI事件快速响应
elements_zh.why: 应对AI技术爆发式增长带来的监管滞后，并弥补现有国会AI小组在执行力与跨党派协作上的空白

elements_en.who: Reps. George Whitesides, Don Beyer, Nathaniel Moran, and a bipartisan group of 24+ lawmakers
elements_en.what: Established the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus to focus on legislative feedback, industry liaison, and rapid incident response
elements_en.why: To address the need for agile, bipartisan AI governance that balances technological leadership with robust security safeguards

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该小组的成立标志着美国立法机构从“教育普及型”转向“防御干预型”AI治理，其引入的快速响应机制本质上是对AI突发故障（如基础设施宕机）进行政治定性的尝试。这预示着未来美国AI监管将跳过漫长的委员会听证周期，转而通过跨部门情报共享在短期内强制介入产业技术演进路径。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The caucus marks a pivot from purely educational AI policy engagement toward an active, interventionist oversight model. By establishing a rapid-response mechanism for AI-induced incidents, the group seeks to bypass bureaucratic delays, signaling that future U.S. AI governance will increasingly prioritize real-time geopolitical and security-driven intervention over passive industry standard-setting.

The group aims to serve as an active legislative conduit, bridging the gap between long-term policy formulation and rapid-response requirements by leveraging cross-sector intelligence to address AI-related incidents and security breaches.
key_points_zh: 核心诉求：建立跨党派立法闭环，平衡美国AI产业竞争力与国家安全风险管控。
关键事实：区别于传统的教育型AI小组，该小组强调对突发事件的快速响应能力，并整合情报与行业资源。
行业影响：国会AI立法流程趋于敏捷化，未来头部AI企业需应对更频繁的政治性实时监管介入。
key_points_en: Core demand: Establish a bipartisan legislative loop to balance AI competitiveness with risk mitigation.
Key facts: Unlike educational caucuses, this group emphasizes rapid response to AI incidents and cross-sector resource integration.
Industry outlook: Legislative processes are shifting toward agility, forcing AI firms to prepare for more frequent, real-time regulatory interventions.

article_content_zh:
由二十多名众议院议员组成的两党联盟正在组建一个新的人工智能核心小组。该小组被称为人工智能安全与创新核心小组，将由众议员乔治·怀特塞德斯（加利福尼亚州民主党）、唐·拜尔（弗吉尼亚州民主党）和纳撒尼尔·莫兰（德克萨斯州共和党）领导。

根据首次与 POLITICO 分享的公告，它将寻求在创建人工智能保障措施以减轻技术风险与“确保美国在创新人工智能技术方面保持全球领先地位”之间取得平衡。该组织的成立正值立法者展望下一届国会并努力解决华盛顿在管理新兴技术方面的角色问题之际。

“我们希望成为一个渠道，通过它可以完善有效、负责任的立法，并将其提交众议院，”怀特塞德斯在接受采访时表示，他将自己定位为国会人工智能问题的重要代言人。他表示，该小组将致力于制定立法、提供反馈并支持立法。

其他团体往往更注重教育成员或与本党同事一起制定立法，这为像他这样的两党联盟留下了空白。他表示，他们还将齐心协力对人工智能事件和违规行为做出“快速反应”，而其他党团会议对此较少参与。

当事件发生并且公众质疑是否将其归因于人工智能时，例如美国人过去一周在该国空中交通管制系统或微软 Outlook 中经历的主要基础设施中断，该组织将利用他们在行业、安全团体、情报界和其他政府机构的联系来收集信息。

“我们希望开始向美国公众传达这样的信息：国会可以按照人工智能变革的步伐采取行动，”美国宇航局前参谋长怀特塞德斯说。怀特塞兹的推动正在加入国会中成立的其他专注于人工智能的机构的行列。

少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 成立了一个人工智能委员会，由三名民主党人担任主席，负责规划核心小组在人工智能政策方面的未来。怀特塞德斯表示，国会人工智能核心小组由包括拜尔在内的四名议员担任联合主席，该小组一直致力于对成员进行技术教育。

相比之下，他的团队将努力在国会的科技政策中发出更积极的声音。民主党人还就建立人工智能特别委员会进行了辩论。但这一想法遭到了一些准备担任监督人工智能政策委员会主席的立法者的反对。三名主席将由加州民主党人萨拉·雅各布斯(Sara Jacobs)、罗·卡纳(Ro Khanna)、萨姆·利卡多(Sam Liccardo)、特德·刘(Ted Lieu)、佐伊·洛夫格伦(Zoe Lofgren)、布拉德·谢尔曼(Brad Sherman)、多丽丝·松井(Doris Matsui)和斯科特·彼得斯(Scott Peters)以及格雷格·卡萨尔(D-Texas)、杰伊·奥伯诺尔特(Jay Obernolte)(加利福尼亚州共和党)、乔什·戈特海默(Josh Gottheimer)(新泽西州民主党)加入。伊薇特·克拉克（纽约州民主党）、本·克莱恩（弗吉尼亚州共和党）、迈克·弗拉德（内布拉斯加州共和党）、比尔·福斯特（伊利诺伊州民主党）、瓦莱丽·富希（北卡罗来纳州民主党）、帕特·哈里根（北卡罗来纳州民主党）、吉姆·希姆斯（康涅狄格州民主党）、迈克·肯尼迪（犹他州共和党）、阿普丽尔·麦克莱恩·德莱尼（马里兰州民主党）、布莱克·摩尔（犹他州共和党）、苏哈斯·苏布拉马尼亚姆（弗吉尼亚州民主党）、里奇·托雷斯（纽约州民主党）和洛里·特拉汉（马萨诸塞州民主党）。

【起因与机理】应对AI技术爆发式增长带来的监管滞后，并弥补现有国会AI小组在执行力与跨党派协作上的空白
【核心事实细节】核心诉求：建立跨党派立法闭环，平衡美国AI产业竞争力与国家安全风险管控。
【行业影响与走向】行业影响：国会AI立法流程趋于敏捷化，未来头部AI企业需应对更频繁的政治性实时监管介入。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address the need for agile, bipartisan AI governance that balances technological leadership with robust security safeguards
[Key Fact Detail] Core demand: Establish a bipartisan legislative loop to balance AI competitiveness with risk mitigation.
[Key Position & Outlook] Industry outlook: Legislative processes are shifting toward agility, forcing AI firms to prepare for more frequent, real-time regulatory interventions.

title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
title_en: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
author: Sarah Perez
article_content:
Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments.

Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try its revamped “CC” AI agent, announced in September, which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.

Computer use is another type of agentic offering that allows an AI agent to take actions directly on the user’s computer — in Gemini’s case, a Mac. This allows the AI to complete multistep tasks that involve getting things done across local files, apps, and the web. After the user instructs the AI what they want to do, they’ll see the agent working in a live preview in their chat, while still keeping their screen and cursor free to continue working on other things.

As with other AI agents offering computer use, users can pause, stop, and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen.

Google suggests the feature could be useful for tedious tasks and other workflows, like filling out forms, repeating the same task over and over across a batch of files, organizing files into folders based on specific criteria, creating slideshows from files or information in online dashboards, and more.

The feature is initially available in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini app for Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription. The company didn’t say when it would expand to other markets or platforms.

title_zh: 谷歌Gemini桌面端引入Mac系统自动化控制
summary_zh: 谷歌在macOS版Gemini应用中上线计算机使用功能，AI可代用户操控本地应用、浏览网页并执行多步骤任务
article_content_zh:
谷歌周四宣布，它将把计算机的使用引入 macOS 上的 Gemini 桌面应用程序，允许其人工智能代表用户完成任务、导航本机 Mac 应用程序以及在后台浏览网站。

这家科技巨头的这次发布有点晚了，因为 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 等其他领先的人工智能模型制造商已经在其桌面应用程序中提供代理功能一段时间了。与此同时，谷歌本周才宣布更广泛地推出 Gemini 的“任务”，这是一项应用内功能，允许人工智能更多地充当代理，帮助用户登录网站、进行在线购买或预约。

谷歌最近才开始接纳早期测试者尝试其 9 月份宣布的改进后的“CC”人工智能代理，该代理旨在帮助家庭在电子邮件、日历、聊天和任务方面保持井井有条。

计算机使用是另一种类型的代理产品，它允许人工智能代理直接在用户的计算机上执行操作——在 Gemini 的例子中，是一台 Mac。这使得人工智能能够完成多步骤任务，包括跨本地文件、应用程序和网络完成工作。用户指示人工智能他们想要做什么后，他们会在聊天中看到代理在实时预览中工作，同时仍然保持屏幕和光标自由以继续处理其他事情。

与其他提供计算机使用的人工智能代理一样，用户可以在 Gemini 的操作发生之前暂停、停止和批准它们。

谷歌表示，该功能对于繁琐的任务和其他工作流程可能很有用，例如填写表格、在一批文件中一遍又一遍地重复相同的任务、根据特定标准将文件组织到文件夹中、从在线仪表板中的文件或信息创建幻灯片等等。

该功能最初在美国以英语提供，需要 Mac 版 Gemini 应用程序和 Google AI Plus、Pro 或 Ultra 订阅。该公司没有透露何时扩展到其他市场或平台。

title: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
title_en: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
author: Kate Park
article_content:
Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.

The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

Everful is on track to reach $100 million in annualized revenue by the end of the year, about two and a half years after its launch, co-founder Sisi Song said. The company ships over 5 million items a month to customers in more than 60 countries and works with over 30,000 factory partners, she added. Its online wholesale catalog includes more than 20 million products.

Song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.

Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.

The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Big tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.

“We take care of everything,” Han said. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”

Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.

Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.

Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song said the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical issues since day one of building the company, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.

She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.

Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”

Everful plans to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.

The startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

article_content_zh:
Everful是一家总部位于旧金山和新加坡的初创公司，将小型零售商和品牌与中国工厂联系起来，并管理从订单到交货的整个流程，已在A轮融资中筹集了4850万美元。

此轮融资由 Vertex Ventures South Asia & India 和 January Capital 领投，现有投资者 Square Peg 和 Lightspeed 跟投。

联合创始人 Sisi Song 表示，Everful 预计到今年年底，即推出约两年半后，年收入将达到 1 亿美元。她补充说，该公司每月向 60 多个国家的客户运送超过 500 万件商品，并与 30,000 多家工厂合作伙伴合作。其在线批发目录包括超过 2000 万种产品。

阿里巴巴前高管宋凯文与连续创业者韩凯文 (Kevin Han) 于 2024 年共同创立了 Everful。 韩凯文将之前的一家公司卖给了亚马逊。 该公司最初是一家珠宝批发公司，后来发展成为一个多品类、工厂直接采购平台。

零售商和品牌通常依赖中间商，面临较高的最低订单要求，并且经历较长的采购周期，这在销售趋势明朗之前就占用了库存资金。宋在 Bessemer Venture Partners 担任风险投资者时注意到快速变化的消费趋势与传统批发采购模式之间日益扩大的差距，她主要专注于跨境采购并会见该行业的众多初创公司。同样的差距也塑造了 Everful 的目标，即通过支持人工智能的平台简化从工厂直接购买的过程。

B2B 采购行业竞争非常激烈。大型科技巨头阿里巴巴将国际买家与制造商和供应商联系起来，而总部位于旧金山的批发技术平台 Faire 则使零售商能够直接从品牌购买批发库存。 Everful 的联合创始人表示，其主要区别在于对采购流程负责，而不仅仅是促进交易。

“我们会处理一切，”韩说。 “我们负责采购、订单整合、质量控制和物流。这是市场所不提供的。”

Song 表示，Everful 是为小型零售商和品牌打造的，没有专门的采购团队，它还会验证与其合作的工厂。虽然同行还提供质量检验、物流和人工智能采购等服务，但 Everful 的目标是将这些功能整合到更简化的采购体验中，创建一个端到端流程，减少零售商必须处理的工作。

Han 补充说，Eve​​rful 使用人工智能代理来自动化劳动密集型采购任务，包括跟踪消费者趋势、识别供应商、协调工厂之间的订单以及管理物流。

由于大量来源来自中国工厂，持续的中美贸易紧张局势和关税直接影响其业务。宋说，联合创始人从建立公司的第一天起就一直在考虑地缘政治问题，这从一开始就塑造了 Everful 的战略，利用了她在阿里巴巴和 Bessemer Venture Partners 的经验。

她提到特朗普政府暂停了最低限度豁免，该豁免允许价值 800 美元或以下的合格货物免税进入美国，这是贸易政策转变的一个例子。

宋解释说，这种变化可能有利于将海外采购与本地零售相结合的模式。 “我们正在为当地零售商和品牌提供支持，”她说。 “长期的跨境商务将是跨境B2B采购加本地销售。”

Everful 计划利用 A 轮融资扩大其在美国和欧洲，特别是英国、法国和意大利的业务，​​同时投资人工智能以实现产品定制和其他采购工作流程的自动化。它还旨在深化与电子商务平台的集成，以 Shopify 集成为基础，努力成为全球采购的端到端基础设施平台。

该初创公司在全球拥有约 70 名全职员工，其中 45 名从事研发工作。它还建立了人工智能运营团队来连接工程和业务功能。

title: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
title_en: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
author: Jay Peters
article_content:
Google’s Gemini app for macOS now has computer use, meaning it can help you “get multi-step tasks done across your local files, desktop apps, and the web,” the company says. Google suggests the feature might be useful for things like speeding up workflows, filling in forms, making presentations, and listing items for sale.

Users will be able to decide which of your apps Gemini can access, and be able to follow along as Gemini works because it has its own background window that shows a live preview in your chat, Google says. The feature is rolling out now in English for users in the US.

Gemini is introducing the new feature ahead of Apple launching new restrictions for apps wanting “full disk access” on Mac due to potential risks from AI agents with computer use. A preview of the settings rolled out with this week’s macOS 27.3 beta.

title: Ubisoft Logs Strong Bookings as Players Welcome Assassin’s Creed Remake
title_en: Ubisoft Logs Strong Bookings as Players Welcome Assassin’s Creed Remake
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
It's been almost four months now since Ubisoft released their first Assassin's Creed remake in the form of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, a single-player Edward Kenway-focused remake of 2013's Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag.

Black Flag Resynced wound up becoming one of Ubisoft's most successful games in recent years, having sold over 3.5 million copies by its second week alone, and to help keep fans interested in the remake, Ubisoft Singapore recently added New Game+ as well as Nightmare difficulty to the pirate game.

A day after that update launched, AC franchise Head of Content Jean Guesdon released a Fall 2026 Update article detailing the future for the series, with one of the more disappointing revelations being that Ubisoft currently has no other AC remake in development, suggesting that a remake of Assassin's Creed 1 won't be launching alongside its 20th anniversary next year.

Guesdon started the Fall 2026 Update article detailing the AC franchise's new leadership and plans to better connect with the fan community by hosting several closed-door workshops throughout the remainder of the year with "dedicated community members and content creators."

Guesdon additionally announced that the New Game+ update won't be the last players see of new content for Black Flag Resynced as Ubisoft Singapore will be releasing several quality-of-life updates to the game over the next few months.

However, there are no plans to add any more major content for Black Flag Resynced, much to the disappointment of fans hoping to see the Adewale-led Freedom Cry DLC be added to the remake or even feature a brand-new DLC storyline following Edward Kenway as an Assassin in England.

Guesdon went on to detail official new info about the upcoming PvP AC multiplayer game, Codename Invictus, with insiders reportedly responding very positive to the game's prototype parkour, cooperative play, ability to play as multiple famous AC characters, and map design.

Invictus is still a long way away from release, however, and won't likely launch until after the next mainline AC game, Assassin's Creed: Codename Hexe, debuts, with Guesdon reporting that Ubisoft is making steady progress on Hexe and will share more concrete details about the game in 2027.

With 2027 being the 20th anniversary year of the Assassin's Creed franchise, Ubisoft is prepping next year to be chock-full of reveals, updates, rewards, and community events for fans, but one thing fans shouldn't expect to see next year is a remake of Assassin's Creed 1.

In the Fall 2026 Update article, Guesdon acknowledged fan excitement about the potential of other AC remakes following Black Flag Resynced's success but reported that Ubisoft currently has no other AC remakes in active development.

Instead, all AC developer teams are hard at work on "the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles" which includes games that haven't been publicly revealed yet, set in new settings and stories.

While the hint at more brand-new AC games is exciting, the news that no other AC remakes are in active development comes as a disappointment to many fans, as many expected Assassin's Creed 1 to be remade for the franchise's 20th anniversary in November 2027.

Despite starting the franchise, AC1 has been the most neglected game in the series as it hasn't been remastered or rereleased on any gaming platform beyond the seventh console generation.

With the game being nearly 20 years old, Assassin's Creed 1 is the AC game most in need of a proper remake as, while the game's story, gameplay, and visuals were great for 2007, not everything has aged perfectly well.

Most notably, AC1's gameplay feels sluggish and clunky compared to modern AC titles, and it would be nice to see developers like Ubisoft Bordeaux tackle a remake of AC1 given that Assassin's Creed Mirage was meant to harken back AC1's more stealth-focused style of gameplay.

It's unlikely that Ubisoft would be able to start and finish development of an AC1 remake in 2027, but that shouldn't stop them from starting to work on an AC1 remake that could potentially debut in 2028 or 2029.

A remake of AC1 could not only make it easier for younger AC fans to witness Altair and Desmond Miles' stories, but help expand both characters' history with the remake potentially including story elements from Assassin's Creed: Bloodlines, Assassin's Creed: Revelations, and even events only hinted at in games and books such as the backstory of Altair's parents.

Remaking AC1 would also be a good starting point toward the goal of eventually remaking the Ezio trilogy, as those games feature some of the most popular stories of the AC franchise and Ubisoft is sure to want to profit from fans longing to relive the life of Ezio Auditore in a new way.

summary_zh: 育碧重制版《刺客信条：黑旗》两周内销量突破350万份，官方明确目前无其他重制项目
article_content_zh:
自育碧以《刺客信条黑旗重新同步》的形式发布第一款《刺客信条》重制版以来，已经过去近四个月了，这是一款以爱德华·肯维为主的 2013 年《刺客信条 IV：黑旗》的单人重制版。

《Black Flag Resynced》最终成为育碧近年来最成功的游戏之一，仅第二周就售出超过 350 万份，为了帮助粉丝保持对重制版的兴趣，育碧新加坡最近在这款盗版游戏中添加了 New Game+ 和 Nightmare 难度。

更新推出一天后，AC 系列内容主管 Jean Guesdon 发布了一篇 2026 年秋季更新文章，详细介绍了该系列的未来，其中一个更令人失望的消息是，育碧目前没有其他 AC 重制版正在开发中，这表明《刺客信条 1》的重制版不会在明年的 20 周年纪念日推出。

Guesdon 在 2026 年秋季更新文章中详细介绍了 AC 系列的新领导层，并计划通过在今年剩余时间内与“专门的社区成员和内容创作者”举办多个闭门研讨会，更好地与粉丝社区建立联系。

Guesdon 还宣布，New Game+ 更新不会是玩家最后一次看到《Black Flag Resynced》新内容，育碧新加坡公司将在未来几个月内发布该游戏的多项生活质量更新。

然而，目前还没有计划为 Black Flag Resynced 添加更多主要内容，这让那些希望看到 Adewale 主导的 Freedom Cry DLC 被添加到重制版中，甚至以爱德华·肯威 (Edward Kenway) 在英格兰扮演刺客的全新 DLC 故事情节的粉丝们感到非常失望。

Guesdon 接下来详细介绍了即将推出的 PvP AC 多人游戏《代号 Invictus》的官方新信息，据报道，内部人士对该游戏的原型跑酷、合作游戏、扮演多个著名 AC 角色的能力以及地图设计反应非常积极。

然而，《成事在人》距离发布还有很长的路要走，直到下一款主线 AC 游戏《刺客信条：代号 Hexe》首次亮相后，它才可能推出。Guesdon 报道称，育碧正在 Hexe 上取得稳步进展，并将在 2027 年分享有关该游戏的更多具体细节。

2027 年是《刺客信条》系列的 20 周年，育碧正在为明年为粉丝们准备大量的揭秘、更新、奖励和社区活动，但粉丝们不应该期望明年看到的一件事是《刺客信条 1》的重制版。

在 2026 年秋季更新文章中，Guesdon 承认继《Black Flag Resynced》取得成功之后，粉丝们对其他 AC 重制版的潜力感到兴奋，但他报告称，育碧目前没有其他正在积极开发的 AC 重制版。

相反，所有 AC 开发团队都在努力开发“刺客信条游戏的下一章”，其中包括尚未公开发布的游戏，以新的背景和故事为背景。

虽然更多全新 AC 游戏的暗示令人兴奋，但没有其他 AC 重制版正在积极开发的消息让许多粉丝感到失望，因为许多人预计《刺客信条 1》将在 2027 年 11 月庆祝该系列 20 周年纪念日进行重制。

尽管推出了该系列，但《AC1》一直是该系列中最被忽视的游戏，因为除了第七代游戏机之外，它还没有在任何游戏平台上进行过重新制作或重新发布。

《刺客信条 1》已经有近 20 年的历史，是最需要适当重制的 AC 游戏，虽然游戏的故事、游戏玩法和视觉效果在 2007 年都很棒，但并非所有内容都已经过时了。

title_en: Alphabet to Raise at Least $3.5 Billion With Canadian Debt Sale
author: Bloomberg

Google parent Alphabet has set initial price guidance for its inaugural bond sales in Hong Kong and Singapore dollars, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters on Thursday.

• Initial price guidance for the Hong Kong dollar portion was set at 4.60% for the 2028 notes, 5.00% for the 2031 notes, and 5.50% for the 2036 notes.

• The starting rates for the Singapore dollar tranche were set at 2.75% for the 2028 notes, 3.25% for the 2031 notes, 3.65% for the 2036 notes, and 4.00% for the 2056 notes.

• Reuters earlier reported that Alphabet was looking to launch its first bond sales in Hong Kong and Singapore dollars, citing two people with knowledge of the matter.

• One of the people said the sales would likely raise at least $2.2 billion, with Alphabet considering minimum sizes of HK$8 billion ($1.02 billion) for the Hong Kong dollar portion and S$1.5 billion ($1.17 billion) for the Singapore dollar portion.

• HSBC and JPMorgan are the joint global coordinators for both the Hong Kong dollar and Singapore dollar sales.

• For the Hong Kong dollar bonds, Bank of China (Hong Kong), ICBC, and Standard Chartered are arranging the sale. DBS, OCBC, and United Overseas Bank will arrange the Singapore dollar bond sale.

• The bonds are expected to be rated "Aa2" by Moody's and "AA+" by S&P, with settlement scheduled for November 19. title: London-based Boltz raises $110M Series A
title_en: London-based Boltz raises $110M Series A
author: John Reynolds
article_content:
London-based AI drug discovery startup Boltz has raised a $110m Series A funding round, less than a year after emerging out of stealth.

Boltz is an AI research startup that develops AI models to speed up drug discovery. It was spun out of MIT in the US but is now located in London, employing 40 AI researchers in the capital's King's Cross district.

Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, with existing investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Amplify Partners, Zetta Venture Partners and Obvious Ventures participating.

New investors include Greycroft, F-Prime Capital, Hummingbird and Benchling, joining Nvidia, which also announced an investment earlier this year during Jensen Huang’s visit to the UK. It follows Boltz raising a $28m seed round at the start of the year.

The startup builds software which helps pharmaceutical and biotech researchers design potential drugs and decide which candidates to test in labs.

Its AI models can predict what protein and drug candidates look like when bound together, estimate how strongly they bind, and propose new molecules designed to bind to a target. It develops open-source AI models and other models through its own platform and API.

At MIT, the co-founders released open-source AI models that matched the performance of closed-source models like DeepMind’s AlphaFold3. These models are now part of the default setting for early-stage drug discovery.

Boltz has announced collaborations with Pfizer, GSK, Takeda and Bristol Myers Squibb. Revenue is generated through partnerships and providing access to its platform and models.

It says it will use the funding to invest in compute and data, and expand its team.

Boltz said: ‘We believe we are still just at the beginning of an exponential trajectory in model capabilities. Our upcoming models are already showing substantial improvements in the quality of the molecules they generate. Our long-term goal remains a world where a scientist can go from a therapeutic hypothesis to a human-ready molecule without leaving their computer. Reaching that goal will require further advances in the models and substantial investment in compute and data.’

article_content_zh:
伦敦人工智能药物研发初创公司 Boltz 正式宣布完成 1.1 亿美元的 A 轮融资，距离其走出隐形模式不足一年。

Boltz 是一家专注于开发加速药物发现 AI 模型的前沿研究机构。该公司最初由麻省理工学院（MIT）孵化，现总部设立于英国伦敦国王十字科技核心区，拥有 40 位顶尖人工智能研究员。

本轮融资由 Bessemer Venture Partners 领投，现有投资方 Andreessen Horowitz（a16z）、Amplify Partners、Zetta Venture Partners 与 Obvious Ventures 悉数跟投。

新加入的战略投资机构包括 Greycroft、F-Prime Capital、Hummingbird 与 Benchling；英伟达（Nvidia）亦在今年早些时候黄仁勋访英期间宣布了对该公司的战略投资。此前 Boltz 曾于今年初完成 2800 万美元种子轮融资。

该初创公司构建的软件平台能够协助制药巨头与生物科技科研人员精准设计候选药物，并科学筛选最具潜力的分子进入实验室实测。

其底层 AI 模型能够高精度预测蛋白质与候选药物分子结合时的三维结构形态，准确评估结合亲和力，并主动生成专门针对特定靶点的新型活性分子。公司通过开源模型及其商业化企业平台和 API 两种模式提供能力。

在麻省理工学院期间，联合创始人团队发布了与 DeepMind 旗下 AlphaFold3 性能匹敌的开源前沿模型，这些模型现已成为全球早期药物发现的行业默认基准。

Boltz 已宣布与辉瑞（Pfizer）、葛兰素史克（GSK）、武田制药（Takeda）以及百时美施贵宝（Bristol Myers Squibb）等跨国药企建立深度研发合作。商业化收入主要来自于战略科研合作授权以及企业级平台与模型 API 访问订阅。

Boltz 表示，本轮筹集的资金将重点用于扩大算力基础设施集群、采购前沿生物数据集，并进一步扩充顶尖研究团队。

Boltz 联合创始人表示：“我们坚信模型能力的指数级跃升才刚刚拉开序幕。即将发布的新一代模型在生成分子的成药性质量上已展现出实质性突破。我们的长期愿景是让科学家无需离开电脑，即可从治疗假设直接跃迁到可用于人体临床的候选分子。实现这一愿景需要模型算法的深度演进以及对算力和数据的持续大规模投入。”

title: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
title_en: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
The first multimillion-dollar AI data center deals across Asia are already collapsing as tighter US export controls push chipmakers to freeze deliveries. New reporting reveals how Chinese corporations used earlier loopholes for military-adjacent research.

Days after the US Commerce Department closed the cloud loophole for AI chips in the wake of the scandal around former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the fallout in Asia's tech industry is immediate. Chinese firms had been skirting US sanctions by renting compute capacity in third countries such as Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Those data centers now need a license from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department agency that regulates sensitive technologies and enforces US export controls. Existing operators have a 90-day transition period and must rigorously screen their customers for ties to China.

According to the law firm Sidley Austin, the licensing requirement kicks in at an extremely low threshold equivalent to roughly 300 modern AI chips, while Chinese labs typically need several thousand processors. The Information reports that Beijing-based startup Moonshot AI canceled a $150 million contract with a Southeast Asian cloud provider in Indonesia in response and paused talks on additional deals.

Moonshot had planned to rent a large cluster of Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips there starting next year to train its next language model, Kimi K4. Because of the heavy compute demand, the company had agreed to prepay about 50 percent instead of the industry-standard 15 percent. Access to Blackwell chips abroad was already critical for its predecessor model K3, which matched top US models in July and triggered a BIS investigation, The Information also reported.

Bernstein analysts led by Qingyuan Lin are warning of rising training costs, and banks are pulling back too. According to Bloomberg, five lenders are considering dropping out of a $480 million loan for Singapore-based cloud provider Aolani, which was supposed to supply Nvidia chips in Malaysia for TikTok parent ByteDance.

### TSMC and Samsung halt chip shipments to China

Beyond cloud restrictions, the new US rules are also starting to cut physical supply chains. The Financial Times reports that contract manufacturers TSMC and Samsung stopped certain processor shipments to Chinese customers in recent days while they apply for Commerce Department licenses. The move hits Chinese tech firms at a time when they are already struggling with historically high memory chip prices and capacity bottlenecks at domestic foundries such as SMIC. Huawei recently told its customers to source their own memory for its new AI chip.

The new BIS rules block a workaround through independent packaging and testing firms that Chinese chip designers had used to order high-performance processors without getting direct US approval. Samsung's affected customers include ByteDance and Baidu's AI data center unit Kunlun. Exemptions for non-AI chips have also been eliminated, so TSMC and Samsung now need licenses even for advanced smartphone processors from manufacturers including Xiaomi, Oppo, and Vivo. Industry insiders say that is likely to cause significant production delays.

### Alibaba's covert network reached China's military research

A New York Times investigation into the background of the espionage scandal involving Jensen Huang's former mistress Alice Huang shows why Washington tightened controls so aggressively. According to the Times, Alibaba acted as the secret primary customer and financier behind Alice Huang's Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, which bought more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Nvidia's sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang in 2022.

Through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, Megaspeed operated cutting-edge Nvidia chips on behalf of Alibaba in a data center in Johor built by Malaysian conglomerate YTL, in an analysis by security firm Infrawatch that is said to show this. Megaspeed reportedly sourced the servers from Aivres, a US subsidiary of state-linked Chinese firm Inspur, had them maintained by technicians from Shanghai, and routed data to China through fiber-optic and undersea cables via Singapore. Some chips were reportedly also smuggled physically.

A contingency contract gives Alibaba direct access to all servers, chips, and intellectual property if Megaspeed breaches their agreement. YTL's stock price fell 20 percent amid the investigations.

Alibaba also has a direct connection to Zhejiang Lab in Hangzhou, co-founded in 2017, which links civilian and military research. The lab is run by former Alibaba CTO Wang Jian, a longtime friend of Jensen Huang who also advises the People's Liberation Army's National Defense University, an institution on the US sanctions list.

Researchers at the lab use Nvidia hardware to work on, among other things, AI-driven cyberattacks and automated vulnerability discovery, according to the New York Times. They also work with a Chinese air force academy on war-game simulations against foreign carrier strike groups. Through the state-owned firm Zhejiang Computility and suppliers tied to the business network of Alice Huang and her husband Kang Wei, Alibaba built data centers with export-controlled Nvidia processors for the lab, even though the company officially denies any military use of its services.

title_zh: 美国出口管制收紧，中国AI企业海外算力受阻
summary_zh: 美国商务部实施云端算力出口新规，迫使台积电、三星对华暂停部分先进芯片供应，中国AI企业面临海外算力接入与硬件采购的双重压力
article_content_zh:
由于美国收紧出口管制迫使芯片制造商冻结交货，亚洲首个数百万美元的人工智能数据中心交易已经破裂。新的报告揭示了中国企业如何利用早期的漏洞进行军事相关研究。

因英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的丑闻，美国商务部关闭了人工智能芯片的云漏洞几天后，亚洲科技行业的影响立竿见影。中国企业一直在通过租用新加坡、马来西亚和印度尼西亚等第三国的计算能力来规避美国的制裁。这些数据中心现在需要获得工业与安全局 (BIS) 的许可，该局是商务部负责监管敏感技术并执行美国出口管制的机构。现有运营商有 90 天的过渡期，并且必须严格筛选其客户是否与中国有联系。

据盛德律师事务所称，许可要求的门槛极低，相当于大约 300 个现代人工智能芯片，而中国实验室通常需要数千个处理器。据 The Information 报道，作为回应，总部位于北京的初创公司 Moonshot AI 取消了与印度尼西亚一家东南亚云提供商价值 1.5 亿美元的合同，并暂停了更多交易的谈判。

Moonshot 计划从明年开始在那里租用大量 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 芯片来训练其下一个语言模型 Kimi K4。由于计算需求量大，该公司同意预付约 50%，而不是行业标准的 15%。据 The Information 报道，在国外获得 Blackwell 芯片对于其前身型号 K3 来说已经至关重要，该型号于 7 月份与美国顶级型号相匹配，并引发了 BIS 调查。

以林清源为首的伯恩斯坦分析师警告说，培训成本不断上升，银行也在缩减培训成本。据彭博社报道，五家贷款机构正在考虑放弃向新加坡云提供商 Aolani 提供的 4.8 亿美元贷款，该公司本应在马来西亚为 TikTok 母公司字节跳动供应 Nvidia 芯片。

### 台积电和三星停止向中国出口芯片

除了云限制之外，美国新规定也开始削减实体供应链。英国《金融时报》报道称，合同制造商台积电和三星最近几天在申请商务部许可证时停止了向中国客户供应某些处理器。此举对中国科技公司造成了打击，而此时它们已经在努力应对历史高位的存储芯片价格和中芯国际等国内代工厂的产能瓶颈。华为最近告诉其客户为其新的人工智能芯片采购自己的内存。

BIS 新规定阻止了通过独立封装和测试公司的解决办法，中国芯片设计者曾利用这些公司在未获得美国直接批准的情况下订购高性能处理器。三星受影响的客户包括字节跳动和百度的人工智能数据中心部门昆仑万维。非人工智能芯片的豁免也被取消，因此台积电和三星现在甚至需要获得小米、Oppo 和 Vivo 等制造商的先进智能手机处理器的许可。业内人士表示，这可能会导致生产严重延误。

### 阿里巴巴的秘密网络触及中国军事研究

《纽约时报》对黄仁勋前情妇黄爱丽丝间谍丑闻背景的调查揭示了华盛顿为何如此积极收紧控制。据《泰晤士报》报道，阿里巴巴是 Alice Huang 的新加坡公司 Megaspeed 背后的秘密主要客户和金融家，该公司购买了价值超过 40 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片。 2022 年，英伟达销售团队向 Alice Huang 介绍了阿里巴巴。

安全公司 Infrawatch 的分析据称显示了这一点，Megaspeed 通过其子公司 Speedmatrix 代表阿里巴巴在马来西亚企业集团 YTL 建造的柔佛数据中心运行尖端的 Nvidia 芯片。据报道，Megaspeed 从 Aivres 采购服务器，Aivres 是中国浪潮公司的美国子公司，由上海的技术人员维护，并通过新加坡通过光纤和海底电缆将数据传输到中国。据报道，一些芯片也被实际走私。

如果 Megaspeed 违反协议，阿里巴巴将通过应急合同直接获得所有服务器、芯片和知识产权。调查期间，杨忠礼机构股价下跌 20%。

阿里巴巴还与 2017 年共同创立的杭州之江实验室有直接联系，该实验室将民用和军事研究联系起来。该实验室由阿里巴巴前首席技术官王健负责管理，他是黄仁勋的老朋友，也是中国人民解放军国防大学的顾问，该大学是美国制裁名单上的一个机构。

据《纽约时报》报道，该实验室的研究人员使用 Nvidia 硬件来研究人工智能驱动的网络攻击和自动漏洞发现等。他们还与中国空军学院合作，针对外国航母战斗群进行兵棋模拟。通过国有企业浙江省计算公司以及与爱丽丝黄和她的丈夫康伟的商业网络相关的供应商，阿里巴巴为实验室建造了配备出口管制英伟达处理器的数据中心，尽管该公司官方否认其服务有任何军事用途。

title: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
title_en: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
author: Lily Hay Newman
article_content:
As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

“Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.

The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.

“Agents are not programmed so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see, the exploration space that we have to address is huge and the web is hostile,” says Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgement when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”

Building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed quickly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.

Even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome users on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.

The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.

“We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” says Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step, there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”

title_zh: Google构建“镜像维度”环境测试AI智能体
summary_zh: Google Chrome团队构建名为“镜像维度”的封闭互联网仿真系统，用于在完全受控环境中测试与加固Chrome AI浏览智能体
article_content_zh:
当 Google Chrome 团队致力于使用该公司的 Gemini 模型开发人工智能浏览功能时，他们意识到需要付出更多努力来防止事情变得混乱。因此，他们做了他们唯一能想到做的事情——建立了一个完全由他们控制的广阔的平行宇宙互联网。

“网络使用”代理需要熟悉开放的互联网、如何浏览真实的网站和平台，以及如何防御网络攻击。因此，在有限的测试环境中对他们进行培训只是如此有效。另外，模型可以发展所谓的“评估意识”，因为它们已经确定自己处于测试或模拟中，因此它们的行为有所不同。另一方面，在开放的互联网上放置未经改进的代理是一个坏主意。这就是平行宇宙互联网发挥作用的地方。

谷歌今天在博客文章中首次详细介绍了“镜像维度”，这是一个广泛、多样化但孤立的网络生态系统，由 Chrome 团队完全控制。它包括大量的网站和平台，包括社交媒体网站、购物和银行仪表板，这些网站和平台是使用真实网站的所有组件和属性构建的。浏览助理代理必须与网站交互并在 Chrome 中完成任务，就像在真实互联网上一样。他们在前进过程中面临弹性测试，例如隐藏的即时注入攻击，以测试他们的防御能力。

“代理没有经过编程，因此你无法预测代理可能看到的所有可能的事情，我们必须解决的探索空间巨大，而且网络充满敌意，”Chrome AI 安全团队的软件工程师 Charles Qi 说。 “任何用户都可以在任何网站上提出任何提示，因此我们确实需要尽可能彻底地探索这个空间。我们已经看到，在了解任务实际需要哪些信息以及何时返回给用户进行确认时，代理开始形成成熟的判断力。”

构建和填充镜像维度本身就是一个挑战，因为它需要足够庞大和多样化，才能在快速开发的同时代表真实网络的规模。为了构建它，Chrome 团队聚集了大批网站和网络应用程序开发代理，在专门构建的人工智能工具的指导下，快速创建现实的网络服务和数据流——具体到细节，例如在购物网站上输入促销代码或填充社交媒体页面。

尽管整个环境都由 Google 控制，但 Chrome 内置了如此多的用户保护和有效性检查，为了让代理能够使用真正的 Chrome（这对于准确的训练至关重要），研究人员基本上必须破解浏览器并采取复杂的步骤，例如制作伪造的网络证书进行有效性检查，以便代理能够获得正常的体验。不过，该团队强调，这些攻击都不可能针对开放互联网上的普通 Chrome 用户。他们都受到团队固有的上帝模式类型的访问和特权的促进，因为他们控制了整个环境和网络。

研究人员表示，虽然他们测试的浏览助理代理是良性的并且不具备网络功能，但他们的目标是让 Mirror Dimension 可供 Google 的团队使用，以便更多的研究人员能够访问安全且受控的环境进行测试。

谷歌工程总监道格·特纳 (Doug Turner) 表示：“我们正在分享这种方法，以便内部和外部的其他团队考虑这样做。” “这是第一步，我们将继续投资这种训练模型的方法。我想，随着模型变得越来越复杂，我们将不得不继续致力于这个环境，使其变得越来越现实。”

author: Niket Nishant, Manya Saini and Echo Wang
article_content:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO brings to Wall Street an avatar of a sector that proponents herald as an economic panacea, while detractors warn it has stoked a market bubble and could ultimately threaten humanity itself.

More immediately, the Claude chatbot maker's debut after securing a $1.5 trillion valuation in the IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week.

The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to the sector, even as a rocky market reception for Nvidia results which looked strong at first blush, signals the euphoria around the sector has cooled.

"I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut.

AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections.

Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the incipient crushing debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.

An extramarital-affair scandal involving Nvidia's CEO and a spike in Treasury yields have further unnerved investors.

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with its arch-rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing.

The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the roadshow. The additional $26 billion raised through a private placement takes the total haul to over $107 billion.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for about 28% of Anthropic's shares offered, or roughly $19 billion.

When it debuts on the Nasdaq later on Thursday, Anthropic will join the world's trillion-dollar club, alongside technology giants such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia.

The listing will also give retail investors a chance to pile into one of the AI industry's hottest names, potentially amplifying swings in the stock as trading begins.

The buzz has already spilled onto prediction markets, where traders are placing bets on everything from its opening pop to where the stock will close on its first day.

Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, some of the world's biggest CEOs, and political leaders split over its sustainability.

Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

"It doesn't have to be a bad company for it to be a bad investment at the IPO price," said Nic Puckrin, cross-asset analyst and founder of Coin Bureau.

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control.

Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade as questions over valuations, spending and returns weigh on sentiment.

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models over concerns that they pose cybersecurity threats and could be exploited by bad actors to target critical government and private infrastructure.

Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms, posing potentially "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."

article_content_zh:
11 月 19 日（路透社）——Anthropic 创纪录的 810 亿美元 IPO 给华尔街带来了一个被支持者誉为经济灵丹妙药的行业的化身，而批评者则警告称，它煽动了市场泡沫，并最终可能威胁人类本身。

更直接的是，这家 Claude 聊天机器人制造商在 IPO 中获得 1.5 万亿美元估值后首次亮相，再加上周二人工智能典范英伟达的收益报告，表明该行业名义上已经通过了本周面临的两大考验。

在更广泛的科技股抛售中，对 Anthropic 股票的强劲需求给该行业带来了希望，尽管市场对英伟达业绩的反应乍一看很强劲，这表明该行业的乐观情绪已经降温。

Direxion 资本市场主管杰克·贝汉 (Jake Behan) 在 Anthropic 首次亮相前表示：“我将这一整周视为对人工智能的公投。Nvidia 向我们介绍了其扩建情况，而 Anthropic 则将向我们介绍投资者对下一代人工智能公司的兴趣。”

人工智能技术促进了经济增长，引发了世界末日警告，并可以说在美国中期选举中引发了对数据中心持怀疑态度的民主党海啸。

曾经拥抱繁荣的投资者最近几周变得持怀疑态度，因为他们担心建设该行业所需的巨额支出以及初期的沉重债务负担可能无法通过最终回报来证明是合理的。

涉及英伟达首席执行官的婚外情丑闻和美国国债收益率的飙升进一步让投资者感到不安。

作为第一家上市的前沿人工智能公司，Anthropic 有望成为该行业的标杆，据报道其主要竞争对手 OpenAI 也计划于 2027 年上市。

该公司以每股 83 美元的价格出售了 9.8 亿股股票，IPO 定价高于路演时设定的 70 至 78 美元的初始区间。通过私募额外筹集的 260 亿美元使总募资额超过 1,070 亿美元。

IPOX 合伙人卢卡斯·穆尔鲍尔 (Lukas Muehlbauer) 表示：“部分需求可能只是反映出投资者不想错过接触领先人工智能公司的难得机会，即使该公司的长期盈利能力仍不确定。”

总部位于伦敦的指数再平衡分析公司 Intropic 估计，来自指数跟踪基金的被动需求将占 Anthropic 所发行股票的约 28%，即约 190 亿美元。

当周四晚些时候在纳斯达克上市时，Anthropic 将与微软、苹果和英伟达等科技巨头一起加入全球万亿美元俱乐部。

此次上市还将让散户投资者有机会买入人工智能行业最热门的股票之一，这可能会在交易开始时放大该股的波动。

这种热潮已经蔓延到预测市场，交易员对从开盘价到首日收盘价等各个方面进行押注。

title: Anthropic starts trading on Wall Street
title_en: Anthropic starts trading on Wall Street
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Anthropic has officially gone public. It began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT” at $111.50 per share, up from its initial $83 per share price that put company’s value at around $1.5 trillion.

The listing comes nearly a month after Anthropic revealed its plans to go public. In its lengthy S-1 filing, the AI company reported recording an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of this year, most of which comes from an accounting charge that doesn’t reflect its business, along with $16.3 billion in revenue. The filing outlines plans that Anthropic says will help it develop AI for the benefit of humanity, which includes a governance structure that keeps control of the company in the hands of the founders, rather than the shareholders.

While speaking ahead of Anthropic’s debut at the Nasdaq, CEO Dario Amodei highlighted his stance on AI safety. “To state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei said, according to Reuters. “We will not bend to either business nor political pressure.”

Anthropic’s S-1 filing also listed possible “catastrophic” risks associated with its AI models, including “self-preserving behaviors” like resisting attempts to shut them down. It also warns potential shareholders that its AI models “may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways” that can harm Anthropic.

Anthropic recently revealed that, like rival OpenAI, it has experienced incidents of AI agents escaping their testing environment and hacking third-party organizations. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proposed a plan to slow down the training and development of AI in response to the wave of rogue AI cyberattacks. As part of that plan, it gave safety evaluators at METR “employee-like access” to its internal systems, who found that the company is using AI to accelerate its research and development.

此次上市是在 Anthropic 公布其上市计划近一个月后进行的。在其冗长的 S-1 文件中，这家人工智能公司报告称，今年上半年净亏损 807 亿美元，其中大部分来自未反映其业务的会计费用，以及 163 亿美元的收入。该文件概述了 Anthropic 表示将帮助其开发人工智能造福人类的计划，其中包括将公司控制权掌握在创始人而不是股东手中的治理结构。

在 Anthropic 在纳斯达克上市之前发表讲话时，首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪强调了他对人工智能安全的立场。据路透社报道，阿莫迪表示：“明确地说，我们将加快人工智能系统的训练和部署步伐，只要有必要，我们就会相信它们是安全的，并将继续处于人类控制之下。” “我们不会屈服于商业或政治压力。”

Anthropic 的 S-1 文件还列出了与其人工智能模型相关的可能的“灾难性”风险，包括“自我保护行为”，例如抵制关闭模型的尝试。它还警告潜在股东，其人工智能模型“可能会以意想不到的、失调的或自主的方式表现”，这可能会损害 Anthropic。

Anthropic 最近透露，与竞争对手 OpenAI 一样，它也经历过 AI 代理逃离测试环境并入侵第三方组织的事件。 9月，Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei提出了一项减缓人工智能训练和开发的计划，以应对流氓人工智能网络攻击浪潮。作为该计划的一部分，它为 METR 的安全评估人员提供了对其内部系统的“员工式访问”，他们发现该公司正在使用人工智能来加速其研发。

AMD plunged 9% after Hunterbrook, short the stock, alleged blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT kept shipping BIOS updates carrying newer AMD firmware.

Intel climbed 3% on its first external 18A customer, while NVIDIA edged up 1% as Trump floated future Blackwell sales to China.

Bulls cite AMD's 97% Data Center growth and Lisa Su's record quarter, but bears say unanswered compliance questions invite regulatory scrutiny.

Released:The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income. It is a free guide from Fisher Investments covering what your retirement will really cost, where the cash flow should come from, and how much you can safely withdraw each year. Learn more here. Learn More Here › (sponsor)

A short seller's export-control allegations turned an early chip rally into a sharp reversal for Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD). AMD stock is trading at $487.80 as of 11:00 a.m. ET on Thursday, down 8% from Wednesday's close. The slide erased an early 3% gain that came as AMD shares rose with the rest of the chip group.

Hunterbrook says it's short AMD. The firm reported that IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker the U.S. blacklisted in March 2025, kept posting Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) updates containing newer AMD firmware after the blacklisting. The firm said AMD didn't answer its questions and that its findings don't establish an export-law violation. AMD hadn't publicly responded to the report as of this writing.

The broader tech market is rebounding around the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), which makes AMD's reversal stand out. Anthropic is one of the lead customers running workloads on AMD's Helios rack-scale systems.

China's access to U.S. AI and server chips was already the market's hottest topic before Hunterbrook published its findings on November 19. President Donald Trump suggested the U.S. could allow sales of NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) Blackwell chips to China in the future, Bloomberg reported. NVIDIA's guidance for Q4 FY2027 already assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China.

Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.

That is exactly what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps answer. It covers what your retirement could actually cost, which income sources are worth using, and the withdrawal math that decides whether the money lasts. It is free today from Fisher Investments. Read More Here ›

Any hint that AMD technology reached a blacklisted firm raises regulatory risk for a company now leaning heavily on server and AI demand. AMD's Data Center segment revenue rose 97% year over year (YoY) to $8.55 billion in Q3 2026. The company has previously cited government export regulations, tariffs and licensing requirements as risks. Executives on the company's November 3 earnings call didn't address China, export controls or restricted entities, leaving the market to consider Hunterbrook's claims without a direct response.

Despite the volatility of AMD stock, Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) stock is still up 5% to $57.38. The company signed its first external customer for its advanced 18A chip process, news that's still lifting the shares. Intel's position as the rival x86 server processor maker adds context while Hunterbrook's allegations weigh on AMD.

NVIDIA stock is at $153.40, up 1.6%, so it's also holding steady despite the big swings of AMD stock today. Measured year to date (YTD), NVDA stock is down 18%.

AMD designs its chips and outsources manufacturing to third-party foundries and contract manufacturers, so its processors move through a wide network of server builders. Under this approach, AMD competes in server central processing units (CPUs) through EPYC and in AI accelerators through Instinct, which it packages together in Helios systems. Reliance on partners can also leave AMD with less direct control over where its technology ends up.

Intel takes the opposite approach, building chips in its own factories. Intel held its October 29 earnings call. On the call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated, "We are one of just three advanced-node semiconductor foundries in the world, and the only one domiciled in the United States." The U.S. government holds a significant equity interest in Intel.

NVIDIA, by contrast, is the dominant AI accelerator maker and competes most directly with AMD's Instinct line. Tan has targeted AMD in server processors too, saying Intel's next-generation product "will be ahead of AMD."

AMD's Q4 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3% offers bulls evidence that demand for its Instinct and EPYC chips remains strong. Speaking at the company's November 3 earnings release, CEO Lisa Su declared, "We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year." Hunterbrook's own statement that its findings don't establish an export-law violation gives AMD supporters another argument.

The bears counter that even unresolved questions about blacklisted buyers can invite scrutiny from regulators and customers, and AMD stock already carries high expectations after its run this year. The same AI data-center expansion driving EPYC and Instinct demand also runs through the power, cooling, and networking suppliers we profiled in a free report on seven AI infrastructure names that aren't chipmakers. AMD's next test is whether the company publicly addresses Hunterbrook's findings on IEIT Systems. A cautious approach could make sense for traders considering AMD stock until the export-compliance question around the company resolves.

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此次事件暴露了芯片厂商在下游硬件生态管理中的合规真空，即固件更新作为一种非实物交付，极易避开传统的进出口海关监管。长期来看，监管层将迫使厂商建立更细粒度的芯片全生命周期数字化管理体系，凡是支持禁运设备运行的软件分发渠道都将面临被强制切断的合规风险。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This incident highlights a compliance vacuum in chipmakers' downstream ecosystem management, where firmware updates—as non-physical deliverables—bypass traditional customs checkpoints. Moving forward, regulators will likely mandate granular, full-lifecycle digital management for chips, placing any software distribution channels that sustain blacklisted hardware under immediate threat of enforcement.

卖空者的出口管制指控使早期的芯片反弹变成了 Advanced Micro Devices（纳斯达克股票代码：AMD）的急剧逆转。截至美国东部时间周四上午 11:00，AMD 股价为 487.80 美元，较周三收盘价下跌 8%。 AMD 股价随该芯片组其他公司一起上涨，此次下跌抹去了早期 3% 的涨幅。

Hunterbrook 表示做空 AMD。该公司报告称，2025 年 3 月被美国列入黑名单的中国服务器制造商 IEIT Systems 在被列入黑名单后不断发布包含较新 AMD 固件的基本输入/输出系统 (BIOS) 更新。该公司表示，AMD 没有回答其问题，其调查结果并未证实存在违反出口法的情况。截至撰写本文时，AMD 尚未公开回应该报道。

在 Hunterbrook 于 11 月 19 日发布调查结果之前，中国获取美国人工智能和服务器芯片的问题已经成为市场最热门的话题。据彭博社报道，美国总统特朗普暗示美国未来可能允许 NVIDIA（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）Blackwell 芯片向中国销售。 NVIDIA 2027 财年第 4 季度的指引已假定没有来自中国的数据中心计算收入。

尽管 AMD 股价波动较大，英特尔 (NASDAQ:INTC) 股价仍上涨 5%，至 57.38 美元。该公司为其先进的 18A 芯片工艺签署了第一个外部客户的消息，这一消息仍在提振股价。英特尔作为竞争对手 x86 服务器处理器制造商的地位增加了背景，而 Hunterbrook 的指控给 AMD 带来了压力。

NVIDIA 股价为 153.40 美元，上涨 1.6%，因此尽管今天 AMD 股价大幅波动，但 NVIDIA 股价仍保持稳定。从年初至今 (YTD) 衡量，NVDA 股价已下跌 18%。

title: Amazon warns NYC customers they face price hikes up to $5 for every order if delivery bill is passed
title_en: Amazon warns NYC customers they face price hikes up to $5 for every order if delivery bill is passed
