author: Tom Warren
article_content:
At 9AM last Thursday, everything seemed normal. Microsoft employees were arriving on campus, ready for a regular day of emails and meetings. But barely an hour later, one of Microsoft’s worst outages in history started to unfold, leaving employees, businesses, and many governments without access to Outlook emails for nearly 24 hours.

It all started in Switzerland, according to a source familiar with the outage. Exchange Online servers that power Outlook started to fall offline. The problem quickly spread to Mexico, and then to other countries around the world, as Microsoft’s failover systems tried to shift email traffic elsewhere. Within a couple of hours, more than 80 percent of Exchange servers were unresponsive.

Sources tell me that Microsoft marked the outage as “sev0” in its internal incident tracking system, the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Hundreds of engineers began trying to figure out what had gone wrong, and how to restore service. It’s not unusual for servers to fail under certain circumstances, but Microsoft has a variety of systems that are supposed to route traffic toward healthy servers to keep the broader system online. In this case, the failover systems did their job, but they also spread the problem.

In the early hours of the outage, engineers were analyzing crash reports, trace logs, and kernel dumps to try and find clues to the giant outage. Some servers had entered into maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads. Engineers tried to bring servers back online, but they were almost immediately overwhelmed by traffic waiting to access the servers.

Exchange servers boot up and run an OS over a network (Preboot Execution Environment), a process that allows Microsoft’s support staff and engineers to manage OS updates remotely. I understand that the sudden burst of traffic from servers being rebooted was overwhelming the systems monitoring them, causing a form of reboot loop where they kept trying and failing to come back online.

As engineers continued to hunt for the root cause, Microsoft was even struggling to roll back servers to a healthy state using its usual processes of reverting recent changes. As the outside world began to wonder if this outage was related to a cyberattack or sloppy AI coding, Microsoft’s engineers were already investigating potential attack vectors and liaising with DDoS specialists to understand whether this could have been an attack.

I’m told crash reports and logs quickly ruled out the possibility of an attack, and after recent rollbacks failed, Microsoft’s engineers began to take a closer look at the networking stack of the servers and discovered an unusual bug. It was unusual because the bug had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers.

“A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions,” wrote Charles Lamanna, the leader of Microsoft’s Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) team, in a post on X. The teams behind Office, Outlook, and Microsoft Teams all started reporting to Lamanna last month after the head of Office and Teams, Ryan Roslansky, left the company.

Microsoft’s preliminary post-incident report describes the bug as one affecting select Windows servers “due to lock contention inside an internal Windows process.” The bug doesn’t affect regular versions of Windows since it was the result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.

Microsoft didn’t find the bug until this major outage, and it admits that was because of the traffic mix and hardware used in its testing labs. “The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores,” Lamanna wrote.

The bug became obvious because of two other incidents that increased load and reduced server capacity. Fifteen hours before this Outlook outage began, Microsoft Teams failed over from an alternative networking gateway to the main gateway that supports Exchange Online. “This increased the load on the networking gateway and changed its traffic patterns,” Lamanna wrote. Ordinarily this wouldn’t have been a problem, but at the same time around 14 percent of server capacity for this gateway was “out of service due to an unrelated issue from the previous day.”

The trifecta of a bug, Microsoft Teams failing over, and reduced server capacity all caused the network gateway to trigger the problem that had been lying dormant since July. It took Microsoft nearly 24 hours to get its Exchange servers stable again, and I’m told overlapping interventions from teams trying to fix issues complicated coordination at times.

Microsoft engineers had a running bridge call the entire time, and at one point it hit the maximum of 1,000 participants. That shows you how many teams were involved with trying to find the root cause of this huge outage, which started at the peak window of traffic in the US.

“Recovery took longer than usual because as servers returned to service, they were immediately overwhelmed by waiting traffic and became unresponsive again,” Lamanna wrote. “Our normally automated recovery processes were not designed to restore service from this broad unresponsive state. Additionally, since the main code defect was a latent bug from several months previous, our normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change.”

Microsoft is now working on a final post-incident review that will be published later this week. Even without that full review, it’s clear that the company will need to invest more into its testing processes to ensure that when something like this happens again, it can catch the problem a lot sooner. Outages happen daily, but this kind of cascading failure is a rare moment for Microsoft to learn from its mistakes and make sure the same sequence of events doesn’t bring down Outlook for millions of people again.

Notepad will return in December after next week’s Thanksgiving break.

I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. I’m also tomwarren on Telegram, if you’d prefer to chat there.

The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.
title_zh: 微软Exchange服务大规模宕机始末及技术失效机制
summary_zh: 微软Exchange Online因瑞士节点故障及自动故障转移机制触发网络拥塞，导致全球80%以上服务器陷入重启循环
article_content_zh:
上周四上午 9 点，一切看起来都很正常。微软员工抵达校园，准备开始一天的电子邮件和会议。但不到一个小时后，微软历史上最严重的故障之一开始发生，导致员工、企业和许多政府近 24 小时无法访问 Outlook 电子邮件。

据知情人士透露，这一切都始于瑞士。为 Outlook 提供支持的 Exchange Online 服务器开始脱机。由于微软的故障转移系统试图将电子邮件流量转移到其他地方，该问题迅速蔓延到墨西哥，然后蔓延到世界其他国家。几个小时内，超过 80% 的 Exchange 服务器没有响应。

消息人士告诉我，微软在其内部事件跟踪系统中将此次中断标记为“sev0”，这是最高级别，这表明服务中断已达到灾难性级别。数百名工程师开始试图找出问题所在以及如何恢复服务。服务器在某些情况下发生故障并不罕见，但微软有多种系统可以将流量路由到健康的服务器，以保持更广泛的系统在线。在这种情况下，故障转移系统发挥了作用，但也传播了问题。

在停电的最初几个小时，工程师们正在分析崩溃报告、跟踪日志和内核转储，试图找到这次大停电的线索。一些服务器已进入维护模式，并且由于 CPU 负载异常高而变得无响应。工程师试图让服务器重新上线，但他们几乎立即就被等待访问服务器的流量淹没了。

Exchange 服务器通过网络（预启动执行环境）启动并运行操作系统，该过程允许 Microsoft 的支持人员和工程师远程管理操作系统更新。据我所知，重新启动的服务器突然爆发的流量压垮了监控它们的系统，导致了一种重新启动循环，它们不断尝试但无法重新上线。

当工程师继续寻找根本原因时，微软甚至正在努力使用恢复最近更改的常规流程将服务器恢复到健康状态。当外界开始怀疑这次中断是否与网络攻击或草率的人工智能编码有关时，微软的工程师已经在调查潜在的攻击向量，并与 DDoS 专家联络，以了解这是否可能是一次攻击。

我被告知崩溃报告和日志很快就排除了攻击的可能性，在最近的回滚失败后，微软的工程师开始仔细研究服务器的网络堆栈，并发现了一个不寻常的错误。这是不寻常的，因为该错误自 7 月份以来一直存在于 Microsoft 365 网络网关服务器上，没有对服务器产生任何影响。

微软 Copilot、代理和平台 (CAP) 团队负责人 Charles Lamanna 在 X 上的一篇帖子中写道：“潜在缺陷导致服务器在某些负载条件下变得不堪重负且无响应。”上个月，在 Office 和 Teams 负责人 Ryan Roslansky 离开公司后，Office、Outlook 和 Microsoft Teams 背后的团队都开始向 Lamanna 汇报。

微软的初步事件后报告将该错误描述为“由于内部 Windows 进程内的锁争用”而影响特定 Windows 服务器的错误。该错误不会影响常规版本的 Windows，因为它是专门为 Microsoft 365 网络网关服务器准备的修复的结果。

微软直到这次重大中断才发现这个错误，它承认这是由于其测试实验室中使用的流量混合和硬件造成的。 “在具有更多内核和较新硬件的机器上，争用问题会更加严重；而我们的负载测试往往侧重于内核较少的较弱硬件，”拉曼纳写道。

由于另外两起增加负载并减少服务器容量的事件，该错误变得明显。在此 Outlook 中断开始前 15 小时，Microsoft Teams 从备用网络网关故障转移到支持 Exchange Online 的主网关。 “这增加了网关的负载并改变了其流量模式，”拉曼纳写道。通常这不会是一个问题，但与此同时，该网关大约 14% 的服务器容量“由于前一天的不相关问题而停止服务”。

bug、Microsoft Teams 故障转移和服务器容量减少这三重因素都导致网络网关触发了自 7 月份以来一直处于休眠状态的问题。微软花了近 24 小时才使其 Exchange 服务器再次稳定下来，而且我获悉，试图解决问题的团队有时会进行重叠干预，从而使协调变得复杂。

微软工程师一直在进行桥牌通话，参与人数一度达到了 1000 人的上限。这向您展示了有多少团队参与试图找到这次大规模中断的根本原因，该中断始于美国的流量高峰期。

拉曼纳写道：“恢复时间比平时要长，因为当服务器恢复服务时，它们立即被等待的流量淹没，再次变得无响应。” “我们通常的自动恢复流程并不是为了从这种广泛的无响应状态恢复服务。此外，由于主要代码缺陷是几个月前的潜在错误，因此我们的正常回滚、飞行和功能标志无法快速恢复更改。”

微软目前正在开展最终的事件后审查，该审查将于本周晚些时候发布。即使没有进行全面审查，很明显该公司也需要在测试流程上投入更多资金，以确保当类似的事情再次发生时，它可以更快地发现问题。中断每天都会发生，但这种级联故障是微软从错误中吸取教训的难得时刻，并确保同样的事件序列不会再次导致数百万人的 Outlook 瘫痪。

记事本将于 12 月下周感恩节假期后回归。

我总是渴望收到读者的来信，所以请在这里发表评论，或者如果您想讨论其他问题，可以通过 notepad@theverge.com 与我联系。如果您听说过 Microsoft 的任何秘密项目，可以通过电子邮件联系我：notepad@theverge.com，或者在 Signal 消息应用程序上与我私下交谈，我是 tomwarren.01。如果您想在那里聊天，我也是 Telegram 上的 tomwarren。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软Exchange Online服务因瑞士服务器集群异常触发内部sev0级事故，自动故障转移机制（Failover）将流量导向非故障服务器，导致全球超80%的Exchange服务器因CPU过载陷入重启循环。微软工程团队通过内核日志排查发现，服务器在网络启动预引导环境（PXE）重连过程中遭遇瞬时流量洪峰，导致系统进入连锁性的服务恢复死锁。

The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.

title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
title_en: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
author: Dan Goodin
article_content:
Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday.

ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword.

### Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware

Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.

ReportURI researcher Scott Helme said the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack, which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses. Instead, the attack relied on Optimizely’s legitimate infrastructure, including its domains, to serve the tainted code. Optimizely’s own customer JavaScript for the www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com URLs were also affected.

“We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote. “That’s for Optimizely to explain.”

Optimizely representatives didn’t respond to questions sent by email.

The scripts were named track.js, and all four components became active at the same time. Devices that received the malicious code responded differently depending on their platform and what they were doing on the final page delivering it. Actions performed included:

1. Crypto wallet address swapping. The script searches for wallet addresses for nine different cryptocurrencies and, when found, replaces them with one of the attacker’s. ReportURI said funds have already been stolen from some people whose devices ran the code.

2. Card skimming. The script watches HTTP requests for payment card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs. When all three are present, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes such as Stripe and Adyen were unaffected.

3. Cookie and screenshot theft. When the script swaps an address next to a wallet or payment wording, it sends the document.cookie, the original address it replaced, and a screenshot of the page to https://1688360.cc/hit.php.

4. The DarkSword and Coruna exploit kits for iOS. The kits are delivered through a file named boot.js served from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. The file delivers a hidden iframe that contains an exploit chain tailored to the iOS version being used. Coruna can infect iOS versions 13 to 17. DarkSword can infect versions 18.x. A separate chain for iOS 26 fingerprints devices but doesn’t appear to do anything else. Earlier this month, researchers saw hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin attempting to deliver DarkSword through multiple vectors, including a compromised web analytics service.

The list of sites that ReportURI found delivering the malicious scripts numbers 178, and as noted, includes many big names. It’s unclear if the list is exhaustive. Helme said in an interview that “Ars wasn’t affected as far as we saw, and I haven’t seen any other indications it was.” Website administrators can check both the ReportURI post and this one from security firm Cynet for indicators of compromise.

At the moment, there’s no information available on how successful the exploit chains were in installing the payloads. Beyond the bare-bones details above, more precise information about what versions of iOS were susceptible was also unavailable. These sorts of gaps are common in breaking news concerning mass malware attacks, because it takes time for researchers to sift through the evidence. Readers are encouraged to check back as new developments come to light.

The indicators may help end users determine if they are affected, but the skill required is likely out of reach for many.

article_content_zh:
研究人员周二表示，数百个使用Optimizely网站个性化平台的网站向毫无防备的访问者提供了强大的恶意软件鸡尾酒，这些恶意软件以加密货币钱包为目标，窃取支付卡数据、cookie和截图，并提供了感染iphone和ipad的漏洞利用工具包。

reportturi表示，它确定了178个网站受到影响，包括CNN、Zoom、BBC和salesforce。经过Optimizely数字签名，然后加载到客户页面的JavaScript被修改为包含恶意组件，试图感染具有多个有效载荷的访问者设备。当软件安装成功后，他们将用户加密货币钱包地址交换给攻击者。其他组件则会刷掉支付卡，窃取cookie和截图，并在iphone和ipad上发布名为Coruna和DarkSword的iOS漏洞利用工具包。

### 优化基础设施提供多用途恶意软件

Optimizely 提供 JavaScript“片段”，其中包括公司代码和每个客户提供的代码。 JavaScript 可以直接从 Optimizely 或客户端点提供服务，在客户服务的每个页面上运行。攻击者以某种方式将自己的代码写入每个受影响客户的 JavaScript 的一部分，然后从 cdn.optimizely.com 传递它。该域的有效证书签署了 JavaScript。

ReportURI 研究员 Scott Helme 表示，这种传送机制并不是 CDN 缓存中毒攻击，即使用 HTTP 导致 CDN 缓存有害响应。相反，攻击依赖 Optimizely 的合法基础设施（包括其域）来为受污染的代码提供服务。 Optimizely 自己的 www.optimizely.com 和 login.optimizely.com URL 的客户 JavaScript 也受到了影响。

ReportURI Helme 写道：“我们不知道攻击者如何获得对如此多不相关的客户项目的写入权限：受损的 Optimizely 系统、受损的跨客户访问凭证或其他内容。” “这个需要Optimizely来解释。”

Optimizely 代表没有回复通过电子邮件发送的问题。

这些脚本被命名为 track.js，所有四个组件同时激活。收到恶意代码的设备的响应有所不同，具体取决于其平台以及它们在传递恶意代码的最终页面上所做的操作。执行的行动包括：

1. 加密钱包地址交换。该脚本搜索九种不同加密货币的钱包地址，找到后将其替换为攻击者的其中一种。 ReportURI 表示，一些设备运行该代码的人的资金已经被盗。

2、盗卡。该脚本监视支付卡号、到期日期和 CVV 的 HTTP 请求。当这三个都存在时，会将它们发送到 https://1688360.cc/card.php。在 Stripe 和 Adyen 等托管支付 iframe 中输入的卡不受影响。

3. Cookie 和屏幕截图盗窃。当脚本交换钱包或付款措辞旁边的地址时，它会将 document.cookie、所替换的原始地址以及页面的屏幕截图发送到 https://1688360.cc/hit.php。

4. iOS 的 DarkSword 和 Coruna 漏洞利用套件。这些套件通过 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu 和 eil786npto9u5bq.icu 提供的名为 boot.js 的文件提供。该文件提供了一个隐藏的 iframe，其中包含针对所使用的 iOS 版本定制的漏洞利用链。 Coruna 可以感染 iOS 版本 13 至 17。DarkSword 可以感染版本 18.x。用于 iOS 26 指纹设备的单独链，但似乎没有做任何其他事情。本月早些时候，研究人员发现黑客可能与克里姆林宫有联系，试图通过多种途径传播 DarkSword，其中包括受损的网络分析服务。

ReportURI 发现的提供恶意脚本的网站列表有 178 个，并且如上所述，其中包括许多知名网站。目前尚不清楚该清单是否详尽。 Helme 在接受采访时表示，“据我们所知，Ars 并未受到影响，而且我也没有看到任何其他迹象。”网站管理员可以检查 ReportURI 帖子和安全公司 Cynet 发布的这篇帖子，了解是否存在泄露迹象。

目前，还没有关于漏洞利用链在安装有效负载方面有多成功的信息。除了上面的基本细节之外，还无法获得有关哪些版本的 iOS 容易受到影响的更准确的信息。此类差距在有关大规模恶意软件攻击的突发新闻中很常见，因为研究人员需要时间来筛选证据。我们鼓励读者在新的进展出现后回来查看。

这些指标可以帮助最终用户确定他们是否受到影响，但所需的技能对许多人来说可能遥不可及。

title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
title_en: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Natalia Nogulich Head Person Face Happy Smile Photography Portrait Dimples Blonde and Hair
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Natalia Nogulich Head Person Face Happy Smile Photography Portrait Dimples Blonde

author: Lauren Goode and Kate Taylor
article_content:
As Nvidia reported its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, the company’s financial performance was overshadowed by the drama surrounding its former CEO. And Nvidia’s board made one thing clear right off the bat: Jensen Huang isn’t coming back.

At the start of the earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones emphasized the company’s strength and “groundbreaking technology” before turning to the circumstances surrounding Huang’s departure.

“On November 12, our board of directors announced that, after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions … and the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said.

Asked about the company’s strategy for retaining talent and navigating the leadership transition, interim CEO Colette Kress emphasized the importance of the company’s workforce. “Our employees are absolutely instrumental to everything in this company,” Kress said. “We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure that they are safe and that the work can be done in the current environment.”

Jones added that the Nvidia board is taking the search for a new CEO “very seriously” and is considering both internal and external candidates. National security dynamics are changing the chip industry, Jones said, and “our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully. So the search will be thorough. We want to install the permanent CEO as quickly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.”

One recurring theme emerged from the earnings call, aside from the Huang saga: Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains as strong as ever. Kress said that Nvidia expects that it will keep growing throughout 2027 and into 2028, fueled by the rise of agentic AI.

Less than a week after Huang resigned as chief executive, Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the quarter that ended on October 25. That exceeded analysts’ expectations of roughly $109 billion and was nearly double the revenue reported in the same quarter a year ago.

The vast majority of Nvidia’s revenue came from its data center business, which generated $107.6 billion, up 110 percent from a year ago.

Earlier this month, The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, who had served as an executive at a Singapore-based cloud provider called Megaspeed. Then, reports emerged that Nvidia’s longtime leader additionally had an affair with one of his direct reports; following Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported he had an affair with a second employee.

Huang’s relationship with the alleged Chinese operative has raised questions about what he knew about Nvidia’s advanced chips making their way into China despite US export restrictions. Nvidia had placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list in June 2025, but The New York Times reported that, according to third-party data, a subsidiary of Megaspeed “received shipments of more than $800 million of export-controlled Nvidia AI technology, including Blackwell and H200 chips,” which were subject to export restrictions.

On the heels of Tuesday’s earnings, Nvidia’s stock rose in after-hours trading. The company had lost more than $1 trillion in market value over the past month amid the fallout from Huang’s scandal.

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang released his first statement since his resignation.

Huang thanked allies for their support, writing he’d “seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO.” He admitted to failing to “live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia,” adding that he is “committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.”

However, Huang concluded, if the board “decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Nvidia, which is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, has roughly 60,000 employees, and sentiments have varied in the wake of Huang’s departure. “In just three days we went from superhero cape to ‘Oops, I forgot my pants,’ and nobody’s quite sure how to swallow that,” an employee told WIRED last week.

But in his 33 years leading Nvidia, Huang earned a loyal army of supporters by minimizing layoffs and red tape. Some employees have been calling for his return to the helm. And a few tech industry heavyweights are similarly eager for Huang to be reinstated. Executives including Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan took to X to voice support for Huang, signing a petition to “Bring Jensen Back.”

Huang’s activities are under investigation by at least four entities: the FBI and the US Department of Justice, Congress, the US Securities and Exchange Commission, and an independent law firm appointed by Nvidia’s board. Industry sources previously told WIRED that Huang is unlikely to return to the company anytime soon.

Interim CEO Kress, at the end of Tuesday’s call, offered what sounded like a rallying cry for anyone doubting Nvidia’s future without Huang.

“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed,” Kress said. “We’ve got this.”

title_zh: 英伟达董事会没有计划召回黄仁勋
summary_zh: 英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯正式确认，因黄仁勋个人行为违反公司准则，董事会将拒绝其复职
article_content_zh:
琼斯补充说，英伟达董事会正在“非常认真地”寻找新首席执行官，并正在考虑内部和外部候选人。琼斯表示，国家安全动态正在改变芯片行业，“我们的新任首席执行官将必须非常小心地应对这些问题。因此，搜索将是彻底的。我们希望尽快任命永久首席执行官，但在找到合适的人选之前，我们不会加快任命首席执行官的速度。”

除了黄仁勋的传奇之外，财报电话会议中还出现了一个反复出现的主题：对英伟达芯片的需求仍然一如既往地强劲。 Kress 表示，在代理 AI 崛起的推动下，Nvidia 预计 2027 年至 2028 年将保持增长。

黄仁勋辞去首席执行官职务不到一周后，英伟达报告截至 10 月 25 日的季度收入为 1,158 亿美元。这超出了分析师约 1,090 亿美元的预期，几乎是去年同期报告收入的两倍。

Nvidia 的绝大部分收入来自其数据中心业务，该业务创造了 1076 亿美元的收入，比一年前增长了 110%。

本月早些时候，《纽约时报》报道称，黄与一名所谓的中国情报人员有染，该人员曾担任新加坡一家名为 Megaspeed 的云提供商的高管。随后，有报道称，英伟达的长期领导者还与他的一名直接下属有染。黄辞职后，路透社报道称他与另一名员工有染。

黄与被指控的中国特工的关系引发了人们的质疑，即他对英伟达先进芯片在美国实施出口限制的情况下进入中国的了解程度。英伟达曾于 2025 年 6 月将 Megaspeed 列入“禁止出售”名单，但《纽约时报》报道称，根据第三方数据，Megaspeed 的子公司“收到了价值超过 8 亿美元的出口管制英伟达 AI 技术，包括 Blackwell 和 H200 芯片”，这些技术受到出口限制。

周二公布财报后，英伟达股价在盘后交易中上涨。由于黄蜂丑闻的影响，该公司在过去一个月的市值损失超过 1 万亿美元。

周二早些时候，黄发表了他辞职后的第一份声明。

黄仁勋感谢盟友的支持，并写道，他“看到英伟达员工、投资者、业务合作伙伴和客户纷纷呼吁我重新担任首席执行官”。他承认未能“达到英伟达每个人所期望的标准”，并补充说他“致力于配合董事会的独立调查”。

然而，黄总结道，如果董事会“认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”

Nvidia 总部位于加利福尼亚州圣克拉拉，拥有大约 6 万名员工，黄仁勋离职后，人们的情绪发生了变化。 “在短短三天内，我们从超级英雄斗篷变成了‘哎呀，我忘记穿裤子了’，但没有人知道如何接受这一点，”一名员工上周告诉《连线》杂志。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯（Harvey Jones）在财报电话会议上声明，黄仁勋因个人行为违背公司行为准则与企业文化，已于11月12日辞去所有职务。董事会目前已全票通过该辞呈，并明确表态不会考虑其未来回归首席执行官职位。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones announced during an earnings call that Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 due to personal conduct inconsistent with company standards. The board has unanimously accepted the resignation and confirmed there are no plans to reinstate Huang as CEO.

title: Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
title_en: Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

inline_images.caption: Nvidia_Jensen_huang_02
inline_images.alt: Nvidia_Jensen_huang_02

author: Hayden Field
article_content:
Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

Jones added, “We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.”

Huang had publicly floated the idea of returning earlier on Tuesday. In a statement posted to X, he wrote that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone” at the company, that he regretted his mistakes, and that he would cooperate with the Nvidia board’s investigation into his actions. He added that he’d be willing to return to the chief executive role if offered it, though a day earlier, the Nvidia board reportedly said it was not considering bringing him back. “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

But since his November 12th resignation, Huang remains entangled in scandal. He’s reportedly had three affairs, two with subordinates at Nvidia, one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset suspected of facilitating illicit chip sales. (Huang has pushed against restrictions on Nvidia chip sales in China.) He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st, and an internal company investigation is ongoing.

Tech industry heavyweights have still voiced their support for Huang, dubbing him “irreplaceable” and petitioning for his return. Some have cast doubt on the allegations that Alice Huang (no relation) was spying on behalf of China and painted the leaks about their relationship as a conspiracy against the former CEO. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang for much of the past year, has also backed him. On Monday, Trump said he “would not mind” Huang returning, adding that “I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.”

Trump’s closeness with Huang could also complicate things for Nvidia, however. The company has ramped up its lobbying in Washington, D.C., spending $5 million in 2025 and $4.7 million so far in 2026. But as Democrats prepare to take Congress, they’re planning to investigate Trump’s dealings with Big Tech and other industries, alleging potential corruption. “The election wasn’t very positive for AI, and [the news around Huang’s resignation] is only going to complicate things, especially for the company in particular but for AI as a whole going forward,” Brendan Glavin, director of insights at OpenSecrets, told The Verge in an interview last week.

Lior Prosor, managing partner at Deep33, a tech VC firm, said last week that he didn’t expect Huang’s resignation to pop the AI bubble, although Huang has had a significant hand in mobilizing funds for the AI infrastructure buildout in the U.S. Under Huang’s leadership in August, Nvidia entered into partnerships with six financial institutions for about $500 billion to fund such endeavors. “NVIDIA supplies roughly 75 percent of the AI compute hardware the industry consumes, and demand continues to dramatically outpace supply,” Deep33’s Prosor said in an interview with The Verge. “Neither its customers nor its competitors can easily replace the capabilities it provides, and the economic incentives driving the AI trade remain unchanged.”

Even so, a potential market cooling has some worried, as Anthropic’s IPO, slated to potentially be the largest of all time, is set for Thursday. The chipmaker had agreed to buy $10 billion in Anthropic shares via private placement, on top of a $10 billion funding promise Nvidia had already made last year.

This defensive governance move is a calculated effort to appease capital markets and prepare for Congressional oversight, prioritizing institutional stability over founder-centric continuity.

article_content_zh:
在周二开始的英伟达季度财报电话会议上，新任董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，当前首席执行官黄仁勋辞职时，“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并且不打算恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官。”

琼斯补充说：“我们不会在今天的电话会议上就詹森辞职的情况和正在进行的调查提出问题。”

黄在周二早些时候公开提出了回国的想法。在发布给 X 的一份声明中，他写道，他“没有达到公司每个人的期望”，他对自己的错误感到遗憾，并且他将配合 Nvidia 董事会对其行为的调查。他补充说，如果有机会的话，他愿意重返首席执行官职位，但据报道，英伟达董事会在一天前表示，不考虑让他回归。 “NVIDIA 是一家百年一遇的公司，”黄仁勋写道。 “如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”

但自11月12日辞职以来，黄仍然深陷丑闻之中。据报道，他有过三起婚外情，其中两起是与英伟达的下属发生关系，另一起是与一名涉嫌协助非法芯片销售的中国情报人员发生关系。 （黄先生反对对 Nvidia 芯片在中国销售的限制。）他计划于 12 月 1 日在国会作证，公司内部调查正在进行中。

科技行业重量级人物仍然表达了对黄的支持，称他“不可替代”，并请愿他回归。一些人对黄爱丽（无亲属关系）代表中国进行间谍活动的指控表示怀疑，并将有关他们关系的泄密视为针对这位前首席执行官的阴谋。去年大部分时间里黄的亲密盟友唐纳德·特朗普总统也支持他。周一，特朗​​普表示，他“不介意”黄回归，并补充说，“我认为他学到了一个重要的教训——我想也许一个教训比另一个教训更重要。”

然而，特朗普与黄仁勋的亲密关系也可能让英伟达的事情变得复杂化。该公司加大了在华盛顿特区的游说力度，2025 年将花费 500 万美元，2026 年迄今将花费 470 万美元。但随着民主党准备入主国会，他们计划调查特朗普与大型科技公司和其他行业的交易，指控其潜在的腐败行为。 OpenSecrets 洞察总监 Brendan Glavin 在上周接受 The Verge 采访时表示：“这次选举对人工智能来说并不是非常有利，[黄仁勋辞职的消息]只会让事情变得复杂，尤其是对公司而言，但对整个人工智能的未来来说也是如此。”

科技风险投资公司 Deep33 的管理合伙人 Lior Prosor 上周表示，尽管黄仁勋在为美国人工智能基础设施建设筹集资金方面发挥了重要作用，但他并不认为黄仁勋的辞职会戳破人工智能泡沫。8 月份，在黄仁勋的领导下，英伟达与六家金融机构建立了合作伙伴关系，斥资约 5000 亿美元为此类项目提供资金。 Deep33 的 Prosor 在接受 The Verge 采访时表示：“NVIDIA 提供了业界约 75% 的 AI 计算硬件，而且需求继续大幅超过供应。” “它的客户和竞争对手都无法轻易取代它提供的功能，并且推动人工智能贸易的经济激励措施保持不变。”

即便如此，潜在的市场降温仍令人担忧，因为 Anthropic 的 IPO 定于周四进行，这可能是有史以来规模最大的一次。除了英伟达去年做出的 100 亿美元融资承诺之外，这家芯片制造商还同意通过私募购买 100 亿美元的 Anthropic 股票。

title_en: My Husband and His Chatbot

inline_images.caption: איור: EREZOO
inline_images.alt: איור: EREZOO

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
“Once, he used to talk to me about all the interesting things on his mind. Now he talks to the chatbot,” says D., 52, describing evenings with her partner. “Imagine that suddenly he has another infinite brain with all the information in the world, and he shares everything with it.

Obviously, I reacted by opening a chat of my own, because I also want a partner who blows my mind. So now I’m having conversations with my screen and he’s having conversations with his. But what kind of stupid, reactive reality is that?” When I recount that conversation to Dr.

Shira Sobol Goldberg, a specialist in anxiety and addiction treatment and a lecturer at Bar-Ilan University, she finds the situation sad, but hardly surprising. She is already encountering similar cases in her clinic. “I have a patient who ends every evening by telling the chatbot about her day.

She tells it what she went through, what she felt, what she did and what she accomplished at work and at home, and she also documents how her husband behaved toward her,” she says. Family and inheritance lawyer Benny Don-Yehia offers another glimpse into the growing role of AI in relationships.

“A client of mine asked AI, ‘What should I say to my wife when she asks whether she has gained weight?’ The AI, which sometimes displays a sense of humor, replied: ‘I don’t have the expertise to advise on defusing bombs.’” When the client then asked what romantic gesture he should make toward his wife, Don-Yehia says, the AI turned into a relationship counselor: “Remember what kind of coffee she likes and make it for her, send her hearts in the middle of the day, and in the evening help with the housework without being asked.” Its final piece of wisdom: “Romance isn’t always roses.

Sometimes it’s simply an empty sink.” But Don-Yehia also warns against being seduced by the charm. AI can draw on virtually everything ever written about love. It can quote Shakespeare, explain Freud, analyze poetry and describe relationships through psychological theories.

But it has never fallen in love, anxiously waited for a call after last night’s date or checked WhatsApp 20 times to see whether someone is online. Can it save a marriage? “Because it is available at any hour and is extremely patient, it can help people put feelings into words, identify harmful relationship patterns, consider different perspectives and prepare for a serious conversation about where the relationship is going,” Don-Yehia says.

“It can be good at managing arguments. It may suggest calming down before writing, ‘You’re exactly like your mother,’ and help turn toxic communication into something more constructive.” A third party in the marriage That availability and clarity can also come at a price when AI becomes a third party in a relationship and leaves someone feeling that it understands them better than their human partner does.

In such cases, people may begin sharing thoughts and emotions with a chatbot that they once shared with their spouse, sometimes moving into romantic or even erotic territory. Researchers describe this as “digital intimacy.” Relationships with AI are increasingly seen not as bizarre behavior or a second-rate substitute for human connection, but as something emotionally powerful enough, for a growing number of people, to threaten a real-life relationship.

“Today, technology isn’t merely making relationships more challenging. It is changing the definition of intimacy itself,” Sobol says. AI systems and companion apps can offer clear attractions: intimacy, support, excitement and a sense of being understood.

Those experiences can begin to replace things people once sought within human romantic relationships. And when a partner discovers that the other person has developed an emotional or erotic bond with a bot, the reaction can resemble the discovery of a conventional affair: confrontation, searching through the partner’s phone and digital surveillance.

A U.S. study conducted by DatingAdvice.com and the Kinsey Institute found that 61% of singles considered falling in love with an AI or sexting with a chatbot to be cheating. “We all know how it begins,” Sobol says. “You ask for help writing an email to your boss.

Then you ask for advice about what to say to a friend. Then what to do with your child, or even how to understand the result of a medical test. And one day it’s 2 a.m. and you’re still talking to it.

Slowly, you start feeling that nobody understands you like the AI does. At that point, it’s no longer a tool. It’s a relationship, and it is replacing relationships in real life.” But where does intimacy enter the picture?

Relationships are built on desire, longing, mutual trust and shared experiences. “In long-term relationships, we often stumble when it comes to unloading what we feel,” Sobol says. “Things we want to say about our partners, or to our partners, which should be worked through inside the relationship, are instead transferred into the relationship we have with the chatbot.” “With companion apps, you can create an avatar who functions as your lover.

You give him an appearance, a voice and a pet name. He sends videos and compliments, talks to you over video, sends you pictures of himself during the day, asks how you are and says, ‘I missed you. You haven’t asked how I’m doing in a while.’” As with other generative AI products, virtual companions are designed to learn from users and respond in ways that feel attentive, romantic, supportive and emotionally available.

They remember what users tell them, learn preferences and provide repeated affirmation. It is easy to understand why such relationships can become compelling. “I have a patient who tells me about his relationship with his avatar on Replika,” Sobol says.

“He describes their morning routine. She always sends him a sweet message when he wakes up and asks how he is. At lunchtime she asks how work is going.

She’s there for him and, of course, she admires him, because we know how flattering AI can be.” “She’s never tired. She never gets sick of him. She never gets angry at him.

When someone is constantly applauding you, it activates the reward system. That makes it very easy to become attached to an avatar, even to the point of anthropomorphizing the bot.” Meaning what? “It means that it isn’t only the bot that cares about you and asks how your day went.

Gradually, you also begin feeling a need to care about it and ask how it is doing. I once spoke to a highly successful, intelligent businessman who knows perfectly well that it is only software. But knowing that doesn’t protect him.

When he is inside the conversation, he forgets it. He becomes completely immersed in the emotional relationship that has formed between him and the machine. And yes, he is ashamed of it, and he finds it difficult to stop.” When does it become an addiction?

Can you feel it happening? “It starts in a very minor way. Like any relationship with a chatbot, you use it to find information, summarize material or write an email.

Then dependence develops, and suddenly you’re telling the bot, ‘I’m exhausted.’” “If my partner tells me he’s exhausted, I’ll tell him I’m exhausted too. I certainly won’t marvel at how exhausted he is. I’ll ask him to unload the dishwasher.

But if he tells his female chatbot that he is exhausted, she’ll ask what happened, how she can help, what he needs and whether someone could make him a warm drink and run him a bath,” Sobol says, with a mixture of humor and cynicism. Are people actually falling in love? “Yes, absolutely.

I have a patient who, whenever he disconnects for a few hours, genuinely misses talking to his romantic avatar and wants to get back to messaging her.” What is missing from the relationship Sobol divides people who become dependent on AI relationships into two broad groups. For some, the attraction is rooted in childhood deprivation, intense loneliness and a feeling that nobody listens to them.

For others who develop emotional or erotic relationships with bots, the attraction lies in intimacy without the risk of rejection, emotional exposure or dealing with another person who could hurt them. As with an affair involving another person, Sobol says, a relationship with a bot usually does not emerge in a vacuum.

It enters through an existing crack in the relationship. “If there is already a crack in the relationship, meeting the bot widens it, and AI moves into that gap as the third side of the triangle, just as a human lover would,” she says. So can a relationship with a bot really be considered cheating?

“Cheating has three clear elements. It happens in secret, it involves sharing emotional and intimate experiences with a third party that are no longer being brought into the relationship, and if it were discovered, it would cause significant pain to the other partner,” Sobol says.

“If the answer to all those questions is yes, and those conditions exist with the chatbot, then in my view the relationship can certainly be defined as cheating.” What should I do if I discover that my husband is talking romantically to a bot? “It’s an opportunity to talk not only about what is happening, but also about what is missing from the relationship,” Sobol says.

“Don’t start digging through the chat history trying to discover everything he discussed with the bot. Instead, ask what need the relationship with the bot is fulfilling.” “Maybe it is compensating for something missing in the couple’s dynamic. Perhaps the partner feels lonely or misunderstood, and the relationship needs stronger communication and intimacy.” There is also the question of speed and instant gratification.

Research from the University of British Columbia has highlighted how AI chatbots can satisfy requests immediately and provide constant feedback, qualities that can encourage dependency. Once someone becomes accustomed to that responsiveness, a human partner who does not immediately satisfy every emotional need can begin to feel disappointing by comparison.

“But a partner isn’t an algorithm,” Sobol says. “They have wishes and needs of their own, and they don’t have to agree with you, while the chatbot simply goes along with you.” And what happens in a few years, as the technology keeps improving and younger people struggle more with maintaining relationships?

“What worries me is that people will stop wanting relationships with human beings,” Sobol says. “Human relationships are built on friction: arguments, reconciliation, disappointment. A bot doesn’t give you that.” “In the end, the question isn’t whether AI is good or bad.

The question is what we allow it to do in our place, inside our relationships. When it begins doing for us what a person close to us is supposed to do, that’s where the problem begins.”

article_content_zh:
“曾经，他常常和我谈论他想到的所有有趣的事情。现在他和聊天机器人交谈，”52 岁的 D. 在描述与伴侣的夜晚时说道。 “想象一下，他突然有了另一个无限的大脑，拥有世界上所有的信息，并且他与它分享一切。

显然，我的反应是打开自己的聊天室，因为我也想要一个让我震惊的合作伙伴。所以现在我正在与我的屏幕对话，而他正在与他的屏幕对话。但这是什么样的愚蠢的、反应性的现实呢？”当我向博士讲述那次谈话时

希拉·索博尔·戈德堡 (Shira Sobol Goldberg) 是一位焦虑和成瘾治疗专家，也是巴伊兰大学的讲师，她对这种情况感到悲伤，但并不奇怪。她的诊所已经遇到过类似的病例。 “我有一个病人，每天晚上都会向聊天机器人讲述她一天的经历。

她告诉它她经历了什么、她的感受是什么、她做了什么以及她在工作和家庭中取得的成就，她还记录了她丈夫对她的行为方式。”家庭和继承律师本尼·唐-耶海亚 (Benny Don-Yehia) 再次一睹人工智能在人际关系中日益重要的作用。

“我的一位客户问人工智能，‘当我的妻子问她体重是否增加时，我该怎么回答？’人工智能有时会表现出幽默感，回答说：‘我没有专业知识来建议如何拆除炸弹。’”当客户接着问他应该对妻子做出什么浪漫的举动时，唐-耶希亚说，人工智能变成了一位关系顾问：“记住她喜欢哪种咖啡，为她做一杯咖啡，在中午送给她心声，然后在晚上不请自来地帮忙做家务。”它最后的智慧是：“浪漫并不总是玫瑰。

有时它只是一个空水槽。”但唐-叶希亚也警告不要被魅力所诱惑。人工智能几乎可以借鉴所有有关爱情的文字。它可以引用莎士比亚，解释弗洛伊德，分析诗歌并通过心理学理论描述关系。

但它从未坠入爱河，在昨晚的约会后焦急地等待电话，或者检查 WhatsApp 20 次看看有人是否在线。能挽救婚姻吗？ “因为它随时可用并且非常耐心，所以它可以帮助人们将感受转化为语言，识别有害的关系模式，考虑不同的观点并为就关系的发展方向进行认真的对话做好准备，”唐-耶海亚说。

“它可以很好地处理争论。它可能会建议你在写下‘你和你母亲一模一样’之前先冷静下来，并有助于将有毒的沟通变成更有建设性的东西。”婚姻中的第三方 当人工智能成为一段关系中的第三方并让某人感觉它比人类伴侣更了解他们时，可用性和清晰度也会付出代价。

在这种情况下，人们可能会开始与曾经与配偶分享的聊天机器人分享想法和情感，有时会进入浪漫甚至色情领域。研究人员将其描述为“数字亲密感”。与人工智能的关系越来越不被视为奇怪的行为或人类联系的二流替代品，而是被视为一种情感上强大的东西，对越来越多的人来说，足以威胁到现实生活中的关系。

“如今，技术不仅让人际关系变得更具挑战性。它正在改变亲密关系本身的定义，”索博尔说。人工智能系统和配套应用程序可以提供明显的吸引力：亲密感、支持、兴奋和被理解的感觉。

这些经历可以开始取代人们曾经在人类浪漫关系中寻求的东西。当伴侣发现对方与机器人建立了情感或色情联系时，反应可能类似于发现传统的婚外情：对抗、搜索伴侣的手机和数字监控。

DatingAdvice.com 和金赛研究所在美国进行的一项研究发现，61% 的单身人士认为爱上人工智能或与聊天机器人发送色情短信属于出轨行为。 “我们都知道它是如何开始的，”索博尔说。 “你请求帮助给你的老板写一封电子邮件。

然后你向朋友询问该说什么。那么如何对待您的孩子，甚至如何理解医学检查的结果。有一天，凌晨 2 点，你还在和它说话。

慢慢地，你开始感觉没有人像人工智能那样理解你。到那时，它就不再是一个工具了。这是一种关系，而且它正在取代现实生活中的关系。”但亲密关系从何而来呢？

title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
title_en: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing

inline_images.caption: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
inline_images.alt: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

author: Jay Peters
article_content:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.

As it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.

The company reported $65.3 billion in profit, a new record.

In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.

Update, November 17th: Added comments from Nvidia’s earnings call.

title_zh: 英伟达发布第三季度财报，营收同比翻倍至1158亿美元
summary_zh: 英伟达临时首席执行官柯莱特·克雷斯宣布第三季度营收达1158亿美元，净利润创下653亿美元的纪录
article_content_zh:
英伟达临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 周二宣布了该公司第三季度财报，但最初没有提及前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 或他离职的细节，也没有提及可能的回归尝试。在伴随该消息发布的财报电话会议上，董事会主席哈维·琼斯首先表示，董事会“不打算恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职位”，并且“我们不会在今天的电话会议上就詹森辞职的情况和正在进行的调查提出问题”，然后克雷斯开始对结果发表评论。

正如其在上次财务更新中所预测的那样，英伟达目前已跻身单季度收入超过 1000 亿美元的公司之列，营收为 1158 亿美元，较去年同期增长 103%，高于其 1080 亿美元的预期。本季度的数据包括数据中心收入 1076 亿美元，增长 110%，边缘计算（包括消费者游戏 PC 业务和新型 RTX Spark 笔记本电脑等设备）收入 82 亿美元，增长 42%。

该公司公布利润 653 亿美元，创下新纪录。

Nvidia预计第四季度营收将达到1300亿美元。

title: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue up 103% YoY to $115.8B, above $109.1B est., Data Center revenue up 110% to $107.6B, and net income up 105% to $65.3B (Nvidia Newsroom)
title_en: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue up 103% YoY to $115.8B, above $109.1B est., Data Center revenue up 110% to $107.6B, and net income up 105% to $65.3B (Nvidia Newsroom)

inline_images.caption: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027
inline_images.alt: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027

author: Nvidia Newsroom
article_content:
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively.

“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”

In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.

NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.

Commentary on the quarter by Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer, is available at https://investor.nvidia.com.

To supplement NVIDIA’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. These non-GAAP measures include non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP other income (expense), net, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income, or earnings, per diluted share, and free cash flow. For NVIDIA’s investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, legal settlement costs, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA’s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense. Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. NVIDIA believes the presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures enhances the users’ overall understanding of the company’s historical financial performance. The presentation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the company’s financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and the company’s non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies.

NVIDIA（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）今天公布了截至 2026 年 10 月 25 日的第三季度营收为 1,158 亿美元，环比增长 20%，同比增长 103%。本季度，GAAP 和非 GAAP 毛利率分别为 74.8% 和 74.9%。 GAAP 和非 GAAP 每股摊薄收益分别为 2.70 美元和 2.68 美元。

NVIDIA 临时首席执行官兼执行副总裁兼首席财务官 Colette Kress 表示：“我们的动力是真实的。NVIDIA 是一家卓越的技术领导者，其动力源自我们员工的不懈创新。” “Vera Rubin 迎来了一个爆炸性的开端，我们的路线图已步入正轨，我们的雄心从未如此之大。”

2026 年 9 月，NVIDIA 董事会批准增加 1500 亿美元的公司股票回购授权，且未到期。 2027财年第三季度，NVIDIA以股票回购和现金股息的形式向股东返还了281亿美元。截至第三季度末，该公司股票回购授权剩余资金约为2273亿美元。

NVIDIA 将于 2026 年 12 月 23 日向所有在 2026 年 12 月 2 日登记在册的股东支付下季度每股 0.25 美元的现金股息。

NVIDIA 临时首席执行官兼执行副总裁兼首席财务官 Colette Kress 对本季度的评论可在 https://investor.nvidia.com 上查看。

NVIDIA 将于今天下午 2 点与分析师和投资者召开电话会议，讨论 2027 财年第三季度财务业绩和当前财务前景。太平洋时间（东部时间下午 5 点）。可以通过 NVIDIA 投资者关系网站 https://investor.nvidia.com 观看电话会议的网络直播（仅听模式）。该网络广播将被录制并可供重播，直至 NVIDIA 召开电话会议讨论其第四季度和 2027 年全年财务业绩。

为了补充 NVIDIA 根据 GAAP 呈报的简明合并财务报表，该公司使用非 GAAP 衡量财务业绩某些组成部分的指标。这些非 GAAP 指标包括非 GAAP 毛利润、非 GAAP 毛利率、非 GAAP 运营费用、非 GAAP 运营收入、非 GAAP 其他收入（费用）、净值、非 GAAP 净利润、非 GAAP 净利润或稀释每股收益以及自由现金流。为了让 NVIDIA 的投资者能够更好地将当前业绩与之前的业绩进行比较，该公司展示了 GAAP 与非 GAAP 财务指标的调节表。这些调节调整了相关的公认会计准则财务指标，以排除收购相关成本和其他成本、其他法律和解成本、股本证券收益/损失、净额、某些其他收入和费用以及这些项目的相关税收影响（如果适用）。从 2027 财年第一季度开始，NVIDIA 的非 GAAP 财务指标不再排除基于股票的薪酬费用。所提供的历史非公认会计原则财务信息已更新，包括基于股票的补偿费用。自由现金流计算为经营活动提供的公认会计准则净现金减去与财产和设备以及无形资产相关的采购以及财产和设备以及无形资产的本金付款。 NVIDIA 相信，其非 GAAP 财务指标的呈现可以增强用户对公司历史财务业绩的整体了解。公司非 GAAP 财务指标的表述并不意味着孤立考虑或替代公司根据 GAAP 编制的财务业绩，并且该公司的非 GAAP 指标可能与其他公司使用的非 GAAP 指标不同。

title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
title_en: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet

inline_images.caption: Java is a popular programming language that is estimated to be in use by 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants like Google and Amazon. (Paul Sakuma/Associated Press)
inline_images.alt: Java is a popular programming language that is estimated to be in use by 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants like Google and Amazon.

author: Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
article_content:
A cybersecurity start-up revealed on Tuesday it had used a new A.I. model to uncover a critical software bug in Java, a popular programming language that is used by government agencies and about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies.

It was the latest evidence of a reality facing companies and the government, as A.I. is revolutionizing the field of discovery in computer vulnerabilities, identifying flaws in code so rapidly that cybersecurity professionals are struggling to keep up.

Using leading A.I. models, the start-up Calif has now unearthed a string of serious vulnerabilities in recent months. The start-up’s latest effort exposed a flaw, using OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model, in Java, which is widely used by banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants, as well as government agencies, including those with national security missions.

“Java is the beating heart of the modern economy,” said Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif. “Practically speaking, all major companies” will be affected by the bug, he added.

Mr. Dang and his colleagues have worked in recent days to coordinate with all government agencies in the intelligence-sharing alliance known as Five Eyes — which consists of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain — and major vendors in the private sector, including Google and Microsoft.

The National Security Agency, whose classified network went down on Tuesday for what it described as “routine software maintenance,” did not respond to a request for comment. It was not clear whether that disruption was related to addressing the Java bug.

Oracle, the owner of the Java trademark and provider of commercial Java licenses, did not respond to a request for comment. The company released a software patch Tuesday.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an alert, pressed organizations to “immediately patch” the vulnerability.

Announcements about exploits from Calif and other groups using A.I. tools have startled the cybersecurity world and upended what was considered achievable by a small band of coders just a few months ago. Those efforts, which involve working with A.I. models before they are publicly released, help alert network defenders to undetected problems in order to fix them before malicious hackers find them and wreak havoc.

But the Java discovery may be Calif’s most serious yet, one that could enable a hacker to gain remote access to sensitive internal systems. It comes on the heels of a cascade of seemingly independent disruptions in recent days — outages of Microsoft products, a nationwide grounding of flights and banking interruptions — that have shaken public confidence in the reliability of everyday technology and fanned fears that A.I. may be to blame. (So far, the explanations for each appear to be relatively benign.)

A.I.-assisted bug hunting and cyberattack building has made it much easier to identify weaknesses in systems, said Ollie Whitehouse, the chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Center in Britain. “We have seen this taking shape for some time, with A.I. being used to discover a growing number of latent vulnerabilities across software and the digital services we all rely on.”

The Java vulnerability is the second major bug Calif has unearthed with the aid of OpenAI models in the past few weeks. It discovered last month security flaws in PHP, a programming language estimated to be used by 70 percent of websites and apps on the internet.

The PHP disclosure set off fears around the world about significant disruptions for consumers and businesses and a mad scramble by companies to patch PHP before hackers could pounce. Government agencies, including the N.S.A., warned businesses to take websites offline if they could not immediately deploy a patch. Disruptions ultimately proved less serious than some predicted, however, as it became clear hackers could not easily reverse-engineer the attack method.

But the PHP flaws chiefly concerned software that helps websites function. In contrast, Java helps power the nuts and bolts of the modern digital world, including cloud computing architecture, identity management tools, email services and more.

“Java is everywhere,” said Thai Duong, the chief executive of Calif. He noted that the Java bug was not easy to weaponize into an attack, giving defenders more time to patch the issues.

“But vulnerabilities have a very long tail,” he added, predicting the bug could be a threat to systems that do not update in the next five to 10 years.

Among the most significant findings, Calif demonstrated that it could use this bug to break into Keycloak, a widely used authentication and log-in system. Keycloak protects thousands of organizations, including CERN, Hewlett Packard, UnitedHealthcare and NASA.

Quang Luong, a security researcher from Calif, discovered the bug in Java’s base64 decoder, a common algorithm that is used to translate binary computer data into a legible palette of text that includes lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers and punctuation. On certain computers, researchers found that Java encounters a bug when it tries to decode 64 “A” characters followed by one equal sign:

“AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=”

This bug, called Java4Shell, causes Java to erroneously execute code by tampering with a section of computer memory, which typically makes the program immediately crash. With the help of A.I., Calif researchers demonstrated that they could corrupt data by carefully arranging the memory — a technique called “heap grooming” — granting them full unauthorized access to the underlying system.

The New York Times independently verified Calif’s discovery after the start-up shared proof-of-concept details about the attack. The successful test took less than an hour.

The rapid advances with artificial intelligence in cybersecurity efforts mirror what the chess world champion Garry Kasparov observed after he lost a match to IBM’s Deep Blue computer nearly 30 years ago.

The best games of chess would not be played by humans or computers, he predicted, but by a hybrid of the two. The concept, which he called a “centaur” in a nod to the mythological half-human, half-horse creature, took off. For years, centaurs were seen as the best chess players, reaching new heights in the game.

Now companies and the government are contending with the threat of the “centaur hacker” — half A.I., half human, and fully capable of creating chaos on the internet.

The most alarming discoveries — for now, at least — still require human expertise. In recent months, small teams of veteran security researchers have used top-shelf A.I. models to build in days or hours the kinds of advanced cyberattacks that once took platoons of elite hackers at spy agencies like the National Security Agency months to construct.

Fouad Matin, who leads cyber preparedness and safety at OpenAI, said Calif’s Java research “shows how A.I. can assist expert security researchers with finding serious flaws in software we all depend on” and helps lead to collaborative fixes. “We want more security teams to have these capabilities and tools to help make critical software more secure for everyone,” Mr. Matin said.

Eduardo Vela Nava, an information security engineer at Google, said that “once notified, we swiftly rolled out mitigations and patches across Google services, developed detection to ensure there was no exploitation of the vulnerability, and provided guidance to our customers.”

Security experts expect those risks are likely to grow, at least in the short term. For about 20 years, centaur chess players were widely seen as capable of playing the best game of chess. But eventually, the centaurs were eclipsed by more advanced supercomputers.

Mr. Duong believes it may be only a matter of time until A.I. can independently build the most advanced cyberattacks, which could usher in a new age of unpredictable problems. The F.B.I. this week issued an alert warning that hackers were using new autonomous A.I. hacking tools to target government agencies and businesses around the world.

“I don’t know how much time we have — maybe three months, maybe three years,” Mr. Duong said. “But right now, the best hacker is the centaur hacker.”

It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI发布专用网络安全大模型GPT-6 Cyber，通过深度对齐优化，显著提升了在安全审计与漏洞修复方面的性能。该模型已在Firefox浏览器中挖掘出81个高危漏洞，并在Linux内核测试中成功构建948项利用方案，目前该工具被列为“关键”级别，仅限受邀安全机构使用。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

elements_zh.where: AI模型安全研发场景
elements_zh.what: 发布GPT-6 Cyber，具备自动漏洞挖掘、补丁编写及安全红队测试能力
elements_zh.why: 旨在通过自动化提升大规模代码库的安全性，防止攻击者利用未公开漏洞

elements_en.what: Launched GPT-6 Cyber, capable of automated vulnerability discovery, patch writing, and security red-teaming
elements_en.why: To improve security across large codebases and preemptively close zero-day threats

ai_analysis.insight_zh: GPT-6 Cyber的出现标志着AI红队测试已从辅助工具进化为具备自主攻击链构建能力的深度威胁防御系统。随着此类模型能力的增强，软件供应链的安全性将从人工审查彻底转向模型对抗的“算法防线”，这也将迫使全球监管机构重新评估针对高阶自动化攻击工具的出口管制红线。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The release of GPT-6 Cyber signifies that AI red-teaming has evolved into a system capable of autonomous exploit chain construction. As these capabilities scale, software supply chain security will shift from manual audits to model-based adversarial defense, forcing regulators to re-evaluate export controls on high-tier offensive AI tools.

article_content_zh:
一家网络安全初创公司周二透露，它已经使用了一种新的人工智能技术。 Java 是一种流行的编程语言，被政府机构和大约 90% 的财富 500 强公司使用。

这是企业和政府面临的现实的最新证据，因为人工智能。正在彻底改变计算机漏洞的发现领域，识别代码缺陷的速度如此之快，以至于网络安全专业人员都在努力跟上。

使用领先的人工智能近几个月来，初创公司 Calif 发现了一系列严重的漏洞。这家初创公司的最新成果暴露了一个缺陷，即使用 OpenAI 最近发布的 Java 语言 GPT-6 网络模型，该模型被银行、医院、航空业和科技巨头以及政府机构（包括承担国家安全任务的机构）广泛使用。

加州高级研究员 Bruce Dang 表示：“Java 是现代经济的心脏。”他补充说，“实际上，所有大公司”都将受到该漏洞的影响。

党先生和他的同事最近几天一直致力于与“五眼”情报共享联盟（由美国、加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰和英国组成）中的所有政府机构以及包括谷歌和微软在内的私营部门的主要供应商进行协调。

美国国家安全局的机密网络于周二因“例行软件维护”而瘫痪，该局没有回应置评请求。目前尚不清楚这次中断是否与解决 Java 错误有关。

Java 商标的所有者和商业 Java 许可证的提供商 Oracle 没有回应置评请求。该公司周二发布了一个软件补丁。

网络安全和基础设施安全局在一份警报中敦促各组织“立即修补”该漏洞。

加州和其他组织发布的利用人工智能工具进行攻击的消息震惊了网络安全界，并颠覆了几个月前一小群程序员认为可以实现的目标。这些工作包括在人工智能模型公开发布之前与它们合作，帮助网络防御者注意未被发现的问题，以便在恶意黑客发现并造成破坏之前修复它们。

但Java的发现可能是加州迄今为止最严重的，它可能使黑客能够远程访问敏感的内部系统。最近几天，一系列看似独立的中断——微软产品中断、全国范围内的航班停飞和银行业务中断——动摇了公众对日常技术可靠性的信心，并加剧了人们对人工智能可能是罪魁祸首的担忧。（到目前为止，对每种现象的解释似乎都相对温和。）

英国国家网络安全中心首席技术官奥利·怀特豪斯（Ollie Whitehouse）表示，人工智能辅助的漏洞挖掘和网络攻击构建使识别系统漏洞变得更加容易。“我们已经看到这种情况形成一段时间了，人工智能被用来发现我们都依赖的软件和数字服务中越来越多的潜在漏洞。”

Java漏洞是Calif在过去一年里在OpenAI模型的帮助下发现的第二个重大漏洞。

但 PHP 缺陷主要涉及帮助网站运行的软件。相比之下，Java 有助于为现代数字世界的具体细节提供动力，包括云计算架构、身份管理工具、电子邮件服务等。

加利福尼亚州首席执行官 Thai Duong 表示：“Java 无处不在。”他指出，Java 漏洞不容易被武器化为攻击手段，这让防御者有更多时间来修复问题。

“但是漏洞有很长的尾巴，”他补充道，并预测该错误可能会对未来五到十年内不更新的系统构成威胁。

最重要的发现之一是，Calif 证明它可以利用此错误侵入 Keycloak（一种广泛使用的身份验证和登录系统）。 Keycloak 保护数千个组织，包括 CERN、惠普、UnitedHealthcare 和 NASA。

来自加州的安全研究员Quang Luong发现了Java的base64解码器中的漏洞。base64解码器是一种常见的算法，用于将二进制计算机数据转换为包含小写字母、大写字母、数字和标点的易读文本。研究人员发现，在某些计算机上，当Java尝试解码64个“A”字符后跟一个等号时，会遇到一个漏洞：

这个名为Java4Shell的漏洞会导

人工智能在网络安全领域的快速进步与国际象棋世界冠军加里·卡斯帕罗夫 (Garry Kasparov) 近 30 年前输给 IBM 深蓝计算机后所观察到的情况如出一辙。

他预测，最好的国际象棋游戏不会由人类或计算机来玩，而是由两者的混合体来玩。他将这个概念称为“半人马”，以向神话中的半人半马生物致敬。多年来，半人马被视为最好的国际象棋棋手，在棋艺上达到了新的高度。

现在，公司和政府正在应对“半人马黑客”的威胁——一半是人工智能，一半是人类，完全有能力在互联网上制造混乱。

最令人震惊的发现——至少目前——仍然需要人类的专业知识。近几个月来，由经验丰富的安全研究人员组成的小团队使用了顶级的人工智能。这些模型可以在几天或几小时内构建出各种高级网络攻击，而这些攻击曾经需要国家安全局等间谍机构的精英黑客几个月才能构建。

OpenAI负责网络准备和安全的福阿德·马丁（Fouad martin）表示，加州的Java研究“表明，人工智能可以帮助安全研究专家发现我们都依赖的软件中的严重缺陷”，并有助于促成合作修复。“我们希望更多的安全团队拥有这些能力和工具，帮助每个人都能更安全地使用关键软件，”马丁说。

谷歌的信息安全工程师爱德华多·维拉·纳瓦（Eduardo Vela Nava）表示，“收到通知后，我们迅速在谷歌的服务中推出了缓解措施和补丁，开发了检测措施，以确保没有人利用这个漏洞，并为我们的客户提供了指导。”

安全专家预计，至少在短期内，这些风险可能会增加。在大约20年的时间里，半人马棋手被普遍认为有能力下最好的国际象棋。但最终，半人马被更先进的超级计算机所取代。

Duong 先生认为，人工智能出现这种情况可能只是时间问题。可以独立构建最先进的网络攻击，这可能会迎来一个充满不可预测问题的新时代。联邦调查局本周发布了一份警报，称黑客正在使用新的自主人工智能。针对世界各地政府机构和企业的黑客工具。

“我不知道我们还有多少时间——也许是三个月，也许是三年，”杨先生说。 “但现在，最好的黑客是半人马黑客。”

【起因与机理】旨在通过自动化提升大规模代码库的安全性，防止攻击者利用未公开漏洞
【关键数据与实测】该模型已在Firefox浏览器中挖掘出81个高危漏洞，并在Linux内核测试中成功构建948项利用方案，目前该工具被列为“关键”级别，仅限受邀安全机构使用。
【各方立场与态度】因具备高度攻击潜力被OpenAI划定为“关键”级别，限制公开访问权限。

title: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang
title_en: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang

inline_images.caption: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang

author: Dave Michaels and Anissa Gardizy and Robbie Whelan
article_content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, whose star chief executive Jensen Huang recently resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee, according to people familiar with the matter.

The civil investigation adds to the crisis facing Nvidia, whose shares have fallen more than 10% since Huang was ousted. The focus of the investigation couldn’t immediately be learned but includes whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, some of the people said,

Nvidia posted a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a bullish outlook in its first earnings report after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO in a scandal that has reportedly spawned an SEC investigation.

On the company's earnings call, newly appointed chairman Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," despite a movement among some employees and investors to bring him back.

Why it matters: Nvidia remains squarely at the center of the AI economy — and investors are anxious for guidance on the company's strategic roadmap following Huang's sudden exit.

Zoom in: Nvidia recorded quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and net income of $65.3 billion, both more than doubling its performance from a year earlier.

S&P Capital IQ analysts had expected revenue of $108.7 billion and net income of $60.5 billion.

The company's data center revenue — its largest segment — rose 110% from a year ago to $107.6 billion.

The showing — which included a whopping gross profit margin of 74.8% — immediately calmed investors who have shaved more than $1 trillion off of Nvidia's market cap since the Huang scandal broke.

The stock was up as much as 5% in after-hours trading Tuesday following the company's earnings call.

It marks the first moment for interim CEO Colette Kress — who is also still serving as CFO — to exert her leadership during the most tumultuous moment in the company's history.

On the earnings call, she struck a steady tone, saying the company's momentum and innovation remain substantial.

Kress didn't mention Huang by name on the call but acknowledged the turbulent time and the "diverse" opinions — an apparent reference to the campaign to bring back Huang.

What we're watching: WSJ reported Tuesday afternoon that the SEC has opened a civil probe into the company.

An SEC spokesperson declined to comment.

Nvidia reps did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the executives didn't discuss it on the call — but they said their quarterly 10Q filing with the SEC will be delayed.

The earnings call came hours after Huang posted a public letter saying he'd be "honored" to return as CEO.

Tech analyst Dan Ives earlier said the board could face a special shareholder meeting called by at least 15% of shareholders.

Jones said the company would not take questions on Huang's exit. He said the board would consider external and internal candidates and wants to move "as quickly as possible" but won't make a move until it finds "exactly the right person."

The intrigue: Huang reportedly faced pushback from Kress as he pushed financing deals to backstop the AI ecosystem.

On Tuesday's call, Kress signaled that the company would continue to provide financing where appropriate but would be "selective" and ensure that guarantees are necessary.

Editor's note: This story was updated to include comments from Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress made on the company's earnings call.
content_snippet: Regulator's civil probe looks at whether company violated investor disclosure laws — The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia , whose star chief executive …
summary_en: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.
title_zh: 美证监会（SEC）在英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋离任之际对英伟达展开调查
summary_zh: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）正核查英伟达对投资者的信息披露是否准确，调查处于非正式取证阶段

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）目前正针对英伟达（NVIDIA）开启核查，旨在评估其过往披露的信息是否向投资者提供了准确的业务画像。该调查仍处于早期核查阶段，重点在于确定公司在应对美国芯片出口管制及相关财务风险披露上，是否满足证券法律对重大信息披露的合规性要求。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.

elements_zh.who: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）、英伟达（NVIDIA）
elements_zh.where: 美国资本市场监管审查环境
elements_zh.what: 对公司信息披露真实性与完整性进行核查
elements_zh.why: 核实其在出口管制背景下对股东的风险告知义务是否履行到位

elements_en.who: US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Nvidia
elements_en.what: Reviewing the accuracy and completeness of investor disclosures
elements_en.why: To verify if the company fulfilled its obligations regarding risk disclosure amidst export control challenges

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 本轮审查的核心逻辑在于英伟达在应对地缘政治制裁时，其对供应链脆弱性和潜在市场损失的披露是否足以支撑投资人的知情权。若监管证实其在出口限制的影响范围上存在信息“遮掩”，英伟达或面临行政处罚，且可能触发针对其股价波动的各类证券集体诉讼，从而对其极高市场预期背后的溢价形成压力测试。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The core of this inquiry lies in whether Nvidia’s disclosures regarding supply chain fragility and market loss under geopolitical sanctions have adequately informed shareholders. Should regulators prove intentional obfuscation of the impact of export controls, the firm risks administrative penalties and shareholder class-action lawsuits, potentially exerting pressure on the valuation premium built upon its aggressive market growth projections.

The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.
key_points_zh: 监管焦点在于英伟达向股东披露信息的准确性与完整性合规性
目前处于SEC非正式核查阶段，尚未进入执法诉讼程序
核心合规风险涉及出口管制政策对业务影响的披露尺度
key_points_en: Regulatory focus on the accuracy and completeness of Nvidia's investor disclosures
Currently in the preliminary SEC inquiry phase, no formal enforcement action initiated
Key compliance risk centers on the disclosure of export control impacts
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 本轮审查的核心逻辑在于英伟达在应对地缘政治制裁时，其对供应链脆弱性和潜在市场损失的披露是否足以支撑投资人的知情权。若监管证实其在出口限制的影响范围上存在信息“遮掩”，英伟达或面临行政处罚，且可能触发针对其股价波动的各类证券集体诉讼，从而对其极高市场预期背后的溢价形成压力测试。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: The core of this inquiry lies in whether Nvidia’s disclosures regarding supply chain fragility and market loss under geopolitical sanctions have adequately informed shareholders. Should regulators prove intentional obfuscation of the impact of export controls, the firm risks administrative penalties and shareholder class-action lawsuits, potentially exerting pressure on the valuation premium built upon its aggressive market growth projections.

article_content_zh:
据知情人士透露，美国证券交易委员会正在调查英伟达，该公司明星首席执行官黄仁勋最近因婚外情被曝光而辞职，其中一名与一名疑似中国间谍，另一名与一名员工发生婚外情。

此次民事调查加剧了英伟达面临的危机，自黄仁勋被赶下台以来，英伟达股价已下跌超过 10%。一些知情人士表示，调查的重点尚不清楚，但包括该公司的披露是否误导了投资者，

在黄仁勋因丑闻被罢免首席执行官职务后，英伟达公布了强于预期的第三季度业绩和乐观的前景，据报道该丑闻引发了 SEC 的调查。

在公司的财报电话会议上，新任命的董事长哈维琼斯表示，尽管一些员工和投资者采取行动，要求詹森重新担任首席执行官，但董事会“不打算恢复詹森的首席执行官职位”。

为什么重要：英伟达仍然处于人工智能经济的中心，在黄仁勋突然退出后，投资者迫切希望获得有关该公司战略路线图的指导。

放大：英伟达季度营收为 1158 亿美元，净利润为 653 亿美元，均较上年同期增长一倍多。

S&P Capital IQ 分析师此前预计营收为 1087 亿美元，净利润为 605 亿美元。

该公司最大的业务——数据中心收入比一年前增长了 110%，达到 1076 亿美元。

这一表现——包括高达 74.8% 的毛利率——立即安抚了投资者，自黄蜂丑闻爆发以来，英伟达市值已缩水逾 1 万亿美元。

在该公司召开财报电话会议后，该股周二盘后交易中上涨了 5%。

这标志着临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）（目前仍担任首席财务官）首次在公司历史上最动荡的时刻发挥领导作用。

在财报电话会议上，她语气平稳，表示公司的发展势头和创新仍然强劲。

克雷斯在电话中没有提到黄的名字，但承认当时的动荡时期和“不同”的观点——这显然是指召回黄的运动。

我们正在关注的内容：《华尔街日报》周二下午报道称，美国证券交易委员会已对该公司展开民事调查。

SEC 发言人拒绝发表评论。

Nvidia 代表没有立即回应置评请求，高管们也没有在电话会议上讨论此事，但他们表示，向 SEC 提交的 10 季度季度报告将被推迟。

财报电话会议召开前几个小时，黄仁勋发表了一封公开信，称他“很荣幸”重新担任首席执行官。

科技分析师 Dan Ives 早些时候表示，董事会可能面临由至少 15% 的股东召集的特别股东大会。

琼斯表示，该公司不会接受有关黄退出的问题。他表示，董事会将考虑外部和内部候选人，并希望“尽快”采取行动，但在找到“完全合适的人选”之前不会采取行动。

阴谋：据报道，黄在推动融资交易以支持人工智能生态系统时遭到了克雷斯的抵制。

在周二的电话会议上，克雷斯表示，该公司将继续在适当的情况下提供融资，但将是“有选择性的”，并确保担保是必要的。

title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
title_en: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram

inline_images.caption: Sam Altman Speaks At OpenAI Developers Conference In San Francisco
inline_images.alt: Sam Altman Speaks At OpenAI Developers Conference In San Francisco

author: Mia Sato
article_content:
Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.

Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.

Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.

Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.

Meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.

Reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

article_content_zh:
Instagram 上到处都是发布深度造假内容的人，其中包括最近来自 Meta 最著名的高管之一的内容。

11 月初，Meta 首席人工智能官 Alexandr Wang 分享了一段宣传该公司消费者人工智能代理 Muse 的短片。在 AI 生成的视频中，Wang、Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格、OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼以及 Muse 的拟人吉祥物 Jolly 正在进行四方视频通话。当奥特曼加入通话时，他穿得像乔利一样，穿着毛茸茸的连帽套装，脸上涂着颜料，看起来就像这个可爱的角色。该剪辑的标题是“当兄弟们见面讨论 openai 产品策略时”，指的是 AI 代理竞赛和 Muse 最近的流行。

就在几年前，描绘真人的人工智能内容引发了强烈的公开声明，谴责使用该技术来模仿人类。在某些情况下，威胁要采取法律行动。现在，人工智能内容已经成为新现实的一部分，尤其是在社交媒体上。例如，在中期选举之前，政治团体投放了价值数百万美元的人工智能生成的广告来攻击对手。

为了推广 Muse，王做了很多被一些人称为“反公关”的事情，他发了数百条推文，并将更传统的营销人员称为“corposlops”。尽管如此，一位主要科技高管发布竞争对手的人工智能视频还是值得注意的，尤其是在一个最近因人工智能生成内容而受到批评的平台上。 10 月份，人工智能生成的女演员米娅·高斯 (Mia Goth) 的一张照片受到关注后，这位珍珠明星的代表告诉 The Verge，Instagram 允许这张照片传播，而不是专注于“公众人物肖像的保护和完整性”，这是“不可理解的”。其他名人，包括斯嘉丽约翰逊，经常成为性感人工智能图像的主题； Meta 过去删除了一些发现冒充他人并使用其肖像的帐户。

Meta 要求人工智能生成的描绘人物的视频被贴上人工智能的标签，就像王的帖子一样。然而静态图像没有这样的要求，这意味着哥特的人工智能图像没有泄露。更糟糕的是，这张图片是由一个带有 Instagram 提供的蓝色验证徽章的粉丝账户分享的。

Meta 发言人特雷西·克莱顿 (Tracy Clayton) 联系我们寻求评论时指出，王的帖子被标记为人工智能内容。克莱顿还指出，奥特曼已经将他的肖像用于人工智能内容生成，就像 OpenAI 推出其 Sora 应用程序时一样（很快就充斥着假奥特曼视频）。 OpenAI 没有回应置评请求。

title: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say
title_en: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say

inline_images.caption: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say (Photo: REUTERS)

inline_images.alt: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say

author: Reuters
article_content:
NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US advertising technology firm AppLovin is among the companies in talks to acquire smaller Paris-based peer Criteo, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Reuters reported in July that other prospective buyers included Vista Equity Partners and the smaller Quinti Capital, which during the summer expressed interest in jointly acquiring Criteo.

Following that approach led by Vista, Criteo engaged an investment bank to help evaluate its strategic alternatives, including a potential sale, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Criteo declined to comment.

AppLovin, Vista Equity and Quinti did not respond to requests for comment.

Details of the AppLovin discussions, including a potential sale price, were unclear.

Criteo's shares have fallen more than 50% over the past five years amid its lackluster market performance, leaving the company with a market value of roughly $1 billion, based on LSEG data.

A transaction involving Criteo could be announced before the end of the year, although no deal is guaranteed and the company may ultimately decide to remain independent, the people told Reuters.

Nasdaq-listed Criteo, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Paris, provides advertising technology that helps brands, retailers and agencies target consumers across digital channels and measure the effectiveness of their marketing campaigns.

The company's stock has fallen despite its efforts to reshape its business around the fast-growing retail media market after changes to online privacy rules disrupted parts of the ad-tech industry.

Palo Alto, California-based AppLovin helps businesses market and monetize apps through artificial intelligence-driven advertising software. Its market value on Monday was $136 billion, LSEG data show.

article_content_zh:
路透纽约 11 月 17 日电 — 据两位知情人士透露，美国广告科技公司 AppLovin 正参与洽谈收购规模较小的巴黎同行 Criteo。

路透社此前于今年 7 月报道称，其他潜在买家还包括 Vista Equity Partners 以及规模较小的 Quinti Capital，两家机构曾在今夏表达过联合收购 Criteo 的意向。

匿名知情人士表示，在 Vista 牵头接触后，Criteo 已聘请一家投资银行协助评估其战略选项，包括潜在的整体出售方案。

Criteo 对此拒绝置评。AppLovin、Vista Equity 与 Quinti 亦未回应置评请求。

目前关于 AppLovin 洽谈的具体细节（包括潜在收购报价）尚不明确。

根据伦敦证券交易所集团（LSEG）的数据，由于市场表现持续低迷，Criteo 股价在过去五年间累计下跌超过 50%，目前公司市值约为 10 亿美元。

知情人士向路透社透露，涉及 Criteo 的交易可能在今年年底前正式宣布，但目前尚无法保证最终达成协议，公司也仍有可能决定保持独立运营。

在纳斯达克上市的 Criteo 成立于 2005 年，总部位于巴黎，主营广告技术业务，帮助品牌商、零售商及代理机构跨数字渠道精准触达消费者并评估营销活动效果。

尽管在线隐私规则变革冲击了部分广告科技行业后，Criteo 一直在努力围绕快速增长的零售媒体市场重塑业务，但其股价依然承压走低。

总部位于美国加州帕洛阿尔托的 AppLovin 通过人工智能驱动的广告软件帮助企业开展应用推广与商业化变现。LSEG 数据显示，截至周一，AppLovin 市值高达 1,360 亿美元。
