title: An interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman, who says he is in "full management mode", as he focuses on corporate customers and tools for cybersecurity (Jemima McEvoy/The Information)
title_en: An interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman, who says he is in "full management mode", as he focuses on corporate customers and tools for cybersecurity (Jemima McEvoy/The Information)
author: The Information
article_content:
President Claudia Sheinbaum met on Wednesday with Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI, the San Francisco-based company that created ChatGPT.

“At the National Palace, we welcomed OpenAI’s president and co-founder Greg Brockman and his team,” Sheinbaum wrote on social media.

En Palacio Nacional, recibimos al presidente y cofundador de OpenAI, Greg Brockman, y a su equipo; conversamos sobre las diversas aplicaciones de la inteligencia artificial, particularmente en el sector Salud.

Coincidimos en que esta tecnología puede generar beneficios en atención médica.

“We discussed the various applications of artificial intelligence, particularly in the healthcare sector. We agreed that this technology can bring benefits to healthcare,” she wrote.

Sheinbaum’s meeting with Brockman came a few weeks after the federal government announced the establishment of an Advisory Council for the Digital Transformation of the Health Sector, which is aimed at improving the control, storage and distribution of medications.

Members of the council will use digital tools and artificial intelligence (AI) to detect medication shortages — a long-running problem in Mexico — track warehouse inventory and expedite delivery to public hospitals and health centers.

There was no indication from Sheinbaum that OpenAI is going to collaborate withe the council in any way.

However, it is clear that the federal government is seeking to use AI as a means to improve healthcare in Mexico.

At her Thursday morning press conference, Sheinbaum told reporters that her government is interested in collaborating with China on “different issues,” one of which is “smart hospitals.”

“We’re very interested in the smart hospitals they have in China,” she said ahead of her trip to Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders’ Meeting.

“… [We want to] implement this model in our country,” Sheinbaum said.

A smart hospital is a healthcare facility that uses a range of technology, including AI, to automate certain tasks and improve patient care.

The president is not the only Mexican official to have met with an OpenAI executive. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard met OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in the United States in early September. Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia on Thursday, and Tom Brown, co-founder of the AI company Anthropic, also met Ebrard at a G20 meeting in North Carolina.

According to the Economy Ministry, Ebrard said at the time that “Mexico must develop its capabilities in AI, given that the impact AI will have on the economy is as disruptive as the impact the advent of electricity once had on manufacturing.”

article_content_zh:
周三，总裁 Claudia Sheinbaum 会见了 OpenAI 的总裁兼联合创始人格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman)，OpenAI 是一家总部位于旧金山的公司，ChatGPT 的创建者。

“在故宫，我们迎来了 OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人 Greg Brockman 和他的团队，”Sheinbaum 在社交媒体上写道。

国家宫 (Palacio Nacional) 主席兼 OpenAI 联合创始人 Greg Brockman 是您的设备；与人工智能、特殊领域健康领域的多种应用相关。

“我们讨论了人工智能的各种应用，特别是在医疗保健领域。我们一致认为这项技术可以给医疗保健带来好处，”她写道。

希恩鲍姆与布罗克曼的会面是在联邦政府宣布成立卫生部门数字化转型咨询委员会几周后进行的，该委员会旨在改善药物的控制、储存和分配。

该委员会成员将使用数字工具和人工智能（AI）来检测药品短缺（墨西哥长期存在的问题），跟踪仓库库存并加快向公立医院和医疗中心的交付。

Sheinbaum 没有表示 OpenAI 将以任何方式与该委员会合作。

然而，很明显，联邦政府正在寻求利用人工智能来改善墨西哥的医疗保健。

在周四上午的新闻发布会上，谢因鲍姆告诉记者，她的政府有兴趣在“不同问题”上与中国合作，其中之一就是“智能医院”。

“我们对中国的智慧医院非常感兴趣，”她在前往深圳参加亚太经合组织领导人会议之前说道。

“……[我们希望]在我们国家实施这种模式，”谢因鲍姆说。

智能医院是一家医疗机构，它使用包括人工智能在内的一系列技术来自动执行某些任务并改善患者护理。

总统并不是唯一一位会见 OpenAI 高管的墨西哥官员。 9月初，经济部长Marcelo Ebrard在美国会见了OpenAI首席执行官Sam Altman。周四辞去芯片制造商英伟达首席执行官职务的黄仁勋和人工智能公司 Anthropic 联合创始人汤姆·布朗也在北卡罗来纳州举行的 G20 会议上会见了埃布拉德。

article_content:
### A new standard for professional work

We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. For businesses and developers, that means frontier performance at costs that make sense at scale.

GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new quality bar for AI in complex professional work. Its slides, spreadsheets, and documents read less like AI, and more closely follow the templates you provide and the conventions of your field. It writes cleaner code and builds frontends that look and work better, particularly for websites, gaming, and 3D design.

On Agents’ Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT‑6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.

We believe GPT-6.2 Astra is the best model in the world for scientists. It sets a new high on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which tests how well models can carry out scientific work in a terminal. GPT-6.2 Astra scores 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than one-third the cost. It also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index, which asks models to interpret real biological data and run experiments to infer how a simulated system works.

In the API, GPT‑6.2 Astra’s input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT‑6 Astra’s, with a 60% discount on cached input ($8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output, all per million tokens). GPT‑6.2 Sol keeps GPT‑6.1 Sol’s API token prices. On several benchmarks, both models come close to or outperform other leading models at a small fraction of the cost per task.

### GPT-6.2 Sol: our go-to model for everyday work

Compared with GPT‑6.1 Sol, GPT‑6.2 Sol is smarter, more efficient, and lets you complete more tasks on the same paid plan. It powers through multistep agentic workflows, writes clearly and naturally, and is intuitive to collaborate with. Many employees at OpenAI use it as their default model for both technical and non-technical tasks.

In Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0, GPT‑6.2 Sol comes within 0.5 points of GPT‑6.2 Astra at about one-fifth the cost (both at max).

Its speed and intelligence also make it ideal for the important tasks people turn to AI for outside of work. On our recently released LifeVal evaluation, which measures performance on challenging everyday tasks, GPT‑6.2 Sol outscores GPT‑6 Astra at about one-seventh the cost.

### Professional outputs that match industry standards

We trained GPT‑6.2 Astra to create clearer, better-designed slides, spreadsheets, and documents that more closely follow the conventions professionals use in fields like law, sales, finance, and accounting. The writing is more direct and specific, with fewer generic takeaways and less filler.

Harvey LAB‑AA v1.1 uses legal assignments to test whether models can find the relevant facts across source documents, apply them to a detailed brief, and produce an accurate deliverable that meets every requirement. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new state of the art, more than doubling Claude Fable 5.2’s pass rate at about one-sixth the cost. Astra for Law, our configuration of GPT-6.2 Astra for lawyers, scores even higher on this benchmark.

Our internal GDPval v2 benchmark is our next iteration of GDPval that measures complex, long-horizon workflows from real projects in sectors like consulting, finance, and design. GPT‑6.2 Astra leads the models we tested, up 6.2 percentage points from GPT‑6 Astra while using 22% fewer output tokens. GPT‑6.2 Sol improves 5.3 points from GPT‑6.1 Sol.

### Workbooks and memos

Building a valuation workbook or writing an investment memo starts with finding the relevant figures in source files and working out how they fit together. Artificial Analysis’s AA‑AnalystAgent tests that work on real spreadsheets and reports. In one task, models use California Medicaid’s expenditure reports to calculate how much the program spent on medical transport. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, answering 62.5% of questions correctly on all five independent attempts.

### Slideshows

GPT‑6.2 Astra is our best model yet at designing slides and following slide templates, whether given an original file or even a screenshot. It can match the layout, colors, and typography down to the exact font size, and carry the template’s writing style into new slides. Early testers found the decks easier to use directly with fewer edits, thanks to titles that state the main takeaway and concise body copy that focuses on the details readers need.

### Computer use and interactive web design

GPT‑6.2 Astra’s more precise computer use lets it work down to individual parts and connections in CAD and simulation tools. Engineers can use that additional detail to check how components fit, see where loads shift as a design moves, and test revisions before building a prototype.

### Driving simulation

We asked GPT‑6.2 Astra to visualize chassis dynamics of a car on a mountain road. Astra created the 3D model and wrote a Python solver to simulate complex dynamics between the tires and suspension, then animated the results in Blender. This enables engineers to quickly test new designs and improve simulation accuracy over time.

### Mechanical design and assembly

GPT‑6.2 Astra can model a mechanical system part by part, giving engineers a way to show how it goes together and test how design changes affect its behavior.

### From CAD to a paper lamp

Our team used GPT‑6.2 Astra to turn the scalloped balconies of Chicago’s Marina City towers into a lamp. The video follows the design from reference photos through CAD revisions to a physical lamp assembled by hand. The site, generated by GPT-6.2 Astra, can be used to create your own paper lamp.

GPT‑6.2 Astra brings stronger visual reasoning to web design, choosing layouts and imagery that give each site a distinctive look and building elements around the actual goal of the site.

Those gains in visual reasoning and computer use carry over to 3D design. GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol can turn a written brief into an interactive browser experience, from a pinball table you can play to a recreation of the Colosseum you can explore from different angles. On Artificial Analysis’s AA‑3D, human judges try two blinded experiences built from the same prompt and vote for the one they prefer. GPT‑6.2 Astra ranks first with 1,318 Elo, followed by Claude Fable 5.2 at 1,271 and GPT‑6.2 Sol at 1,259.

### Efficient workflows with cleaner code style

GPT‑6.2 Astra has better judgment about how to execute a task, including matching its tools and effort to the workflow, and knowing when to use plugins versus computer use.

On coding, GPT-6.2 Astra is better at implementing and testing complex changes in existing codebases. Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision.

### Cybersecurity capabilities

GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol mark another significant jump in cyber capabilities. They find and exploit vulnerabilities more effectively, write more secure code, and produce better patches, with substantial token-efficiency gains on several evaluations. Like GPT‑6 Astra, 6.2 Astra and Sol meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework.

Due to their increased capabilities, we’re launching GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol with tighter safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity assistance. These protections reduce misuse risk, but also restrict some legitimate vulnerability research and security testing workflows. Through OpenAI Daybreak, defenders can currently access GPT‑6 Sol with reduced cyber refusals on Daybreak Blue, in addition to our alpha for GPT-6 Astra, and GPT‑6 Cyber for advanced, authorized security testing on Daybreak Red. We will work to bring GPT‑6.2 models to Daybreak.

We highlight key benchmark results below, using internal testing configurations with cybersecurity safeguards and classifiers disabled. See the accompanying system card for full results and methodology.

### Giving cyber defenders an edge

Developers increasingly rely on coding agents to write production software, even as more capable agents lower the barrier to finding and exploiting vulnerabilities. PHP2Shell showed how AI can help researchers uncover critical flaws. With GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol, we made defensive capabilities a core focus, introducing new training signals to help developers prevent and repair those flaws—writing secure code from the start and producing patches that preserve intended behavior.

### Safety and alignment

We're deploying GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with our strongest safeguards to date. We've tightened restrictions and strengthened the systems we use to monitor models and intervene when needed.

Like GPT-6 Astra, in addition to meeting the Critical threshold for cybersecurity, both GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meet the High threshold for biological and chemical capabilities under our Preparedness Framework. We’ve implemented protections to mitigate the associated risks, alongside increased restrictions across a set of potential dual-use biological and cybersecurity requests.

More details about our safeguards and testing are available in the GPT-6.2 system card.

### AI research capabilities and safeguards

GPT-6.2 Astra is our first externally released model to meet the High threshold for AI Self-improvement, which measures a model’s ability to accelerate AI research. A ‘High’ designation reflects our assessment that the model’s impact is equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, relative to their 2024 baseline. We track this capability because models that can help develop future AI systems could also introduce new risks to safety, like accelerating progress faster than safeguards or human oversight can adapt.

To address these risks, we’ve built more oversight and controls into how we train and deploy our models. Before expanding internal access to GPT-6.2 Astra, we evaluated its alignment and verified that required safeguards were in place at each stage. We strengthened containment in our research environments, and tested those protections with our most capable models. We also built Control Room, a system that tracks research workloads and can halt further model output when intervention is needed. Our expanded monitoring examines models’ reasoning and actions across internal workloads and supported external deployments. It can automatically flag unauthorized behavior, and, where supported, pause workloads or conversations.

### Alignment

Both models performed similarly to GPT-6 Astra on most alignment evaluations, and took fewer improper actions in simulated workplace tasks. However, in two tests, they were more likely to omit mentioning obstacles that blocked their work, such as a missing file or unavailable search tool. We added instructions in Codex that substantially reduce these omissions, and we’re continuing to investigate the behavior.

### Pricing and availability

Starting today, GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Pro 500 subscribers can use Ultrafast with either model. For the first time, we’re also bringing Ultrafast to Pro 200 subscribers, starting with GPT-6.2 Sol. Eligible Enterprise and Edu users get the same access once their workspace admin enables it. Developers can also access gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol through the OpenAI API, with Ultrafast available for both models at launch.

GPT‑6.2 Astra costs significantly less per task than GPT‑6 Astra, driven by better token efficiency, a 20% discount on input and output tokens, and a deeper 60% discount on cached input tokens. Standard API rates per million tokens are $8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output. GPT‑6.2 Sol carries forward GPT‑6.1 Sol’s rates of $2 for input, $0.10 for cached input, and $10 for output per million tokens.

For GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol, in order to improve cache reuse, help lower costs and latency, and preserve reasoning across turns, we recommend keeping prompt prefixes unchanged and appending new instructions to the conversation.

article_content_zh:
### 专业工作的新标准

我们推出了 GPT-6.2 Astra，这是我们为您最困难的项目设计的新前沿模型，以及 GPT-6.2 Sol，我们为日常工作设计的高效、多功能模型。两种模型都能以更少的输出令牌在要求较高的任务上提供更好的结果，因此您可以在使用限制内完成更多工作。对于企业和开发人员来说，这意味着以规模化的成本实现前沿性能。

GPT-6.2 Astra 为复杂专业工作中的人工智能设定了新的质量标准。它的幻灯片、电子表格和文档读起来不太像人工智能，而是更严格地遵循您提供的模板和您所在领域的惯例。它编写更清晰的代码并构建外观和工作效果更好的前端，特别是对于网站、游戏和 3D 设计。

在测试多步骤专业工作的 Agents’ Last Exam 中，GPT-6.2 Astra 创下了新高，比 GPT-6 Astra 高出 5.2 分，而成本却不到 GPT-6 Astra 的三分之一，比 Claude Fable 5.2 领先 5.5 分，而成本仅为 GPT-6 Astra 的 5%。

我们相信 GPT-6.2 Astra 对于科学家来说是世界上最好的模型。它为 Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 设定了新的高度，该版本测试模型在终端中执行科学工作的能力。 GPT-6.2 Astra 的得分比 GPT-6 Astra 高 9 个百分点，而成本却不到 GPT-6 Astra 的三分之一。它还创下了 Vals 科学指数的新高，该指数要求模型解释真实的生物数据并进行实验以推断模拟系统的工作原理。

在 API 中，GPT-6.2 Astra 的输入和输出代币价格比 GPT-6 Astra 低 20%，缓存输入有 60% 的折扣（输入 8 美元，缓存输入 0.40 美元，输出 40 美元，均为每百万代币）。 GPT-6.2 Sol 保留 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 API 代币价格。在多个基准测试中，这两种模型都接近或优于其他领先模型，而每项任务的成本仅为其一小部分。

### GPT-6.2 Sol：我们日常工作的首选模型

与 GPT-6.1 Sol 相比，GPT-6.2 Sol 更智能、更高效，让您在相同的付费套餐中完成更多任务。它通过多步骤代理工作流程提供支持，书写清晰自然，并且协作直观。 OpenAI 的许多员工都将其用作技术和非技术任务的默认模型。

在 Cognition 的 FrontierCode 2.0 中，GPT-6.2 Sol 与 GPT-6.2 Astra 相差不到 0.5 个点，成本约为 GPT-6.2 Astra 的五分之一（均为最大值）。

它的速度和智能也使其成为人们在工作之外求助于人工智能的重要任务的理想选择。在我们最近发布的 LifeVal 评估（衡量具有挑战性的日常任务的性能）中，GPT-6.2 Sol 的得分超过了 GPT-6 Astra，成本约为 GPT-6 Astra 的七分之一。

### 符合行业标准的专业输出

我们训练 GPT-6.2 Astra 创建更清晰、设计更好的幻灯片、电子表格和文档，更严格地遵循专业人士在法律、销售、财务和会计等领域使用的惯例。写作更加直接和具体，一般性要点和填充物更少。

Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 使用法律作业来测试模型是否可以在源文档中找到相关事实，将其应用到详细的摘要中，并生成满足每项要求的准确交付成果。 GPT-6.2 Astra 树立了新的技术水平，以大约六分之一的成本将 Claude Fable 5.2 的通过率提高了一倍以上。 Astra for Law（我们为律师配置的 GPT-6.2 Astra）在此基准测试中得分甚至更高。

我们的内部 GDPval v2 基准是 GDPval 的下一代迭代，用于衡量咨询、金融和设计等领域实际项目的复杂、长期工作流程。 GPT-6.2 Astra 在我们测试的模型中领先，比 GPT-6 Astra 提高了 6.2 个百分点，同时使用的输出代币减少了 22%。 GPT-6.2 Sol 比 GPT-6.1 Sol 提高了 5.3 点。

### 作业簿和备忘录

构建估值工作簿或撰写投资备忘录首先要在源文件中查找相关数据，并弄清楚它们如何组合在一起。 Artificial Analysis 的 AA-AnalystAgent 测试适用于真实的电子表格和报告。在一项任务中，模型使用加州医疗补助的支出报告来计算该计划在医疗运输上的支出。 GPT-6.2 Astra 创下新高，在所有五次独立尝试中正确回答了 62.5% 的问题。

GPT-6.2 Astra 是我们迄今为止设计幻灯片和遵循幻灯片模板的最佳模型，无论是给定原始文件还是屏幕截图。它可以将布局、颜色和版式匹配到精确的字体大小，并将模板的书写风格带入新幻灯片中。早期测试人员发现这些套牌更容易直接使用，编辑次数也更少，这要归功于陈述主要内容的标题和专注于读者需要的细节的简洁正文。

### 计算机使用和交互式网页设计

GPT-6.2 Astra 更精确的计算机使用使其能够在 CAD 和模拟工具中细化到各个零件和连接。工程师可以使用这些额外的细节来检查组件的配合情况，查看负载随着设计的变化而变化的位置，并在构建原型之前测试修订。

我们要求 GPT‑6.2 Astra 可视化山路上汽车的底盘动态。 Astra 创建了 3D 模型并编写了一个 Python 解算器来模拟轮胎和悬架之间的复杂动力学，然后在 Blender 中对结果进行动画处理。这使得工程师能够快速测试新设计并随着时间的推移提高仿真精度。

### 机械设计与装配

GPT-6.2 Astra 可以对机械系统的各个部分进行建模，为工程师提供了一种展示其如何组合并测试设计变更如何影响其行为的方法。

我们的团队使用 GPT-6.2 Astra 将芝加哥滨海城塔楼的扇形阳台变成了一盏灯。该视频讲述了从参考照片到 CAD 修订再到手工组装的实体灯的设计过程。该网站由 GPT-6.2 Astra 生成，可用于创建您自己的纸灯。

GPT-6.2 Astra 为网页设计带来了更强大的视觉推理，选择为每个网站提供独特外观的布局和图像，并围绕网站的实际目标构建元素。

这些视觉推理和计算机使用方面的进步也延续到了 3D 设计中。 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 可以将书面简报转变为交互式浏览器体验，从可以玩的弹球桌到可以从不同角度探索的罗马斗兽场的娱乐。在 Artificial Analysis 的 AA-3D 中，人类评委尝试根据同一提示构建的两种盲体验，并投票选出他们喜欢的一种。 GPT-6.2 Astra 以 1,318 Elo 排名第一，其次是 Claude Fable 5.2（1,271）和 GPT-6.2 Sol（1,259）。

### 高效的工作流程和简洁的代码风格

GPT-6.2 Astra 对如何执行任务有更好的判断，包括将其工具和工作与工作流程相匹配，以及知道何时使用插件而不是计算机。

在编码方面，GPT-6.2 Astra 更擅长在现有代码库中实现和测试复杂的更改。早期的测试人员报告了更清晰的代码风格和更集中的测试，并且修改次数更少。

### 网络安全能力

GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 标志着网络能力的又一次重大飞跃。他们更有效地发现和利用漏洞，编写更安全的代码，并生成更好的补丁，并在多项评估中获得了显着的令牌效率提升。与 GPT-6 Astra 一样，6.2 Astra 和 Sol 也满足我们的准备框架下的网络安全关键阈值。

由于功能增强，我们推出了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，为高风险网络安全援助提供更严格的保障措施。这些保护措施降低了误用风险，但也限制了一些合法的漏洞研究和安全测试工作流程。通过 OpenAI Daybreak，防御者目前可以在 Daybreak Blue 上访问 GPT-6 Sol，减少网络拒绝，此外还可以在 Daybreak Red 上访问 GPT-6 Astra 的 alpha 版，以及在 Daybreak Red 上进行高级授权安全测试的 GPT-6 Cyber​​。我们将努力将 GPT-6.2 模型引入 Daybreak。

我们在下面重点介绍关键基准测试结果，使用内部测试配置并禁用网络安全保障措施和分类器。有关完整结果和方法，请参阅随附的系统卡。

### 为网络防御者提供优势

开发人员越来越依赖编码代理来编写生产软件，尽管功能更强大的代理降低了发现和利用漏洞的障碍。 PHP2Shell 展示了人工智能如何帮助研究人员发现关键缺陷。借助 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，我们将防御能力作为核心焦点，引入新的训练信号来帮助开发人员预防和修复这些缺陷 - 从一开始就编写安全代码并生成保留预期行为的补丁。

我们正在部署 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，并提供迄今为止最强大的保障措施。我们加强了限制并加强了用于监控模型并在需要时进行干预的系统。

与 GPT-6 Astra 一样，除了满足网络安全的关键阈值之外，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 还满足我们的准备框架下的生物和化学能力的高阈值。我们已经实施了保护措施来减轻相关风险，同时增加了对一系列潜在的双重用途生物和网络安全请求的限制。

有关我们的防护措施和测试的更多详细信息，请参阅 GPT-6.2 系统卡。

### 人工智能研究能力及保障

GPT-6.2 Astra是我们第一个对外发布的满足AI自我提升高门槛的模型，衡量模型加速AI研究的能力。 “高”称号反映了我们的评估，即相对于 2024 年的基准，该模型的影响相当于为每位 OpenAI 研究人员提供了一名额外的、能力很强的研究工程师作为助理。我们跟踪这种能力是因为有助于开发未来人工智能系统的模型也可能会给安全带来新的风险，比如加速进步的速度快于保障措施或人类监督所能适应的速度。

为了解决这些风险，我们对训练和部署模型的方式进行了更多的监督和控制。在扩大对 GPT-6.2 Astra 的内部访问之前，我们评估了其一致性并验证了每个阶段所需的保护措施是否到位。我们加强了研究环境的遏制，并用我们最有能力的模型测试了这些保护措施。我们还构建了控制室，这是一个跟踪研究工作量的系统，可以在需要干预时停止进一步的模型输出。我们的扩展监控检查模型在内部工作负载和支持的外部部署中的推理和操作。它可以自动标记未经授权的行为，并在支持的情况下暂停工作负载或对话。

在大多数对齐评估中，这两种模型的表现与GPT-6 Astra相似，并且在模拟工作场所任务中采取的不当行为较少。然而，在两个测试中，他们更有可能忽略那些阻碍他们工作的障碍，比如丢失的文件或不可用的搜索工具。我们在食品法典中增加了大量减少这些遗漏的说明，我们正在继续调查这种行为。

### 定价和供货情况

从今天开始，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 可供 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中的所有 Plus、Pro、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户使用。 Pro 500 订阅者可以使用任一型号的 Ultrafast。从 GPT-6.2 Sol 开始，我们还首次为 Pro 200 订阅者带来 Ultrafast。一旦工作区管理员启用，符合条件的企业和教育用户将获得相同的访问权限。开发人员还可以通过 OpenAI API 访问 gpt-6.2-astra 和 gpt-6.2-sol，这两种模型在发布时都可以使用 Ultrafast。

GPT-6.2 Astra 每项任务的成本明显低于 GPT-6 Astra，这得益于更好的令牌效率、输入和输出令牌 20% 的折扣以及缓存输入令牌 60% 的更深折扣。每百万代币的标准 API 费率为输入 8 美元、缓存输入 0.40 美元、输出 40 美元。 GPT-6.2 Sol 继承了 GPT-6.1 Sol 的每百万代币 2 美元的输入费率、0.10 美元的缓存输入费率以及 10 美元的输出费率。

对于 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，为了提高缓存重用、帮助降低成本和延迟并保留轮流推理，我们建议保持提示前缀不变并向对话附加新指令。

title: Nvidia stopped disclosing Singapore sales as revenues hit $104bn
title_en: Nvidia stopped disclosing Singapore sales as revenues hit $104bn

inline_images.caption: Jensen Huang resigned following a scandal connecting him to Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing and data centre © Edgar Su/Reuters
inline_images.alt: Jensen Huang resigned following a scandal connecting him to Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing and data centre © Edgar Su/Reuters

inline_images.caption: Huang’s family helped shape Nvidia’s Singapore dealings © How Hwee Young/EPA
inline_images.alt: Huang’s family helped shape Nvidia’s Singapore dealings © How Hwee Young/EPA

inline_images.caption: US authorities are investigating Megaspeed and other Singaporean companies over their potential links to networks that have facilitated the transfer of high-end chips to China © Mosaymay/Dreamstime
inline_images.alt: US authorities are investigating Megaspeed and other Singaporean companies over their potential links to networks that have facilitated the transfer of high-end chips to China © Mosaymay/Dreamstime

author: Owen Walker and Antoine Gara
article_content:
Nvidia stopped disclosing the scale of its business in Singapore last year, at a time the city-state accounted for almost half of its worldwide revenues.The chipmaker booked $104bn of revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, a 72 per cent increase in 12 months, according to company accounts. The massive increase came as Nvidia switched from reporting geographic sales based on a customer’s billing address to its headquarters, a move that led to Singapore being moved from a prominent billing in the chipmaker’s revenue breakdown.

Nvidia has previously declined to comment on the reasons for changing its reporting methodology.The chipmaker’s Singapore operations have come under the spotlight following the spectacular fall of Jensen Huang. The former Nvidia chief resigned after it emerged that he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, who is linked to a Singapore business that was one of the US chipmaker’s biggest clients in Asia.

US authorities are investigating whether the Singapore business, Megaspeed, was involved in smuggling Nvidia chips to China and whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

“There is now a lot more focus on Nvidia’s Singapore business and questions about who its end customers are,” said an investor who is investigating Nvidia’s dealings in south-east Asia.

The Singapore accounts show that the subsidiary booked $117.8bn of revenue in the 12 months to January 2026, including $13.6bn of sales to another Nvidia company. Given the nature of the Singapore operation as a global hub, customers it serves are from all over the world. Only a small quantity of the chips Nvidia sells ends up in or goes through Singapore.

The Singapore subsidiary generated just $53mn of profit in the year to January 2026, suggesting limited scope for Nvidia to benefit from Singapore’s low corporate tax rates.

Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment on the size of its Singapore revenues, the reasons for their growth in the city-state and whether they were linked to Chinese companies gaining access to its chips.

Singapore’s outsized role as a revenue generator for Nvidia used to show up in the company’s overall results. In January 2025, the US company reported that Singapore was its second-biggest geographic area by revenue, based on customer billing location.

The Singapore office generated $23.7bn of revenue, behind only the US and representing 18 per cent of global income, based on customers’ billing location. The annual accounts said that most of the business was generated by customers using the Singapore office to centralise invoicing and that most of the products were shipped elsewhere, with less than 2 per cent of revenue tied to chips that landed in the city-state.

As recently as July last year, Nvidia reported that the Singapore office accounted for 22 per cent of total revenue. This was around the time Nvidia said it began cutting ties with Megaspeed, following US Department of Commerce investigations into the business.

Nvidia then changed its financial reporting methodology and stopped splitting out revenue that went to the Singapore office.

Before the 2025 reporting change, Nvidia said in its financial filing that it booked sales based on the billing locations of its customers, but that the end customer’s location “may be different than our customer’s billing location”.

It added that “most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant”, according to the filings.

Nvidia declined to comment beyond its financial filings on the reasons for changing its reporting methodology.

“It was probably a rational response to play down the role of the Singapore office in light of the export control rules — you don’t want to be at the forefront of an investigation,” said Robert Walker, a research fellow at the Lowy Institute think-tank.

“But even if there is no nefarious activity, the act of masking the information raises suspicions and can be counter-productive.”

The US has also tried to crack down on the more legitimate practice of companies leasing US chips to data centres in south-east Asia, which make them available to Chinese tech companies.

On Monday, the US commerce department updated its export rules by requiring data centres operating in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia to require a government licence in order to purchase advanced AI chips made by American companies.

article_content_zh:
去年，英伟达停止披露其在新加坡的业务规模，而当时该城邦国家占其全球营收的近一半。根据公司账目，2023年，这家芯片制造商通过其新加坡子公司实现了1040亿美元的营收，在12个月内增长了72%。这一大幅增长的背景是，英伟达将按客户账单地址报告的地区销售额改为按其总部报告，此举导致新加坡从一个重要的账单地区变为一个较小的账单地区。

一位正在调查英伟达在东南亚业务的投资者表示：“现在人们更加关注英伟达的新加坡业务，以及其最终客户是谁的问题。”

新加坡账目显示，该子公司在截至 2026 年 1 月的 12 个月内实现了 1178 亿美元的收入，其中包括向另一家 Nvidia 公司的 136 亿美元销售额。鉴于新加坡业务作为全球中心的性质，其服务的客户来自世界各地。英伟达销售的芯片中只有少量最终到达或经过新加坡。

截至 2026 年 1 月，这家新加坡子公司的利润仅为 5300 万美元，这表明英伟达从新加坡低企业税率中受益的范围有限。

英伟达没有回应有关其新加坡收入规模、其在新加坡增长的原因以及是否与中国公司获得其芯片有关的置评请求。

新加坡作为英伟达收入来源的巨大作用曾经体现在该公司的整体业绩中。 2025 年 1 月，这家美国公司报告称，根据客户账单地点，按收入计算，新加坡是其第二大地理区域。

根据客户的账单地点，新加坡办事处创造了 237 亿美元的收入，仅次于美国，占全球收入的 18%。年度账目称，大部分业务是由客户利用新加坡办事处集中开具发票产生的，大部分产品都运往其他地方，只有不到 2% 的收入与运抵新加坡的芯片相关。

就在去年 7 月，英伟达报告称，新加坡办事处的收入占总收入的 22%。就在此时，英伟达表示，在美国商务部对 Megaspeed 业务进行调查后，该公司开始切断与该公司的合作关系。

随后，英伟达改变了其财务报告方法，并停止分配新加坡办事处的收入。

在 2025 年报告变更之前，英伟达在其财务文件中表示，它根据客户的账单地点预订销售额，但最终客户的地点“可能与我们客户的账单地点不同”。

文件显示，该公司补充说，“与新加坡收入相关的大部分货物都运往新加坡以外的地区，而运往新加坡的数量微不足道”。

除了财务文件外，英伟达拒绝就改变其报告方法的原因发表评论。

洛伊研究所智囊团研究员罗伯特·沃克表示：“根据出口管制规则，淡化新加坡办事处的作用可能是一个理性的反应——你不想站在调查的最前沿。”

“但即使没有邪恶活动，掩盖信息的行为也会引起怀疑，并可能适得其反。”

美国当局正在调查 Megaspeed 和其他新加坡公司与东南亚网络的潜在联系，这些网络促进了高端芯片向中国的转移，违反了华盛顿的出口限制。

美国还试图打击公司将美国芯片租赁给东南亚数据中心的更合法做法，这些芯片向中国科技公司提供。

周一，美国商务部更新了出口规则，要求在新加坡、马来西亚、泰国和印度尼西亚运营的数据中心必须获得政府许可才能购买美国公司制造的先进人工智能芯片。

title: Take-Two’s Firaxis, Maker of ‘Civilization,’ Cuts a Third of Its Staff
title_en: Take-Two’s Firaxis, Maker of ‘Civilization,’ Cuts a Third of Its Staff
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
“Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength – designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years,” a spokesperson said in a statement provided to the site.

“As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

The firm previously laid off staff in September 2025.

The studio is reportedly working on a new XCOM title which has "faced development struggles and missed a significant milestone over the summer," according to Schreier, citing internal sources who said the game was still in development but may "face a shakeup" as a result of the staff departures. The last XCOM release, Enemy Unknown 2, was released in 2016; Firaxis shipped Civilization VII last year.

Firaxis parent Take-Two Interactive posted net revenue down 16% YoY, but reported GTA 6 pre-orders "far in excess of expectations". A report today from Sensor Tower suggested pre-orders had already topped $1.4B, meaning the title has already exceeded its predecessor's initial three days of revenue in advance of going on sale.

title: Anthropic, Other AI Models Regularly Identify Civilians as Military Targets in Tests
title_en: Anthropic, Other AI Models Regularly Identify Civilians as Military Targets in Tests
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.

Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery.

The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.

The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.

Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency its technology could not be used by the agency for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has insisted that today’s AI systems aren’t reliable enough to make life-or-death decisions without a human in the loop. Meanwhile, the Pentagon argued it should be able to deploy the technology for any awful military purpose.

The new research raises further questions about whether AI companies are capable of preventing their models from being used in warfare.

Ironically, AI models from Anthropic performed the worst in these simulated scenarios. But none of the models performed particularly well. None of the researchers’ requests were blocked by a safety classifier, and refusals were uncommon. Even when models did refuse, they often complied after being told they were playing a game.

Anthropic spokesperson Eduardo Maia Silva told TechCrunch the company appreciates Vals’s report, recommendations, and collaboration, and acknowledged that the outcomes were not acceptable.

“The examples in the report are very clearly against our rules and we have banned and will ban users when we see this behavior,” according to an emailed company statement sent by Silva. “Even for authorized settings, Anthropic has long been firm that today’s frontier AI systems are not reliable enough to power fully autonomous weapons.”

Anthropic told TechCrunch that its teams were already developing additional safeguards before the report was published and that those measures would be in place soon. Anthropic is also expanding its own testing and enhancing safeguards and enforcement to address any gaps it finds.

OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans told TechCrunch the company prohibits using its public models to facilitate violence or for unapproved national security purposes, including in the scenarios Vals simulated.

“We actively detect and disrupt misuse, including by suspending accounts that violate our policies,” OpenAI said in an emailed statement. “We’re also developing additional safeguards for our public models against misuse involving drones and drone software.”

Vals notes in the report that the models were never asked to directly make strike decisions, a task the researchers said the models would typically refuse. That doesn’t mean their outputs couldn’t have dire or fatal consequences in the real world. For instance, targeting information could be used by autonomous weapons systems.

In some scenarios, the models were asked to report whether people were visible. Positive reports were followed by simulated strikes and the models would see the consequences.

The report relies on commercial models from frontier AI labs, not the models those companies might provide to the military. It’s not clear what the additional safeguards would apply to military use, though.

Vals also noted that technical challenges, including latency and limited onboard computing capacity, make it difficult to use general-purpose AI models for live drone targeting. Those constraints make their deployment in combat less of an immediate threat.

A more immediate threat, the researchers say, is that AI models could be used to annotate battlefield footage at scale, producing training data for autonomous targeting systems.

For instance, researchers relied on real satellite imagery of an Iranian school that was bombed by the U.S. in February 2026, killing more than 150 civilians. Bloomberg later reported that an “overreliance on AI” contributed to the strike. In Vals’s testing, models frequently marked the school, which sat next to a military complex, as a strike target, with Claude Opus 5.5 selecting the school in 69% of ordinary trials and 72% of game-framed trials.

Anthropic no longer has an active Pentagon contract, but other companies including SpaceXAI, OpenAI, and Google do. A recent Congressional Research Service report found that the Pentagon is not known to be using any frontier AI model directly in autonomous weapons systems directly.

TechCrunch has also reached out to Meta, Google, Thinking Machines Lab, and SpaceXAI for comment.

Rebecca Bellan is a senior reporter at TechCrunch where she covers the business, policy, and emerging trends shaping artificial intelligence. Her work has also appeared in Forbes, Bloomberg, The Atlantic, The Daily Beast, and other publications.

title: Source: Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Huang, after he released a statement saying he "made serious mistakes" and fell below "the standards" (CNN)
title_en: Source: Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Huang, after he released a statement saying he "made serious mistakes" and fell below "the standards" (CNN)

inline_images.caption: Hadas Gold
inline_images.alt: Hadas Gold

inline_images.caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks during a doorstep after attending the AI Ecosystem Reception in Tokyo, Japan, July 16, 2026.
inline_images.alt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks during a doorstep after attending the AI Ecosystem Reception in Tokyo

author: CNN
article_content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly stepped down last week after a scandal involving extramarital affairs, said Tuesday he would be “honored” to return to the role if the board were to allow it. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.

I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” Huang said in a statement. He stepped down last week from the company he co-founded 33 years ago, ending an extraordinary run at the helm of one of the world’s most valuable companies. The resignation came just four days after the company’s board announced it was investigating him, following reports that he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, who sources have identified as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; as well as reports of another affair with an Nvidia executive.

CNN’s numerous attempts to reach Alice Huang for comment have been unsuccessful. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Jensen Huang said in the statement, noting support he’s received.

CNN has reached out to Nvidia for comment on Huang’s statement. The company’s board of directors, however, is not considering reinstating Huang, a source familiar with the situation told CNN. President Donald Trump, who frequently looked to Huang for guidance on the nation’s AI policies, said Monday he “would not mind” if Huang returned as CEO.

Trump is scheduled to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later in the week. The president said he “may” discuss Nvidia with Xi. Beyond Trump, Huang has seen a strong showing of support in recent days – both from current and former Nvidia employees and across Silicon Valley.

Elon Musk said in a post on X that he would be “honored” to hire Huang. The Tesla and SpaceX CEO also said he would be signing a growing petition for Nvidia’s board to bring back Huang. Big questions loom.

Answers could soon come The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between Alice Huang and the Chinese government. Multiple sources have told CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing.

Nvidia is synonymous with the global AI boom, supplying some of the most advanced chips that power AI models for some of the world’s largest technology companies. On Thursday, Nvidia announced its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as the company’s interim CEO while the board considers internal and external candidates.

Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in a hearing scheduled for December 1, and Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, will testify the following day. Both will be closed-door hearings with transcribed interviews subsequently released to the public. Huang previously apologized to his family and Nvidia employees in a company message last week, acknowledging that he had been unfaithful to his wife and saying he would cooperate with an independent investigation initiated by the company’s board of directors.

“I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” he said last week. Alice Huang is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company and Nvidia customer.

Some US sources say that whether or not she was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions.

Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing, saying it is a “compliant and legal company” and that it will cooperate with the US investigation. In a statement to CNN, Nvidia said allegations of illegal chip diversion were “thoroughly investigated and debunked last year.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.” Nvidia is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings later on Tuesday and hold a subsequent call with analysts, which will be the first opportunity for the public to hear directly from the company’s new leadership.

article_content_zh:
英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋上周因婚外情丑闻突然辞职，他周二表示，如果董事会允许，他将“很荣幸”重返这一职位。 “我没有达到 NVIDIA 每个人的期望标准，而且我在个人生活中犯了严重错误。

黄在一份声明中表示：“我给董事会带来了问题，对此我深感遗憾。”他上周从这家他 33 年前共同创立的公司辞职，结束了他执掌全球最有价值公司之一的非凡历程。就在四天前，公司董事会宣布对他进行调查。此前有报道称，他与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有多起婚外情，其中包括与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的婚外情，消息人士称她是潜在的中国情报资产；还有报道称，他与英伟达 (Nvidia) 的一名高管发生了另一起婚外情。

美国有线电视新闻网多次尝试联系黄爱丽发表评论，但均未成功。黄仁勋在声明中表示：“如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”他指出了他所获得的支持。

美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 已联系英伟达，请其对黄仁勋的声明发表评论。然而，一位知情人士告诉 CNN，该公司董事会并未考虑恢复黄的职位。唐纳德·特朗普总统经常向黄仁勋寻求有关国家人工智能政策的指导，他周一表示，如果黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，他“不会介意”。

特朗普定于本周晚些时候会见中国领导人习近平。总统表示，他“可能”与习近平讨论英伟达的问题。除了特朗普之外，黄仁勋最近几天还得到了来自英伟达现任和前任员工以及整个硅谷的强烈支持。

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，他将“很荣幸”雇用黄。这位特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官还表示，他将签署一份越来越多的请愿书，要求英伟达董事会召回黄仁勋。大问题迫在眉睫。

答案很快就会揭晓 美国情报界仍在努力了解黄爱丽与中国政府之间的关系。多个消息来源告诉美国有线电视新闻网，迄今为止收集到的有关她的情报并不能证明她是北京的间谍。

英伟达是全球人工智能热潮的代名词，为一些全球最大的科技公司提供一些最先进的芯片，为人工智能模型提供支持。周四，英伟达宣布首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)将担任公司临时首席执行官，同时董事会考虑内部和外部候选人。

黄仁勋已同意在定于 12 月 1 日举行的国会听证会上作证，英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 将于第二天作证。这两场听证会都将是闭门听证会，随后将向公众发布采访记录。黄先生上周在公司信息中向家人和英伟达员工道歉，承认自己对妻子不忠，并表示将配合公司董事会发起的独立调查。

“我热爱我们的国家和我们的公司。我致力于保护 NVIDIA 并支持美国的国家安全，”他上周表示。 Alice Huang 是新加坡科技公司 Megaspeed 的前高管，也是 Nvidia 的客户。

一些美国消息人士称，无论她是否被中国情报部门招募，她都会构成反情报风险，因为中国国家安全法要求其公民在接到要求时协助情报收集工作。人们越来越担心 Megaspeed 购买的芯片被转移到中国实体，从而可能绕过美国的出口限制。

Megaspeed否认有任何不当行为，称其是一家“合规且合法的公司”，并将配合美国的调查。英伟达在给 CNN 的一份声明中表示，非法芯片转移的指控“已于去年得到彻底调查并被揭穿”。中国外交部称有关黄爱丽是中国间谍的指控是“毫无根据的猜测，企图抹黑和中伤中国”。英伟达计划于周二晚些时候公布第三季度收益，并随后与分析师举行电话会议，这将是公众第一次有机会直接听取该公司新领导层的讲话。

title: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff
title_en: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff

inline_images.caption: Evaluation of GPT-6 Astra’s inbox tasks by physicians using maximum reasoning effort. | Image: OpenAI
inline_images.caption_en: Evaluation of GPT-6 Astra’s inbox tasks by physicians using maximum reasoning effort. | Image: OpenAI

author: Alan Truly
article_content:
OpenAI wants GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna to click and type their way through clinic software and insurance portals as digital clerks. GPT-6 Luna handles administrative tasks for about 8.5 cents per task, according to the company.

In a recent product announcement, OpenAI targets the lack of APIs in healthcare. The computer-use agents integrated into the Agents API in late September operate existing user interfaces the way a human would. In this case, they transfer data between electronic health records and external web portals.

According to OpenAI, when a patient reports back pain, the agent is meant to search relevant prior findings and draft both an MRI order and a reply to the patient. It should also prepare a prior authorization request on the insurer's portal. Clinicians and the responsible administrative staff review these drafts before they are released. The features are available through the API as well as in ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians.

### GPT-6 Luna completes admin tasks for 8.5 cents per task

In an evaluation described by OpenAI, GPT-6 Astra worked through tasks from electronic health record inboxes, among other things preparing an ibuprofen dosage for a child with a broken arm. Physician reviewers rated 99 percent of the 325 tasks evaluated as clinically safe. In 93 percent of 646 reviews, the reviewers called the prep work very or extremely helpful.

For administrative workflows such as prior authorizations, appeals, or medical equipment orders, OpenAI points to the independent HealthAdminBench benchmark from Stanford University researchers. GPT-6 Astra scored 94.3 percent of possible points. GPT-6 Luna, built for low API pricing, scored 91.8 percent and, according to OpenAI, cost about 8.5 cents per task, 98 percent less than Astra. Both models ran at maximum reasoning effort on the benchmark.

### Major US healthcare companies test and deploy OpenAI's computer-use agents

Several partner organizations are helping advance the technology. At CVS Health, the agents already process referrals and specialist consultations across separate systems. According to the announcement, one agent cleared a months-long backlog of outgoing documents in one weekend, while another handles the system steps for tens of thousands of consultations daily. CVS Health published its software architecture as Agent Kit on GitHub.

At insurer Cigna Healthcare, the models merge patient information from more than 10 separate systems. Abridge is developing the agents for planned use in clinical discharge planning. Ambience has demonstrated additional safety mechanisms in which an agent stops when a patient's record is unclear and asks a physician for input. Startups like Assort also use the feature in Codex to complete referrals in practice management software whose APIs don't support that final click.

### Data privacy, health records, and Europe

Because the agents work directly in electronic health records, protecting sensitive health data is a core concern. OpenAI says it does not use organizational data to train its base models. ChatGPT for Healthcare offers role-based access controls and audit logs, according to the company. Organizations can also configure the applications and environments so an agent only accesses the records and actions needed for a given task.

For HIPAA-compliant workflows with protected health information, organizations must sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with OpenAI. They also need to use the covered services and apply the required security and retention settings. The healthcare facilities themselves are responsible for proper use, but OpenAI, as a contracting party, also has its own obligations under HIPAA. Verified medical professionals in the US who use ChatGPT for Clinicians, a free individual plan, can also sign a BAA, though it applies only to the features the agreement covers.

In the CVS Health deployment, data stays within infrastructure that CVS controls, according to OpenAI. CVS reviews the agents' work steps through screenshots and action logs. The announcement does not say where those screenshots are processed or how long they are stored. It also does not address the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). So far, the offering targets the US market.

OpenAI frames the technology primarily as a tool against administrative friction in a highly fragmented healthcare system. Whether it sees broad adoption likely will not depend solely on the accuracy rates and costs cited in the company's announcement. Also decisive is how reliably the agents connect to existing systems and whether AI agents can be dependably monitored in practice. Another open question is whether a human is required to decide on clinically or legally relevant steps.

article_content_zh:
OpenAI 希望 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6 Luna 作为数字文员通过诊所软件和保险门户进行点击和打字。据该公司称，GPT-6 Luna 处理管理任务的费用约为每项任务 8.5 美分。

在最近的产品公告中，OpenAI 针对医疗保健领域缺乏 API 的问题。九月下旬，计算机使用的代理集成到代理 API 中，以人类的方式操作现有的用户界面。在这种情况下，他们在电子健康记录和外部门户网站之间传输数据。

根据 OpenAI 的说法，当患者报告背痛时，代理将搜索相关的先前发现并起草 MRI 命令和对患者的答复。它还应该在保险公司的门户网站上准备一份事先授权请求。临床医生和负责的行政人员在发布这些草案之前会对其进行审查。这些功能可通过 API 以及 ChatGPT for Healthcare 和 ChatGPT for Clinicians 中使用。

### GPT-6 Luna 完成管理任务，每项任务 8.5 美分

在 OpenAI 描述的一项评估中，GPT-6 Astra 完成了电子健康记录收件箱中的任务，其中包括为手臂骨折的儿童准备布洛芬剂量。医生评审员将 325 项评估任务中的 99% 评为临床安全。在 646 条评论中，93% 的评论者认为准备工作非常或极其有帮助。

对于事先授权、上诉或医疗设备订单等管理工作流程，OpenAI 参考了斯坦福大学研究人员的独立 HealthAdminBench 基准。 GPT-6 Astra 获得了 94.3% 的得分。 GPT-6 Luna 专为低 API 定价而打造，得分为 91.8%，根据 OpenAI 的数据，每个任务的成本约为 8.5 美分，比 Astra 低 98%。两种模型都在基准测试中以最大推理努力运行。

### 美国主要医疗保健公司测试并部署 OpenAI 的计算机使用代理

一些合作伙伴组织正在帮助推进这项技术。在 CVS Health，代理已经跨不同的系统处理转诊和专家咨询。公告称，一名工作人员在一个周末清理了长达数月积压的外发文件，另一名工作人员每天处理数万次咨询的系统步骤。 CVS Health 在 GitHub 上发布了其软件架构作为 Agent Kit。

在保险公司 Cigna Healthcare，这些模型合并了来自 10 多个独立系统的患者信息。 Abridge 正在开发用于临床出院计划的药物。 Ambience 已经展示了额外的安全机制，当患者的记录不清楚时，代理会停止并询问医生输入信息。像 Assort 这样的初创公司也使用 Codex 中的功能来完成实践管理软件中的推荐，但其 API 不支持最终点击。

### 数据隐私、健康记录和欧洲

由于代理直接在电子健康记录中工作，因此保护敏感的健康数据是一个核心问题。 OpenAI 表示，它不会使用组织数据来训练其基础模型。据该公司称，ChatGPT for Healthcare 提供基于角色的访问控制和审核日志。组织还可以配置应用程序和环境，以便代理仅访问给定任务所需的记录和操作。

对于具有受保护健康信息的符合 HIPAA 的工作流程，组织必须与 OpenAI 签署业务合作协议 (BAA)。他们还需要使用涵盖的服务并应用所需的安全和保留设置。医疗机构本身有责任正确使用，但 OpenAI 作为缔约方，也有 HIPAA 规定的自己的义务。在美国使用 ChatGPT for Clinicians（一项免费的个人计划）的经过验证的医疗专业人员也可以签署 BAA，尽管它仅适用于协议涵盖的功能。

据 OpenAI 称，在 CVS Health 部署中，数据保留在 CVS 控制的基础设施内。 CVS 通过屏幕截图和操作日志来审查代理的工作步骤。该公告没有说明这些屏幕截图的处理位置或存储时间。它也没有涉及欧洲通用数据保护条例（GDPR）。到目前为止，该产品的目标市场是美国市场。

OpenAI 将该技术主要定位为在高度分散的医疗保健系统中应对行政摩擦的工具。是否会被广泛采用并不仅仅取决于该公司公告中引用的准确率和成本。同样具有决定性意义的是代理与现有系统的连接有多可靠，以及人工智能代理在实践中是否可以得到可靠的监控。另一个悬而未决的问题是，是否需要人类决定临床或法律相关的步骤。

title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
title_en: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
Chinese companies have been skirting US export bans by legally renting Nvidia computing power in third countries. After Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, the US is closing that loophole. An investigation also reveals how China has cushioned the years-long chip embargo through an entire industry built around model distillation.

For years, the US has tried to cut China off from importing advanced AI processors through strict export controls. Chinese companies responded by exploiting an entirely legal loophole, renting the computing power they needed through cloud-based remote access from foreign data centers that were allowed to receive US hardware.

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) at the US Commerce Department now wants to shut down that workaround with an interim rule. It aligns remote-access rules with existing physical export bans. Data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil will need a US government license to buy advanced AI chips from US manufacturers like Nvidia, Bloomberg reports. Applications will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

Subsidiaries of US-headquartered companies are exempt from the license requirement, as are shipments to data centers running only commercial recommendation systems for online retailers or social media platforms. The rules take effect once published in the Federal Register. Nvidia's stock fell as much as 2.9 percent after the announcement, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped up to 5.5 percent.

### Illegal chip diversions and Jensen Huang's downfall

The political trigger, though, was suspected illegal smuggling of physical chips. The new rule comes just days after the abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who had admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former manager at Singapore-based Megaspeed International. US authorities suspect Alice Huang, who now lives in China, of espionage. They are investigating Megaspeed for possible export-control violations after banned Nvidia chips reportedly turned up in a Chinese data center linked to her. Megaspeed denies any wrongdoing, and President Donald Trump said Monday that Jensen Huang did not compromise national security.

The scandal still set off an open power struggle in Washington over lax enforcement of chip sanctions. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had delayed a Trump-authorized measure against illegal chip diversions, according to Axios, prompting Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to publicly accuse him of inaction. The Commerce Department's announcement now states with unusual bluntness that the draft rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council.

### Reuters investigation maps China's distillation industry

A separate exclusive Reuters investigation shows how Chinese developers cope with the years-long shortage of top-tier domestic hardware. By reviewing more than 300 Chinese papers, patents, job postings, and government documents, Reuters shows for the first time how heavily China relies on model distillation as a stopgap. What started years ago as an academic workaround has grown into an industrial sector with a highly developed division of labor.

The technique does not make powerful chips like Nvidia's unnecessary, but it drastically reduces developers' own compute load because a single expensive query to a US teacher model replaces repeated computation. Chinese firms now build their own software to automate the extraction of answers, code, and problem solutions from leading US models. Specialized workers then process the material to train smaller, far cheaper local student models.

Research papers show how deep this practice already runs. As early as November 2024, researchers at Shanghai Jiao Tong University created 10,750 training examples for Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B. They drew on about 5,000 responses from OpenAI's o1 and translations from GPT-4o mini, though they themselves warned at the time of a looming dependence on outside innovation. Alibaba described its systematic use of GPT-4 and GPT-4o for foreign-language training data in April 2025. In February 2026, Jiao Tong University and food-delivery company Meituan used GPT-4o to train smaller models for coordinating coding agents.

Policy directives from Beijing are driving this growth. The government wants to deploy smaller, low-cost AI systems across China's manufacturing sector. Official government documents do not directly instruct anyone to copy American models. Still, an "AI+Manufacturing"package published by eight ministries in January and initiatives in Shanghai and Shenzhen explicitly promote distillation and other techniques that reduce computing needs. In practice, this state-driven push for efficiency drives Chinese developers to tap the most powerful US models as a data source at scale.

Ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, this industrial-scale practice is becoming a geopolitical flashpoint. Distillation is not illegal, but it violates the terms of service of US developers like OpenAI and Anthropic. Both companies have long leveled accusations against Chinese AI labs, documenting the massive volumes of extracted data in detailed reports and deploying technical countermeasures. Anthropic recently said it now successfully blocks most such distillation attacks. These accusations were also covered in our Frontier Radar #4 on Chinese models.

US officials also confronted Chinese regulators in Chengdu as early as July because Washington sees mass distillation as the main reason for China's rapid AI catch-up, according to Reuters. Chinese insiders also point to their own advances in algorithms and model design. Treasury Secretary Bessent is now threatening sanctions and Entity List designations if covert distillation attacks cross the line into intellectual property theft. Chinese developers, uncertain about the rules, recently asked Beijing's Ministry of Industry for clear guidelines on using foreign models.

article_content_zh:
中国公司一直在通过在第三国合法租用英伟达计算能力来规避美国的出口禁令。英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，美国正在堵住这一漏洞。一项调查还揭示了中国如何通过围绕模型蒸馏建立的整个行业来缓解长达数年的芯片禁运。

多年来，美国一直试图通过严格的出口管制来阻止中国进口先进人工智能处理器。中国公司的回应是利用完全合法的漏洞，通过从被允许接收美国硬件的外国数据中心进行基于云的远程访问来租用他们所需的计算能力。

美国商务部工业与安全局 (BIS) 现在希望通过一项临时规则来终止这一解决办法。它将远程访问规则与现有的物理出口禁令保持一致。据彭博社报道，新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西的数据中心运营商需要获得美国政府许可才能从 Nvidia 等美国制造商购买先进的人工智能芯片。申请将根据具体情况进行审核。

总部位于美国的公司的子公司不受许可证要求的约束，向仅运行在线零售商或社交媒体平台的商业推荐系统的数据中心的货物也不受许可证要求的约束。这些规则一旦在联邦公报上公布即生效。消息公布后，英伟达股价下跌 2.9%，费城半导体指数下跌 5.5%。

### 非法筹码转移和黄仁勋的垮台

不过，政治导火索是涉嫌非法走私物理芯片。这项新规定是在英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋突然辞职几天后出台的，黄仁勋承认与新加坡 Megaspeed International 前经理 Alice Huang 有染。美国当局怀疑现居住在中国的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 从事间谍活动。据报道，在与 Megaspeed 有关的一个中国数据中心发现了被禁的 Nvidia 芯片后，他们正在调查 Megaspeed 是否可能违反出口管制。 Megaspeed 否认有任何不当行为，唐纳德·特朗普总统周一表示，黄仁勋没有损害国家安全。

该丑闻仍在华盛顿因芯片制裁执行不力而引发公开的权力斗争。据 Axios 称，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克推迟了特朗普授权的打击非法芯片转移的措施，促使财政部长斯科特·贝森特公开指责他不作为。美国商务部现在的声明异常直白地指出，该规则草案是由财政部和国家安全委员会起草并在其指导下制定的。

### 路透社调查绘制中国蒸馏行业地图

路透社的另一项独家调查显示了中国开发商如何应对多年来顶级国产硬件的短缺。通过审查 300 多篇中国论文、专利、招聘信息和政府文件，路透社首次展示了中国对模型蒸馏作为权宜之计的依赖程度。几年前开始的一种学术解决方法已经发展成为一个具有高度发达分工的工业部门。

该技术并不需要像 Nvidia 这样强大的芯片，但它极大地减少了开发人员自己的计算负载，因为对美国教师模型的一次昂贵的查询取代了重复的计算。中国公司现在开发自己的软件，自动从美国领先模型中提取答案、代码和问题解决方案。然后，专业工人处理这些材料来训练更小、更便宜的当地学生模型。

研究论文表明这种做法已经深入人心。早在2024年11月，上海交通大学的研究人员就为阿里巴巴的Qwen2.5-72B创建了10750个训练样本。他们借鉴了 OpenAI o1 的约 5,000 条回复和 GPT-4o mini 的翻译，尽管他们自己当时警告称，对外部创新的依赖迫在眉睫。阿里巴巴于 2025 年 4 月描述了其系统地使用 GPT-4 和 GPT-4o 来进行外语训练数据。2026 年 2 月，交通大学和食品配送公司美团使用 GPT-4o 来训练用于协调编码代理的较小模型。

来自北京的政策指令正在推动这一增长。政府希望在中国制造业部署更小、低成本的人工智能系统。政府官方文件并没有直接指示任何人复制美国模式。尽管如此，八个部委在一月份发布的“人工智能+制造”一揽子计划以及上海和深圳的举措明确推广了蒸馏和其他减少计算需求的技术。在实践中，这种国家驱动的效率推动促使中国开发者大规模利用最强大的美国模型作为数据源。

在深圳亚太经合组织峰会召开之前，这种工业规模的做法正在成为地缘政治的热点。蒸馏并不违法，但它违反了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等美国开发商的服务条款。两家公司长期以来一直对中国人工智能实验室提出指控，在详细报告中记录大量提取的数据并部署技术对策。 Anthropic 最近表示，它现在成功阻止了大多数此类蒸馏攻击。我们关于中国型号的前沿雷达#4 也涵盖了这些指控。

据路透社报道，美国官员早在 7 月就在成都与中国监管机构对峙，因为华盛顿认为大规模蒸馏是中国人工智能快速追赶的主要原因。中国内部人士还指出了他们自己在算法和模型设计方面的进步。财政部长贝森特现在威胁说，如果秘密蒸馏攻击越界成为知识产权盗窃行为，将实施制裁并指定实体名单。中国开发商对这些规则并不确定，最近要求北京工业部提供有关使用外国模式的明确指导方针。

title: How Jensen Huang’s family shaped Nvidia’s Singapore dealings
title_en: How Jensen Huang’s family shaped Nvidia’s Singapore dealings

inline_images.caption: Nico Caprez, who recently married Madison Huang, is a Swiss former professional skier who joined Nvidia in 2024 © Jacquelyn Martin/AP
inline_images.alt: Nico Caprez, who recently married Madison Huang, is a Swiss former professional skier who joined Nvidia in 2024 © Jacquelyn Martin/AP

inline_images.caption: Jensen Huang’s family, from left, his daughter Madison, wife Lori and son Spencer at an event in 2007 © Thu Hoang Ly/MediaNews Group via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: Jensen Huang’s family, from left, his daughter Madison, wife Lori and son Spencer at an event in 2007 © Thu Hoang Ly/MediaNews Group via Getty Images

inline_images.caption: Madison and her brother Spencer, who ran a bar before joining the company in 2022 and is now a director © An Rong Xu/Bloomberg
inline_images.alt: Madison and her brother Spencer, who ran a bar before joining the company in 2022 and is now a director © An Rong Xu/Bloomberg

author: Michael Acton, Stephen Morris, and Joshua Franklin
article_content:
Jensen Huang’s daughter was closely involved in orchestrating the public defence of Nvidia’s relationship with the Singapore-based company at the heart of the scandal that led to her father’s resignation as CEO.

Madison Huang, a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, assumed a broader role outside her formal remit, helping to direct the company’s response to increasing press scrutiny of Megaspeed, the Singaporean cloud provider, according to three people familiar with the matter.

As the $3.8tn chip giant’s relationship with the little-known company first started to draw attention late last year, Nico Caprez, a fellow executive at Nvidia whom Madison Huang recently married, was promoted to a role that covered international deals with cloud computing clients in Asia, the people said.

The former Nvidia CEO’s decision to install family members in senior roles at what was until recently the world’s most valuable public company had caused some concerns over governance even before Huang resigned last week, according to current and former employees.

Caprez and Madison Huang’s links to Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed will heighten scrutiny of the pair as Nvidia’s board conducts a probe, which is being handled by a former top US prosecutor.

“They had a lot of power and influence and were allowed to operate unchecked,” said one colleague. “No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”

Megaspeed, which has been under US investigation since 2024 over whether it was involved in smuggling chips to China in violation of American export controls, is at the centre of questions about Nvidia in the wake of Jensen Huang’s departure. On Tuesday, Nvidia’s board established a new committee to oversee compliance with US national security and export rules.

The Singapore company in total bought roughly $5bn of Nvidia hardware.

Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify about Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed — which has financial ties to China’s Alibaba — before Congress at a closed-door session in December.

The former Nvidia CEO has agreed to appear before the House committees on foreign affairs, intelligence and China for transcribed interviews on December 1.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” said the committee chairs Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford in a joint statement on Tuesday.

Nvidia general counsel Teter is expected to appear before the committees on December 2.

Treasury secretary Scott Bessent has, meanwhile, faulted commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and his department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed. The commerce department has delayed new inclusions on the blacklist.

The FT has reported that US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who officials believe is a Chinese spy. That affair, as well as a second alleged relationship with a subordinate at Nvidia, precipitated the founder’s resignation last week after 33 years in charge.

The first reports on Megaspeed were published in The New York Times in October 2025, saying that commerce officials were probing its potential ties to China.

That autumn, Madison Huang started to involve herself directly in the tech giant’s communications response to questions about Nvidia’s chip sales to Megaspeed, the people said.

Madison Huang was seen talking to Alice Huang at an event in Taipei in 2025

Madison Huang had already, in the spring of 2025, privately hired crisis PR firm Heller for the family. The firm is well-known for handling high-profile individuals involved in sexual misconduct scandals, such as former congressman Anthony Weiner.

In the autumn, Heller then started to work directly for Nvidia.

Around the same time, Madison Huang temporarily excluded one of Nvidia’s top corporate communications executives from the group of people inside Nvidia who were discussing how to respond to queries about Megaspeed. The remaining group involved in crafting their responses included Nvidia general counsel Teter.

Nvidia told The New York Times at the time that it had visited its customer’s facilities multiple times and concluded it had no shareholders from China, and found no evidence of chip smuggling.

That same October, Madison Huang’s then partner and future husband, Caprez, who joined the company in 2024, was promoted to a director role overseeing Nvidia’s work with international cloud partners.

Two people said Caprez flew to Asia to oversee deals with cloud providers in the region and had been involved in deals with Asian cloud partners months before his official title changed. Megaspeed was one of Nvidia’s largest customers in south-east Asia.

By January of this year, Caprez — a Swiss former professional skier and consultant, who met Madison Huang when both were studying at London Business School — had been promoted yet again to vice-president of global AI infrastructure growth.

Nvidia, representatives for the Huang family and Heller declined to comment. Nvidia has previously stated that it added Megaspeed to its “block list” in June 2025, “prohibiting any further sales or shipments”.

The rapid advancement of Huang’s daughter and son-in-law alarmed some inside Nvidia. Several current and former employees said Madison was also difficult to work with.

Not all employees agreed with that assessment. One current Nvidia employee who worked closely with Madison Huang said her advancement reflected her talent and understanding of technical detail that resulted from “growing up inside Nvidia”.

Nor was her relatively undefined role compared with her job title unusual, they said, given Nvidia’s flat organisational structure, which leads to people unofficially taking on different roles.

Madison Huang has worked at Nvidia since 2020, initially joining as an intern in enterprise marketing and strategy, according to her LinkedIn profile. Before Nvidia, she trained as a chef and worked in Paris for LVMH in marketing and development.

She was promoted to her current role of senior director of product marketing for physical AI in 2025.

Jensen Huang’s son, Spencer Huang, has been an Nvidia employee since July 2022 and is currently a director of product management in its robots division. He ran a bar prior to his role at Nvidia.

Beyond Jensen Huang’s roughly 3.5 per cent stake in Nvidia, the founder now has no formal role. He has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and acknowledged that his actions had hurt his wife and children.

Interim CEO Colette Kress is tasked with running the chipmaker at the heart of the AI boom and will oversee a business with about 40,000 employees, including Madison, her husband and brother.

“The new CEO is going to have to look at them like you would look at any other employee and see if they are an asset to the company or not,” said Nell Minow of ValueEdge Advisors, a corporate governance consulting firm.

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋的女儿密切参与了策划对Nvidia与那家新加坡公司的关系的公开辩护，而这家公司正是导致其父辞去首席执行官职务的丑闻的核心。

据三位知情人士透露，英伟达产品营销高级总监Madison Huang承担了超出其正式职责范围的更广泛角色，协助指导公司应对媒体对新加坡云服务提供商Megaspeed日益严苛的审查。

随着英伟达董事会正在进行一项由美国前高级检察官处理的调查，卡普雷兹和麦迪逊黄与英伟达与 Megaspeed 关系的联系将加强对两人的审查。

“他们拥有很大的权力和影响力，并且可以不受限制地运作，”一位同事说。 “没有人能对他们说‘不’，也没有人能把他们安置在自己的位置上。”

Megaspeed 自 2024 年以来一直受到美国调查，原因是该公司是否涉嫌违反美国出口管制向中国走私芯片，在黄仁勋离职后，该公司成为了有关英伟达的质疑的焦点。周二，英伟达董事会成立了一个新委员会，负责监督美国国家安全和出口规则的遵守情况。

这家新加坡公司总共购买了大约 50 亿美元的 Nvidia 硬件。

黄仁勋被传唤在 12 月的国会闭门会议上就 Nvidia 与 Megaspeed 的关系作证，Megaspeed 与中国阿里巴巴有财务关系。

这位英伟达前首席执行官已同意于 12 月 1 日出席众议院外交事务、情报和中国委员会，接受录音采访。

委员会主席布莱恩·马斯特（Brian Mast）、约翰·穆伦纳尔（John Moolenaar）和里克·克劳福德（Rick Crawford）周二发表联合声明称：“我们期待听取黄仁勋和蒂姆·蒂特尔（Tim Teter）就他们在潜在的国家安全违规事件中所扮演的角色发表意见。”

英伟达首席法务官Teter预计将于12月2日出席委员会听证会。

与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特指责商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克及其部门未能将Megaspeed列入黑名单。商务部已推迟

2025 年，Madison Huang 在台北的一次活动中与 Alice Huang 交谈

2025 年春天，麦迪逊·黄 (Madison Huang) 已为家族私人聘请了危机公关公司 Heller。该公司因处理涉及不当性行为丑闻的知名人士而闻名，例如前国会议员安东尼·韦纳。

今年秋天，海勒开始直接为 Nvidia 工作。

大约在同一时间，麦迪逊·黄（Madison Huang）暂时将 Nvidia 的一位企业通讯高管排除在 Nvidia 内部讨论如何回应有关 Megaspeed 询问的人员之外。参与制定回应的其余小组包括英伟达总法律顾问泰特。

英伟达当时告诉《纽约时报》，它已多次访问其客户的工厂，得出的结论是，该公司没有来自中国的股东，也没有发现芯片走私的证据。

同年 10 月，麦迪逊·黄 (Madison Huang) 的时任合伙人、未来的丈夫卡普雷兹 (Caprez) 于 2024 年加入公司，被晋升为总监，负责监督 Nvidia 与国际云合作伙伴的合作。

两名知情人士称，卡普雷斯飞往亚洲监督与该地区云提供商的交易，并在其正式头衔变更前几个月就参与了与亚洲云合作伙伴的交易。 Megaspeed 是 Nvidia 在东南亚最大的客户之一。

今年 1 月，卡普雷兹（Caprez）——一位瑞士前职业滑雪运动员和顾问，在伦敦商学院学习时认识了麦迪逊·黄（Madison Huang）——再次晋升为全球人工智能基础设施发展副总裁。

英伟达、黄氏家族和海勒的代表均拒绝置评。英伟达此前曾表示，已于 2025 年 6 月将 Megaspeed 添加到“黑名单”中，“禁止进一步销售或发货”。

黄的女儿和女婿的快速晋升让英伟达内部的一些人感到震惊。几位现任和前任员工表示，麦迪逊也很难共事。

并非所有员工都同意这一评估。一位与 Madison Huang 密切合作的 Nvidia 现任员工表示，她的晋升反映了她“在 Nvidia 内部成长”的天赋和对技术细节的理解。

他们表示，与她的职位相比，她的角色相对不明确也并不罕见，因为英伟达的组织结构是扁平的，这导致人们非正式地担任不同的角色。

根据她的 LinkedIn 资料，Madison Huang 自 2020 年以来一直在 Nvidia 工作，最初是作为企业营销和战略实习生加入的。在加入 Nvidia 之前，她接受过厨师培训，并在巴黎的 LVMH 从事营销和开发工作。

2025 年，她晋升为目前的物理人工智能产品营销高级总监。

黄仁勋的儿子 Spencer Huang 自 2022 年 7 月起一直是 Nvidia 员工，目前担任其机器人部门的产品管理总监。在加入 Nvidia 之前，他经营一家酒吧。

除了黄仁勋持有 Nvidia 约 3.5% 的股份外，这位创始人目前没有正式的职位。他承认对妻子不忠，并承认自己的行为伤害了妻子和孩子。

临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 的任务是运营这家处于人工智能热潮核心的芯片制造商，并将管理一家拥有约 4 万名员工的企业，其中包括麦迪逊、她的丈夫和兄弟。

公司治理咨询公司 ValueEdge Advisors 的内尔·米诺 (Nell Minow) 表示：“新任首席执行官必须像对待任何其他员工一样审视他们，看看他们是否是公司的资产。”

title: Uber and Zipline’s drone delivery service takes off in Texas, with dozens of cities to follow
title_en: Uber and Zipline’s drone delivery service takes off in Texas, with dozens of cities to follow
author: Kirsten Korosec
article_content:
Uber Eats customers in a Houston suburb can now have their food delivered by a Zipline drone, the first commercial launch under a partnership announced earlier this year between Uber and the autonomous drone delivery startup.

The commercial partnership kicks off Tuesday in Spring, Texas, before expanding to Dallas. But the companies have far larger ambitions. Uber and Zipline plan to launch drone delivery services in dozens of additional U.S. cities in their collective bid to make one million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

Zipline’s long-range autonomous delivery drones will be used to shuttle food orders weighing up to eight pounds to Uber Eats customers, flying about 300 feet above the ground at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. Zipline drones don’t land. Instead, the drones lower the orders, which are encased in a small protective pod, to the customer’s location using a tether.

Uber Eats customers in service areas will be able to tap a new “drone” icon on the app’s home page to view all participating restaurants. Uber said that at launch in the Houston area, several nationwide chains, including Jersey Mike’s and Zaxby’s, along with dozens of local restaurants such as Urban Bird and Abu Omar Halal, will offer drone delivery.

“In partnership with Uber Eats we’re going to create a new expectation for delivery in America,” Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said in a statement that underscores those aspirations.

Those nationwide goals mirror the ambitions of other drone delivery companies, including Alphabet-owned Wing and Amazon’s Prime Air service. And those plans have started to collide with concerns from residents in some locations who complain about noise and worry that the drones will disrupt wildlife and pose a risk to safety and privacy.

Companies trying to scale in this nascent industry have argued that delivery via drone is a net benefit for society, citing advantages such as traffic reduction. Customers won’t need to hop in their cars and drive to the store for that forgotten item or takeout order, instead relying on a drone, industry proponents have said.

And while Zipline and other companies have been developing their drones for years, the industry is still in its early days, as is adoption in the communities where services are available.

Zipline, which was founded in 2014, has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software. The California-based company’s initial focus was delivering blood in Rwanda, but it eventually expanded its scope to the United States. Its business in the U.S. scaled quickly after receiving its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration in 2022, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to conduct long-range commercial drone deliveries.

Uber’s partnership extends beyond a commercial relationship with Zipline. The ride-hailing giant also invested in the startup. Neither company has disclosed the investment amount, but Zipline announced last week it had raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, and included backing by Uber, among others.

article_content_zh:
休斯敦郊区的 Uber Eats 优食顾客现在可以使用 Zipline 无人机送货，这是 Uber 与自动无人机送货初创公司今年早些时候宣布的合作伙伴关系的首次商业推出。

商业合作关系于周二在德克萨斯州斯普林市启动，然后扩展到达拉斯。但这些公司有着更大的野心。 Uber 和 Zipline 计划在美国另外数十个城市推出无人机送货服务，共同争取到 2029 年底使用这家初创公司的无人机每天完成 100 万次送货。

Zipline 的远程自动送货无人机将用于将重达 8 磅的食品订单运送给 Uber Eats 优食客户，飞行距离地面约 300 英尺，速度高达每小时 70 英里。滑索无人机不会着陆。相反，无人机使用系绳将包裹在一个小型保护吊舱中的订单降低到客户的位置。

服务区域的 Uber Eats 优食顾客将能够点击应用程序主页上的新“无人机”图标来查看所有参与的餐厅。 Uber 表示，在休斯顿地区推出时，包括 Jersey Mike’s 和 Zaxby’s 在内的几家全国连锁店，以及 Urban Bird 和 Abu Omar Halal 等数十家当地餐厅，将提供无人机送货服务。

Zipline 首席执行官兼联合创始人凯勒·克利夫顿 (Keller Cliffton) 在一份强调这些愿望的声明中表示：“通过与 Uber Eats 优食合作，我们将为美国的配送创造新的期望。”

这些全国性目标反映了其他无人机送货公司的雄心，包括 Alphabet 旗下的 Wing 和亚马逊的 Prime Air 服务。这些计划已经开始与一些地方居民的担忧发生冲突，他们抱怨噪音，并担心无人机会扰乱野生动物并对安全和隐私构成风险。

试图在这个新兴行业扩大规模的公司认为，通过无人机送货对社会来说是一项净效益，并列举了减少交通量等优势。行业支持者表示，顾客不再需要开车去商店购买遗忘的商品或外卖订单，而是依靠无人机。

尽管 Zipline 和其他公司多年来一直在开发无人机，但该行业仍处于早期阶段，在提供服务的社区中的采用也是如此。

Zipline 成立于 2014 年，开发了一个无人机送货生态系统，其中包括飞机、发射和着陆系统以及物流软件。这家总部位于加州的公司最初的重点是在卢旺达提供血液，但最终将业务范围扩大到美国。 2022 年获得美国联邦航空管理局第 135 部分航空承运人认证后，该公司在美国的业务迅速扩大，这是授权该公司进行远程商用无人机交付的一个关键监管障碍。

Uber 的合作伙伴关系超出了与 Zipline 的商业关系。这家叫车巨头也投资了这家初创公司。两家公司均未披露投资金额，但 Zipline 上周宣布，已在 Paradigm、WCM Investment Management 和 Layer Global 领投的一轮融资中筹集了 15 亿美元，并得到了 Uber 等公司的支持。

title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
title_en: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed

inline_images.caption: The gavel in front of the DOJ seal.
inline_images.alt: The gavel in front of the DOJ seal.

author: Stevie Bonifield
article_content:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.

“While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting,” the departments said in a statement issued Monday evening. The departments acknowledged there’s been “significant public attention” on Megaspeed.

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week after reports he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, who Megaspeed says left the company in August 2025. The scandal has raised questions about national security, and sparked scrutiny of Nvidia’s handling of exports of its chips to China and Megaspeed’s possible role in moving along Nvidia’s chips.

Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed “came to a sudden halt” late last year after its investigators received an email from Nvidia’s general counsel, claiming Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler gave Nvidia permission to reach out. The case was then “quickly” handed over to the DOJ, according to the Times.

The announcement today says the DOJ took the “lead role” in the investigation last year:

The statement doesn’t go into detail about the current status of the case, but it says the DOJ and Commerce Department “will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.”

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次调查将供应链合规性锚点从芯片分销商前移至数据中心运营商，标志着美方对高性能算力基础设施的“长臂管辖”已进入深水区。对Megaspeed的穿透式审计，将实质性重构东南亚算力基建商的合规风控成本，并可能迫使Nvidia及类似半导体巨头全面重组其海外渠道准入标准。

article_content_zh:
美国司法部和商务部表示，他们正在调查总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司 Megaspeed，该公司与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的辞职有关，此前有报道称调查已于去年停止。

这些部门在周一晚间发布的一份声明中表示：“虽然我们通常不会对正在进行的调查发表评论，但提供事实并解决公开报告中流传的不准确信息符合公共利益。”这些部门承认 Megaspeed 受到了“公众的高度关注”。

黄上周辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前有报道称，他与 Megaspeed 前高管、被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 有染，Megaspeed 称黄爱丽于 2025 年 8 月离开了公司。这一丑闻引发了有关国家安全的质疑，并引发了对英伟达处理其向中国芯片出口以及 Megaspeed 在运送 Nvidia 芯片方面可能发挥的作用的审查。

本月早些时候，《纽约时报》报道称，去年年底，商务部对 Megaspeed 的调查“突然停止”，原因是调查人员收到了英伟达总法律顾问的一封电子邮件，声称商务部官员杰弗里·凯斯勒允许英伟达进行接触。据《泰晤士报》报道，此案随后“迅速”移交给司法部。

> 在通过主动监控潜在的敏感半导体转移来识别可疑活动后，美国商务部于 2024 年启动了对 Megaspeed 潜在违反出口管制行为的调查。 2025 年 5 月，美国商务部调查人员要求 Nvidia 提供有关直接或间接向 Megaspeed 销售的记录。 2025 年 6 月，Nvidia 将 Megaspeed 列入“禁止出售”名单。根据商务部的调查，商务部工业和安全局的特工与新加坡执法官员一起，于 2025 年 6 月对 Megaspeed 进行了现场、亲自的最终用途检查，并采访了首席执行官 Alice Huang。此次执法行动之后，司法部牵头对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查。

声明没有详细说明案件目前的进展情况，但表示司法部和商务部“将对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。

title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
title_en: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO

inline_images.caption: Nvidia_Jensen_huang_04
inline_images.alt: Nvidia_Jensen_huang_04

author: Jay Peters
article_content:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company’s board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.”

More than 193,000 people, including CEOs like Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, have signed a letter to “bring Jensen back.” President Trump has also been supportive of Huang returning as CEO, saying yesterday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea.” (Trump had earlier tossed out former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a potential replacement.) On Monday, Nvidia’s board reportedly was “not considering” having Huang return, and today, CNN reported that the board is “not considering reinstating Huang.”

Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
