title: NHS data contract to stay with controversial US tech giant Palantir until 2029
title_en: NHS data contract to stay with controversial US tech giant Palantir until 2029
author: Hugh Pym
article_content:
The government says it will continue a key NHS data contract in England with the controversial US tech giant Palantir until 2029, rather than triggering an early release clause next year.

But ministers are inviting British firms to bid for the contract from 2029, with a procurement programme beginning next summer.

A Commons Committee had called on the government to part ways and appoint a company "more compatible with UK values". Protesters regularly target Palantir over Israel's use of its technology in the Gaza conflict and oppose its use in US immigration enforcement.

The £330m deal, which began in 2024 to help manage hospital waiting lists in England, was due to run until 2031.

### 'Albatross around the NHS's neck'

The prime minister had faced pressure from some Labour MPs to cut ties with Palantir. They said they were extremely disappointed by the decision, calling the contract "an albatross" hanging around the NHS's neck.

The Liberal Democrats said the deal was "dangerous".

There have also been concerns raised about how patient data will be used.

Palantir, which was co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, has interests in US defence and security, and has contracts with the Israeli military.

Health minister James Frith said the move was "not about the politics of executives of suppliers, nor is it about the territories or customers that one company or one supplier makes".

The government says UK companies will be encouraged to tender to avoid overdependence on one supplier.

The timeframe is not fast enough for some members of the government.

Dame Chi Onwurah, Labour MP for Newcastle upon Tyne Central and West, said the government needed to "act urgently" to procure "credible domestic alternatives".

"The government should not wait two years, it must start reducing this dependency now," she said.

Former Labour shadow chancellor John McDonnell went further, and accused Palantir of "human rights abuses". He said his constituents in Hayes and Harlington "expect the contract to be ended".

Liberal Democrat health spokeswoman Helen Morgan criticised the company for what she called its "appalling human rights record, run by an ally of Donald Trump".

The British Medical Association, which represents doctors, said it was glad the government had shown it was listening to its concerns about Palantir, but was frustrated the process of changing to another company was further delayed.

Palantir UK said it was right to press forward with the programme which was exceeding targets.

"We are proud of our work to date to help deliver more operations, speed up discharge and reduce the time patients need to wait to find out if they have cancer," Palantir UK senior vice-president Tom Watson said.

article_content_zh:
英国政府表示，将继续与备受争议的美国科技巨头 Palantir 签订英国 NHS 关键数据合同，直至 2029 年，而不是在明年触发提前释放条款。

但部长们正在邀请英国公司从 2029 年开始竞标该合同，采购计划将于明年夏天开始。

下议院委员会呼吁政府分道扬镳，任命一家“更符合英国价值观”的公司。抗议者经常因为以色列在加沙冲突中使用 Palantir 技术而针对 Palantir，并反对将其用于美国移民执法。

这笔价值 3.3 亿英镑的交易于 2024 年开始，旨在帮助管理英格兰的医院候诊名单，预计将持续到 2031 年。

### “NHS脖子上的信天翁”

首相面临一些工党议员的压力，要求其切断与 Palantir 的关系。他们表示对这一决定非常失望，称这份合同是挂在国民医疗服务体系脖子上的“沉重负担”。

自由民主党称该协议“危险”。

人们还担心如何使用患者数据。

Palantir 由亿万富翁 Peter Thiel 联合创立，在美国国防和安全领域拥有利益，并与以色列军方签订了合同。

卫生部长詹姆斯·弗里斯表示，此举“与供应商高管的政治无关，也与一家公司或一家供应商的领土或客户无关”。

政府表示，将鼓励英国公司进行投标，以避免过度依赖一家供应商。

对于一些政府成员来说，这个时间框架还不够快。

泰恩河畔纽卡斯尔中部和西部工党议员 Chi Onwurah 女士表示，政府需要“紧急采取行动”，以寻求“可靠的国内替代方案”。

“政府不应该等两年，必须现在就开始减少这种依赖，”她说。

前工党影子财政大臣约翰·麦克唐纳 (John McDonnell) 更进一步，指责 Palantir “侵犯人权”。他表示，海耶斯和哈灵顿的选民“预计合同将被终止”。

自由民主党卫生发言人海伦·摩根批评该公司“由唐纳德·特朗普的盟友经营，其人权记录令人震惊”。

代表医生的英国医学协会表示，很高兴政府表明正在倾听其对 Palantir 的担忧，但对更换到另一家公司的过程进一步推迟感到沮丧。

Palantir UK 表示，推进该计划是正确的，该计划已经超出了目标。

Palantir UK 高级副总裁 Tom Watson 表示：“迄今为止，我们为帮助开展更多手术、加快出院速度并减少患者发现是否患有癌症所需等待的时间所做的工作感到自豪。”

克服人类大脑极限的探索已经超越了科幻小说的范围。从渐进式大脑替换到将记忆上传到云端，研究人员和技术人员正在探索扩展人类认知的激进方法。今天，《麻省理工科技评论》在现场圆桌讨论中审视了这些想法。

与科学编辑玛丽·贝丝·格里格斯和生物医学高级编辑安东尼奥·雷加拉多一起探索认知永生可能是什么样子，以及我们离实现它有多近。

我梳理了互联网，为您找到当今最有趣/最重要/最可怕/最迷人的技术故事。

1 美国正在加强对中国远程获取人工智能芯片的控制，堵住了中国企业在海外获取美国芯片的漏洞。 （美联社）+ 习近平可能会在本周与特朗普举行峰会之前进行报复。 （彭博社 $）+ Nvidia 警告客户不要向中国出租芯片。 (CNBC) + 中国正在扩大人工智能提炼，以解决限制措施。 （路透社$）+ Nvidia私下表示可以追踪芯片运往中国。 （麻省理工科技评论）

2 美国超大型数据中心的二氧化碳排放量与丹麦一样多 一项新研究发现，2018 年至 2025 年间排放量增加了两倍。 (Verge) + 400 个数据中心的用电量比密歇根州还多。 (连线 $) + 各国希望利用人工智能来减少排放。 （自然）+ 但人工智能模型很快就会成为气候危机的否认者。 （监护人）

3 加州就流氓人工智能黑客事件起诉 OpenAI 总检察长称该公司未能保护公众。 ( FT $) + 并且承认了80起模型失控的案例。 (CNBC) + 当人工智能代理失控时，谁该承担责任？ （麻省理工科技评论）

4 最高法院驳回了特朗普削减研究经费的提议，下级法院认为此举可能侵犯了言论自由权。 （哥伦比亚广播公司）+ 特朗普对美国科学造成了沉重打击。 （麻省理工科技评论）

5 美国主要银行遭遇大范围的在线中断 数千名客户报告账户访问问题。 (Gizmodo) + 联合航空航班单独停电延误。 （路透社$）

6 Alice Huang 的丈夫在中国建立了一个数据中心帝国 当他的妻子追求 Nvidia 芯片时，他赢得了政府的支持。 ( WSJ $) + MAGA 正在利用这一丑闻来削弱特朗普与大型科技公司的关系。 （阿克西奥斯）

7 一名儿童在基因编辑试验中死亡后，中国解雇了一名科学家。这名女孩在 2025 年接受实验性治疗后死亡。（《自然》） + 初创公司希望制定基因编辑新规则。 （麻省理工科技评论）

8 美国的电动汽车热潮在没有汽车购买者的情况下发生 送货车队、机器人出租车和警车正在转向电动。 （大西洋$）

9 新的宇宙数据挑战了我们的宇宙模型 研究结果表明暗能量可能正在减弱。 （广达）

10 一个佛教教派计划为硅谷打造一位人工智能大师 它希望创建一个基于集体思维的模型。 （《纽约客》$）

—Counterpoint Research 研究副总裁尼尔·沙阿 (Neil Shah) 告诉路透社，华盛顿在减缓中国人工智能野心的行动中开辟了一条新战线。

肯尼亚大裂谷拥有五个地热发电站，这些发电站利用蒸汽云产生该国约四分之一的电力。但一些能量逃逸到大气中，而更多的能量则由于缺乏需求而留在地下。这就是明锐碳纤维来到这里的原因。

去年，这家初创公司开始利用一些多余的能源来去除空气中的二氧化碳。该公司表示，该方法高效、经济，而且最重要的是可扩展。但该项目也面临激烈的反对。

我们仍然可以拥有美好的事物

+ 一只作为孤儿被救并重新野化的大猩猩现在已经有了自己的孩子。 + 不列颠哥伦比亚省基洛纳选举了一名竞选市议会议员的人作为笑话。 + 欧几里得太空望远镜的大量新数据覆盖了令人惊叹的天空区域和 9 亿个星系。 + 科学家重现了侏罗纪昆虫久违的鸣叫声，营造出 1.65 亿年前的音景。

( AP ) + Xi may retaliate ahead of this week’s summit with Trump. ( Bloomberg $) + Nvidia is warning customers against renting chips to China. ( CNBC ) + China is expanding AI distillation to work around curbs. ( Reuters $) + Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

( Wired $) + Nations want to harness AI to cut emissions. ( Nature ) + But AI models can quickly become climate crisis deniers. ( Guardian )

3 California has sued OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents The attorney general said the company failed to protect the public. ( FT $) + And that it admitted to 80 cases of losing control of models. ( CNBC ) + Who’s liable when AI agents go rogue? ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Alice Huang’s husband built a data-center empire in China He won government backing as his wife pursued Nvidia chips. ( WSJ $) + MAGA is using the scandal to weaken Trump’s Big Tech ties. ( Axios )

8 America’s EV boom is happening without car buyers Delivery fleets, robotaxis, and police cars are going electric. ( Atlantic $)

9 New cosmic data has challenged our model of the universe The findings suggest dark energy may be weakening. ( Quanta )

10 A Buddhist sect plans to build an AI guru for Silicon Valley It wants to create a model based on a collective mind. ( New Yorker $)

—Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, tells Reuters that Washington has opened a new front in its campaign to slow China’s AI ambitions.

Kenya’s Great Rift Valley is home to five geothermal power stations, which harness clouds of steam to generate about a quarter of the country’s electricity. But some of the energy escapes into the atmosphere, while even more remains underground for lack of demand. That’s what brought Octavia Carbon here.

Last year, the startup began harnessing some of that excess energy to remove CO2 from the air. The company says the method is efficient, affordable, and—crucially—scalable. But the project also faces fierce opposition.

BRUSSELS, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The European Union tech regulator charged Chinese e-commerce giant Temu on Tuesday for not doing enough to stop the sale of illegal products on its platform in breach of online content rules, putting it at risk of a second hefty fine.

The European Commission, which acts as the tech regulator for the 27-country bloc, said Temu's mitigation measures "include ineffective controls to check the compliance of products; a weak content moderation system; and an ineffective sanction system".

A spokesperson for Temu said the company disagreed with the Commission's preliminary findings and that the company makes significant efforts to mitigate illegal product risk. The e-commerce giant will respond to the Commission, he said.

"We are confident that we will reach an amicable resolution of the matter that fully addresses the Commission's remaining concerns," the spokesperson said.

The Commission said that Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, has the possibility to exercise its rights to defence and reply to its preliminary findings.

If the Commission's findings were ultimately confirmed, it would adopt a "non-compliance decision", which would trigger a fine of up to 6% of the company's annual worldwide turnover.

Such a fine would be the second imposed on Temu, after a €200 million ($220.12 million) penalty in May in the first part of an investigation opened two years ago under the Digital Services Act that requires large online companies to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content on their platforms.

The earlier fine was for not assessing the risks of sales of illegal products, while Tuesday's charges were for not taking adequate measures to stop such sales.

The Commission said last month it had accepted Temu's action plan to remedy the breach that had triggered the existing fine.

Temu, along with Shein and other e-commerce platforms, has also been hit by the EU imposing €3 fees on low-value e-commerce packages since the start of July. Parcels worth less than €150 previously entered the bloc duty-free.

路透布鲁塞尔11月17日 - 欧盟科技监管机构周二指控中国电子商务巨头Temu未采取足够措施阻止其平台上销售非法产品，违反了在线内容规则，使其面临第二次巨额罚款。

作为 27 个国家集团的技术监管机构的欧盟委员会表示，Temu 的缓解措施“包括检查产品合规性的无效控制、薄弱的内容审核系统以及无效的制裁系统”。

Temu 的发言人表示，该公司不同意委员会的初步调查结果，并表示该公司为降低非法产品风险做出了重大努力。他表示，这家电子商务巨头将向委员会做出回应。

该发言人表示：“我们相信，我们将就此事达成友好解决方案，充分解决委员会剩余的关切。”

委员会表示，PDD Holdings 旗下的 Temu 有可能行使其辩护权，并对初步调查结果作出答复。

如果委员会的调查结果最终得到证实，它将采取“不合规决定”，这将引发高达该公司全球年营业额 6% 的罚款。

此类罚款将是 Temu 面临的第二次罚款，此前两年前根据《数字服务法》展开的调查第一部分在 5 月处以 2 亿欧元（2.2012 亿美元）罚款，该调查要求大型在线公司采取更多措施处理其平台上的非法和有害内容。

早些时候的罚款是因为没有评估非法产品销售的风险，而周二的指控是因为没有采取适当措施阻止此类销售。

该委员会上个月表示，它已接受 Temu 的行动计划，以纠正引发现有罚款的违规行为。

自 7 月初以来，Temu 以及 Shein 和其他电子商务平台也受到了欧盟对低价值电子商务套餐征收 3 欧元费用的打击。此前，价值低于 150 欧元的包裹可免税进入欧盟。

title: Apple Watch’s New AI Features Hear Your Conversations But Miss the Point
title_en: Apple Watch’s New AI Features Hear Your Conversations But Miss the Point
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Apple’s AI-powered “Audio Intelligence” technology for the Apple Watch is rolling out into beta testing on Tuesday, initially for developers in the iOS 27.3 update, after first being announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine hardware event in September. The technology includes a set of four opt-in AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes.

The news was first announced via an emailed press release sent out by Apple’s communications team in India early on Tuesday. The update rolled out in the U.S. and other markets later in the day.

The sound recognition feature will help deaf and hard-of-hearing users identify important sounds like sirens, alarms, or doorbells from their watch, while the song recognition feature taps into Apple’s Shazam app to detect music playing in the background and identify the song name and artist.

However, the more potentially controversial features are those that listen to human conversations: Live Rewind and Siri Recaps.

Given the backlash to AI recording devices, like Meta’s AI glasses and other AI wearables, Apple has attempted to carve out a space where the features can be useful to Apple Watch owners, while still respecting the privacy of those around them.

With Live Rewind, the idea is to let you go back in time to see what someone just said, in case you missed it. For instance, if someone was giving you verbal directions or reading a long list of specials at a restaurant, you could double-press on the Watch’s digital crown to see what was said in the last 15 seconds as a text snippet displayed on the watch face. You can view this snippet and then do nothing, and it will disappear permanently. Or you can save it to the stand-alone Siri app that shipped with iOS 27 for later access, which might be helpful if you’re trying to remember someone’s name or take a quick note from a fast-paced presentation.

Apple says that users will also be able to tap an “Ask Siri” option that appears below the text snippet if they have questions about something that was said — like a technical term they don’t understand, or perhaps some sauce option the waiter mentioned that they’re unfamiliar with, among other things.

When you double-press the digital crown, an audible chime appears and an animation displays on the watch. This is meant to signal to people through the combination of the gesture, sound, and visual display that you’ve recorded something that was said.

These snippets will be deleted automatically after 30 seconds if you don’t save them.

The other option, Siri Recaps, takes this ambient listening technology even further by allowing Apple Watch owners to take high-level notes of their conversations.

Importantly, Apple says it’s not identifying speakers, saving the raw audio, or providing word-for-word transcriptions. Instead, the feature summarizes a conversation with a short sentence and some bullet points that identify key points. For instance, depending on the topic, the bullet points might include things like important dates or deadlines, pricing or payment plan information, and other factual information.

Apple suggested the feature could be used in scenarios like work meetings, parent-teacher conferences, personal training sessions, or other places where you may need to remember what tasks you have to complete or things that were said. Essentially, it’s supposed to mimic a user’s ability to jot down their own notes — without adding emotion or tone.

This could be helpful particularly at times when you aren’t able to write up your own notes, either because your hands are full or you’re trying to concentrate on whatever’s being said at the time. The recaps won’t record conversations when you’re listening to music with your headphones or using their noise cancellation features.

At the end of the day, you’re prompted to review your saved Siri Recaps when the feature is enabled, and then choose which, if any, you want to save. These notes can be saved to your Notes app or even exported to your Journal app, if they’re more personal in nature. If you do nothing, the recaps will delete themselves within seven days.

This reminder to review the Siri Recaps you’ve recorded also appears when you first unlock your Apple Watch in the morning.

Users can opt to enable the Siri Recaps manually, or they can configure a schedule, such as only having the recapping take place while at work, or making sure that they never run at night. Even if they’re running on a schedule, you can still turn off the recapping feature at any time from the Control Center.

Apple notes that Siri Recaps has been designed to omit sensitive information like government-assigned identifiers, financial and authentication data, certain personal identifiers, and any language that would promote self-harm.

The Audio Intelligence features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 rely on a combination of Apple’s hardware, software, and services. This includes the S11 chip, built-in microphone, and the Apple Intelligence models that run on the iPhone, as well as Apple’s Private Cloud Compute.

The always-on processor includes a secure enclave — a hardware-protected memory space that can’t be accessed by the rest of the operating system — where a dedicated audio buffer processes the raw audio. This allows the audio to be processed without it actually being accessible to anyone, including Apple. The audio is only accessible to the paired iPhone through a secure pairing mechanism between it and the watch.

To work, lightweight AI models on the S11 chip on the Apple Watch detect if there’s a conversation happening that the wearer is a part of, which is then transferred to the secure enclave on the iPhone. On-device processing on the iPhone turns the audio into condensed text, meaning the text of the conversation with the filler words removed. This condensed text is then encrypted and sent to Apple’s Private Cloud Compute (PCC) to create the recap of the conversation that is sent back to the phone. (The recap and any summarizations used to create it are deleted from PCC immediately afterwards.)

The recaps you can then access on your iPhone are only accessible to you, not to Apple. And they’re encrypted when they’re synced between your multiple Apple devices.

Similarly, Apple Watch transfers audio to the iPhone for processing to create the 15-second snippets for Live Rewind.

Apple says none of these features should impact the battery life of your watch or phone. The features will later roll out to the public beta for broader testing before becoming publicly available to all.

Post updated after publication to indicate the current status of the software’s rollout.

article_content_zh:
苹果公司在 9 月份的 Surprise and Shine 硬件活动上首次宣布，Apple Watch 的人工智能“音频智能”技术将于周二进入 Beta 测试，最初是在 iOS 27.3 更新中面向开发者进行测试。该技术包括一组四个可选的 AI 功能，使 Apple Watch Series 12 佩戴者能够检测重要的声音、识别歌曲、跟进对话和做笔记。

这一消息首先是由苹果公司印度通讯团队于周二早些时候通过电子邮件发送的新闻稿宣布的。该更新于当天晚些时候在美国和其他市场推出。

声音识别功能将帮助失聪和有听力障碍的用户识别手表上的警笛、闹钟或门铃等重要声音，而歌曲识别功能则利用苹果的 Shazam 应用程序来检测背景中播放的音乐并识别歌曲名称和艺术家。

然而，更具潜在争议的功能是那些监听人类对话的功能：Live Rewind 和 Siri Recaps。

鉴于对人工智能记录设备（如 Meta 的人工智能眼镜和其他人工智能可穿戴设备）的强烈反对，苹果试图开辟一个空间，让这些功能对 Apple Watch 用户有用，同时仍然尊重周围人的隐私。

借助“实时倒带”功能，您可以回到过去查看某人刚刚说过的话，以防万一您错过了。例如，如果有人在餐厅向您口头指示或阅读一长串特色菜，您可以双击手表的数字表冠，以文本片段形式显示在表盘上，查看过去 15 秒内所说的内容。您可以查看此片段，然后不执行任何操作，它将永久消失。或者，您可以将其保存到 iOS 27 附带的独立 Siri 应用程序中，以便以后访问，如果您想记住某人的名字或在快节奏的演示中快速做笔记，这可能会很有帮助。

苹果表示，如果用户对所说的内容有疑问，比如他们不理解的技术术语，或者服务员提到的一些他们不熟悉的酱汁选项等，他们还可以点击文本片段下方出现的“询问 Siri”选项。

当您双击数字表冠时，手表上会出现提示音并显示动画。这是为了通过手势、声音和视觉显示的结合向人们发出信号，表明你已经记录了所说的内容。

如果您不保存，这些片段将在 30 秒后自动删除。

另一个选项 Siri Recaps 进一步完善了这种环境聆听技术，让 Apple Watch 用户能够对他们的对话进行高级笔记。

重要的是，苹果表示它不会识别说话者、保存原始音频或提供逐字转录。相反，该功能用一个短句和一些识别关键点的要点来总结对话。例如，根据主题的不同，要点可能包括重要日期或截止日期、定价或付款计划信息以及其他事实信息等内容。

苹果建议该功能可以用于工作会议、家长教师会议、个人培训课程或其他可能需要记住必须完成的任务或说过的话的场景。从本质上讲，它应该模仿用户记下自己笔记的能力——而不添加情感或语气。

这可能会很有帮助，尤其是当你无法写自己的笔记时，要么是因为你的手很忙，要么是你试图集中注意力在当时所说的内容上。当您用耳机听音乐或使用噪音消除功能时，回顾不会记录对话。

在一天结束时，启用该功能后，系统会提示您查看已保存的 Siri 回顾，然后选择要保存的内容（如果有）。这些笔记可以保存到您的笔记应用程序中，甚至可以导出到您的日记应用程序中（如果它们本质上更个性化）。如果您不采取任何行动，摘要将在 7 天内自行删除。

当您早上首次解锁 Apple Watch 时，也会出现这条提醒您查看已录制的 Siri 回顾的提醒。

用户可以选择手动启用 Siri 回顾，也可以配置时间表，例如仅在工作时进行回顾，或确保从不在晚上运行。即使它们按计划运行，您仍然可以随时从控制中心关闭重述功能。

苹果指出，Siri Recaps 的设计旨在忽略敏感信息，例如政府分配的标识符、财务和身份验证数据、某些个人标识符以及任何可能宣扬自残的语言。

Apple Watch Series 12 和 Apple Watch Ultra 4 的音频智能功能依赖于 Apple 硬件、软件和服务的组合。这包括 S11 芯片、内置麦克风、在 iPhone 上运行的 Apple Intelligence 模型以及 Apple 的私有云计算。

永远在线的处理器包括一个安全飞地——一个受硬件保护的内存空间，操作系统的其余部分无法访问——其中有一个专用的音频缓冲区处理原始音频。这使得音频可以在任何人（包括苹果）实际上无法访问的情况下进行处理。音频只能由配对的 iPhone 通过 iPhone 和手表之间的安全配对机制访问。

为了工作，Apple Watch 上 S11 芯片上的轻量级 AI 模型会检测佩戴者是否参与了对话，然后将其传输到 iPhone 上的安全区域。 iPhone 上的设备端处理会将音频转换为压缩文本，这意味着删除了填充词的对话文本。然后，该压缩文本被加密并发送到 Apple 的私有云计算 (PCC)，以创建发送回手机的对话摘要。 （随后将立即从 PCC 中删除概述和用于创建它的任何摘要。）

然后，您可以在 iPhone 上访问的回顾只有您自己可以访问，Apple 无法访问。当它们在多个 Apple 设备之间同步时，它们会被加密。

同样，Apple Watch 将音频传输到 iPhone 进行处理，以创建用于实时倒带的 15 秒片段。

苹果表示，这些功能都不会影响手表或手机的电池寿命。这些功能稍后将推出公开测试版，进行更广泛的测试，然后再向所有人公开。

发布后更新帖子以表明软件推出的当前状态。

title: Trump’s New A.I. Chip Rules Rattle Southeast Asia
title_en: Trump’s New A.I. Chip Rules Rattle Southeast Asia

inline_images.caption: A sprawling data center in Johor Darul Takzim, Malaysia.Credit...Ulet Ifansasti for The New York Times
inline_images.alt: A sprawling data center in Johor Darul Takzim, Malaysia.Credit...Ulet Ifansasti for The New York Tim

author: Adam Satariano and Alexandra Stevenson
article_content:
The Trump administration’s proposal to restrict China’s access to advanced A.I. chips overseas rattled Southeast Asia on Tuesday, threatening a data center investment boom fueled by Chinese companies using the region to sidestep U.S. restrictions on Nvidia’s most powerful chips.

Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore have become offshore computing hubs for Chinese companies such as Alibaba and ByteDance. Data center operators in those countries provide the Chinese firms with remote access to advanced Nvidia chips they cannot buy directly or bring into China.

The strategy has drawn billions of dollars in investment to the region. But in Washington, officials seeking tighter controls on China’s A.I. sector have increasingly viewed data centers as a workaround that poses economic and national security risks.

Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, was ousted last week after revelations he had an affair with a woman who formed a Singaporean data center company called Megaspeed. U.S. authorities deemed the woman, Alice Huang, to be an asset for Chinese intelligence services, and they are investigating Megaspeed over allegations of smuggling chips to China. China has denied that Ms. Huang was spying for it.

Separately, Nvidia’s board of directors announced on Tuesday that it had established a committee to oversee “the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management.” Nvidia’s board is engaged in a search for a permanent successor to Mr. Huang. The company’s interim chief executive, Colette Kress, is set to preside over the release of the company’s latest quarterly financial results later on Tuesday.

Shares of technology companies tumbled on Tuesday. In trading in Hong Kong, Alibaba fell more than 5 percent, while Tencent’s stock dropped nearly 4 percent. The Chinese A.I. firms MiniMax Group fell more than 7 percent and Z.AI declined more than 5 percent. In the United States, tech stocks slid lower, pulling the Nasdaq index down nearly 1 percent. Nvidia shares faced a choppy trading day before it reported its earnings after the market close.

Governments across Southeast Asia were scrambling to assess the administration’s 132-page policy, released by the Commerce Department on Monday, as President Trump traveled to Asia for diplomatic meetings.

The timing illustrated how A.I. has moved to the center of global diplomacy. Mr. Trump was expected to meet leaders of several affected countries at the ASEAN summit of 11 Southeast Asian nations in Manila. Then, he traveled to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, forum.

The rules, which take effect in 90 days, will require overseas data center operators to obtain a license from the United States government before supplying a “significant volume” of computing power to companies based in countries deemed high-risk, including China, Iran and Russia.

Licenses would also be required to export advanced chips to companies headquartered in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia or Brazil, countries the Trump administration identified as posing a heightened smuggling risk.

The Singaporean government said in a statement on Tuesday that it was investigating Megaspeed and was “engaging the relevant U.S. authorities on the scope and implementation of the measure.”

“As a global hub for technology and trade, Singapore will continue to safeguard the integrity of our business environment and continued access to advanced semiconductors and computing capabilities for legitimate companies operating here, and act against those who flout our laws,” the statement read.

Indonesia said it was seeking industry input and pledged to enforce American export controls. The government is developing a trade framework to “facilitate legitimate trade” while preventing sensitive technologies from being “diverted or misused,” the country’s Government Communication Agency said.

Steve Okun, chief executive of APAC Advisors, a geopolitical consulting firm, said countries such as Malaysia had benefited from maintaining close ties with Washington and Beijing. The new restrictions could make that balancing act harder to sustain.

“The ‘don’t make us choose’ era is coming to an end,” he said. “When it comes to A.I. and sensitive technologies, countries will need to choose the U.S.-led tech stack versus China.”

Ong Kian Ming, Malaysia’s former deputy minister for investment, trade and industry, said he hoped the Trump administration, which has been divided over A.I. chip export restrictions, would revise the rules before they take effect.

Otherwise, he said, the restrictions could create an opening for Chinese companies to offer competing chips. “This may mitigate some of the negative impact of not allowing these players to access Nvidia GPU chips,” he said.

summary_zh: 美国商务部发布新政，拟限制海外数据中心利用高算力芯片向中国提供远程访问服务

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国商务部发布新规，要求海外数据中心在向中国用户提供“大规模”算力服务前必须获得政府许可。此政策旨在封堵中资企业利用海外算力集群规避英伟达芯片出口禁令的漏洞，受此消息影响，区域性算力投资逻辑重塑，并引发市场对全球AI供应链合规成本激增的连锁反应。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The U.S. Department of Commerce has released new rules requiring overseas data centers to obtain government licenses before providing 'significant' compute power to China. This policy aims to close loopholes where Chinese firms utilize offshore compute clusters to bypass Nvidia chip export restrictions, triggering a revaluation of regional AI investments and rising global compliance costs.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 算力主权正加速从‘硬件禁运’向‘服务流控’深度演进。美国此举标志着监管边界已从实物贸易延伸至算力基础设施的租用模式，这将彻底改变全球云计算厂商的‘跨区域部署策略’，并迫使在东南亚布局算力底层的中国公司面临严重的资产清算与合规性重新洗牌风险。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Compute sovereignty is shifting from hardware embargoes to service-level flow control. This move marks the extension of U.S. jurisdiction from physical trade to the operational model of compute infrastructure, forcing a fundamental rethink of cross-regional deployment for global cloud providers and putting Chinese-backed regional clusters in Southeast Asia at severe risk of asset liquidation and compliance forced-exits.

article_content_zh:
特朗普政府限制中国获取先进人工智能的提议周二，海外芯片风波席卷东南亚，威胁到中国公司利用该地区规避美国对英伟达最强大芯片的限制而推动的数据中心投资热潮。

马来西亚、印度尼西亚、泰国和新加坡已成为阿里巴巴和字节跳动等中国公司的离岸计算中心。这些国家的数据中心运营商为中国公司提供远程访问先进的英伟达芯片的能力，而这些公司无法直接购买或带入中国。

该战略已为该地区吸引了数十亿美元的投资。但在华盛顿，官员们寻求对中国的人工智能实施更严格的控制。越来越多的行业将数据中心视为带来经济和国家安全风险的解决方案。

英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 上周被免职，原因是他与一名创办新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的女性有染。美国当局认为这名名叫 Alice Huang 的女子是中国情报部门的资产，他们正在调查 Megaspeed 涉嫌向中国走私芯片的指控。中国否认黄女士为其从事间谍活动。

另外，英伟达董事会周二宣布，已成立一个委员会来监督“公司的国家安全政策、出口管制合规性和全球贸易风险管理”。英伟达董事会正在寻找黄先生的永久继任者。该公司临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)将于周二晚些时候主持发布该公司最新的季度财务业绩。

周二科技公司股价暴跌。在香港交易中，阿里巴巴股价下跌超过 5%，而腾讯股价下跌近 4%。中国人工智能MiniMax Group 跌幅超过 7%，Z.AI 跌幅超过 5%。美国方面，科技股走低，纳斯达克指数下跌近1%。英伟达股价在收盘后公布财报之前经历了一个波动的交易日。

在特朗普总统前往亚洲参加外交会议之际，东南亚各国政府正在争先恐后地评估商务部周一发布的政府长达 132 页的政策。

这个时机说明了人工智能是如何做到的。已成为全球外交的中心。预计特朗普先生将在马尼拉举行的由 11 个东南亚国家组成的东盟峰会上会见多个受影响国家的领导人。随后，他前往中国深圳参加亚太经济合作组织（APEC）论坛。

该规定将于 90 天后生效，要求海外数据中心运营商在向中国、伊朗和俄罗斯等被视为高风险国家的公司提供“大量”计算能力之前，必须获得美国政府的许可。

向总部位于马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、印度尼西亚或巴西的公司出口先进芯片还需要获得许可证，特朗普政府认为这些国家构成走私风险较高。

新加坡政府周二在一份声明中表示，正在调查 Megaspeed，并“正在与美国相关当局就该措施的范围和实施进行接触”。

声明中写道：“作为全球技术和贸易中心，新加坡将继续维护我们商业环境的完整性，并继续为在这里运营的合法公司提供先进的半导体和计算能力，并对那些藐视我们法律的人采取行动。”

印度尼西亚表示正在寻求行业投入，并承诺执行美国的出口管制。该国政府通信机构表示，政府正在制定一个贸易框架，以“促进合法贸易”，同时防止敏感技术“被转移或滥用”。

地缘政治咨询公司APAC Advisors首席执行官史蒂夫·奥肯(Steve Okun)表示，马来西亚等国家受益于与华盛顿和北京保持密切关系。新的限制可能会使这种平衡行为更难以维持。

“‘不要让我们选择’的时代即将结束，”他说。 “在人工智能和敏感技术方面，各国将需要选择美国主导的技术堆栈，而不是中国。”

马来西亚前投资、贸易和工业部副部长王建民表示，他希望在人工智能问题上存在分歧的特朗普政府能够改变现状。芯片出口限制，将在生效前修改规则。

他表示，否则这些限制可能会为中国公司提供竞争芯片创造机会。 “这可能会减轻一些不允许这些玩家访问 Nvidia GPU 芯片的负面影响，”他说。

【起因与机理】针对利用第三方基础设施规避高性能芯片禁令的“算力绕道”行为
【关键数据与实测】政策设置90天缓冲期，将引发区域算力市场资产价值重构。

author: Benoît Morenne
article_content:
Published on 11/17/2026 at 11:23 am EST

--Brent crude is down 0.5% to $91.93 a barrel.

--European benchmark gas falls 2.5% to 86.88 euros a megawatt-hour.

--Copper futures are down 0.2% at $13,176.50 a metric ton.

--Gold futures rise 0.4% to $3,869 a troy ounce.

Geothermal startup Quaise Energy wants to use futuristic technology to vaporize stone, drill at superhot depths and produce clean power around the clock. Now, it has Google on board.

The tech company has signed a deal valued at more than $500 million to secure 50 megawatts of power from a geothermal project that Houston-based Quaise is developing in central Oregon. The electricity produced at the site will support Google's existing data-center operations in the state.

Goldman Sees Gold Rising Above $4,600 an Ounce by End-2027 on Central-Bank Buying

Gold's near-term outlook is clouded by expectations of higher U.S. interest rates, but central-bank buying is set to drive prices back above $4,600 a troy ounce by the end of next year, Goldman Sachs said in its latest report.

The bank expects gold to reach $4,650 a troy ounce by the end of 2027, about 13% above its October average, as central-bank purchases--particularly by emerging-market countries seeking to diversify their reserves--emerge as the main force supporting prices.

China Flexes Muscle in Iron Ore, Squeezing Australia and Its Miners

Four years ago, China created a single, state-owned buyer to gain more control over resources needed for its mammoth steelmaking sector. This year, it has been putting its newfound power to work.

The market for iron ore, the steelmaking commodity that ranks among the world's most heavily traded, is dominated by Australia and China. The pair account for more than half of all production and purchases, respectively.

Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Shipping Risks Persist

Oil prices rose Tuesday, recovering from initial losses as traders weighed continued threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments against expectations of a global supply surplus.

Front-month Brent crude futures rose 0.5% to $92.90 a barrel, while front-month West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 0.4% to $86.10 a barrel.

U.S. Adds More Battery Energy Storage, Supporting Solar Growth

U.S. utilities, homes and businesses installed 14.3 gigawatt hours of new battery storage capacity in the third quarter of the year to back growth in renewable energy generation, according to a report by the Solar Energy Industries Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

Utility-scale projects added 12.2 gigawatt hours, residential battery storage increased by 746 megawatt hours, while commercial and industrial users added 1.3 gigawatt hours, largely on demand from data centers.

BP Names New Directors as Restructuring Continues

British energy major BP appointed two independent nonexecutive directors as it continues to reshuffle its leadership team as part of a broader business restructure.

It said Tuesday that Andrew Bonfield, a former chief financial officer of Caterpillar, National Grid, Cadbury, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and SmithKline Beecham, will join the company on Dec. 1.

Oil Futures Gain on Continued Shipping Risks -- Market Talk

1027 ET - Oil futures pick up from the previous day's losses as shipping risks in the Middle East limit declines on expectations of a return to a global oil surplus. "More threats from Iran are being noted supporting crude futures in the early trade. However, lately they seem to be losing leverage," Dennis Kissler of BOK Financial says in a note. Ukraine struck another Russian refinery, "so the geopolitical tensions remain a supporting price buffer for crude," he adds. WTI is up 1.1% at $86.66 a barrel and Brent is up 1% at $93.40 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

Wheat Futures Rise as Ukraine Strikes Key Bridge -- Market Talk

1019 ET - Wheat futures lead the market higher after a Ukrainian strike caused significant damage to the Kerch Bridge, which spans the strait connecting the Sea of Azov with the Black Sea. "Obviously, shipments have already been effectively nonexistent relative to pre-war norms, but this damage could mean a substantial delay to resumed commodity flow even if an agreement was somehow reached," Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. He remains skeptical about the likelihood of an agreement between Russia and Ukraine. Speculative selling pushed wheat down on optimism around talks, "but on the ground we've seen nothing but escalation," he adds. Wheat is up 1.9% on CBOT. Soybeans are up 0.6% and corn is up 0.3%.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

Palm Oil Ends Lower as Weakness in Soybean, Crude Oil Weigh -- Market Talk

1039 GMT - Palm oil prices closed lower, weighed by weaker soybean oil and crude oil prices, alongside softer Dalian vegetable oils and concerns over slowing Malaysian export demand, says David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. Ng expects crude palm oil futures to find support at around 4,400 ringgit a ton and face resistance at 4,600 ringgit a ton. The market sentiment will likely remain cautious amid weaker competing vegetable oils and energy prices, he adds. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for February delivery ended 113 ringgit lower at 4,434 ringgit a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)

Ample Inventories, Weak Industrial Demand Weigh on Silver Outlook -- Market Talk

0946 GMT - Silver prices are unlikely to stage a significant rebound as weaker industrial demand and ample inventories weigh on the market, according to ANZ. In the solar sector, technological advances and efforts to reduce silver use are expected to drive a 19% decline in consumption in 2026. Uncertainty surrounding the expansion of artificial-intelligence infrastructure is adding to concerns about future demand. Meanwhile, ample inventories have left the market well-positioned to absorb any sudden increase in demand, limiting the potential for a price squeeze. A sustained recovery will require stronger investment demand, which in turn depends on gold prices resuming their upward trend, ANZ analysts say. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

Oil Falls as Focus Shifts to Market Surplus -- Market Talk

0926 GMT - Oil prices fall on growing expectations of a widening supply surplus next year despite persistent concerns over continued attacks in the Middle East. Brent crude is down 0.5% to $91.93 a barrel, while WTI trades 0.5% lower at $85.29 a barrel. The benchmarks have fallen around 16% and 14% on the month, respectively. However, "the supply flows are unsustainable over the longer term," analysts at ANZ say. "Logistics are under stress, while supply, inventories, refining and effective spare capacity are vulnerable." According to the latest Kpler data, Middle East oil flows--including shipments through Hormuz and alternative routes across the region--averaged more than 15.7 million barrels a day in the week through Nov. 15, below prewar levels of 23.3 million. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

U.S. Natural Gas Futures Extend Retreat -- Market Talk

0923 ET - U.S. natural gas futures extend their pullback from last week's highs as the weekend cold spell eases. "Fundamentals are a mixed bag to start the day with reports of lower production being offset by lower overall demands as well," Gary Cunningham of Tradition Energy says in a note. "Weather models continue to disagree, leaving the door open to a noon forecast revision that could give us a something to trade around," he adds. Nymex natural gas is down 2% at $3.06/mmBtu, retreating for a third consecutive session. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

Gold Remains Pressured by Fed Rate-Hike Bets -- Market Talk

0906 GMT - Gold prices hold below $3,900 a troy ounce, pressured by expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next month. "Sentiment remains fragile, with rising Fed rate-hike expectations and a firmer dollar outweighing support from falling energy prices," analysts at Saxo Bank say. "This divergence highlights concerns that inflationary pressures are becoming broader, stickier and more difficult to reverse." Investors now await the release of the Fed's October meeting minutes for more cues on the monetary policy outlook. In early European trading, gold futures rise 0.4% to $3,869 an ounce. Meanwhile, silver rises 1.2% to $47.45 an ounce and platinum is up 0.6% at $1,457.30 an ounce. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

Gold Seen Around $4,000 in Long Term, But Risks Loom on Both Sides -- Market Talk

0859 GMT - Gold prices are expected to remain well above pre-Covid levels in the coming years, hovering around $4,000 a troy ounce, according to BMI. The outlook, however, is subject to risks in both directions, with geopolitical developments and shifts in U.S. monetary policy likely to shape the metal's trajectory. A preliminary deal to end the U.S.-Iran conflict could ease oil prices and inflationary pressures, paving the way for earlier Federal Reserve rate cuts. A weaker dollar would provide further support, potentially lifting prices back above $4,500 an ounce, analysts at the firm say. But a renewed escalation in the conflict, or a sharper rise in the dollar and bond yields if the Fed resumes raising rates, could undermine demand. Higher yields would make non-interest-bearing gold less attractive, potentially triggering a selloff that pushes prices back to the $3,000-$3,500 range, BMI says. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

——黄金期货上涨0.4%，至每盎司3869美元。

b谷歌采用地热技术蒸发岩石以获得清洁能源

地热初创公司Quaise Energy希望利用未来技术将石头气化，在超高温深处钻探，并全天候生产清洁能源。现在，它有b谷歌在船上。

这家科技公司签署了一项价值超过5亿美元的协议，从总部位于休斯顿的Quaise在俄勒冈州中部开发的一个地热项目中获得50兆瓦的电力。该站点产生的电力将支持b谷歌在该州现有数据中心的运营。

高盛预计，到2027年底，由于央行的买盘，金价将升至每盎司4,600美元以上

高盛在最新报告中表示，美国加息的预期给黄金的近期前景蒙上阴影，但央行的买盘将在明年底前将金价推升至每金衡盎司 4,600 美元以上。

该银行预计，到 2027 年底，金价将达到每金衡盎司 4,650 美元，比 10 月份的平均水平高出约 13%，因为央行的购买行为（尤其是寻求外汇储备多元化的新兴市场国家的购买行为）成为支撑金价的主要力量。

中国在铁矿石领域大展拳脚，挤压澳大利亚及其矿商

四年前，中国创建了一个单一的国有买家，以更好地控制其庞大的炼钢行业所需的资源。今年，它一直在发挥新发现的力量。

铁矿石是全球交易量最大的炼钢商品之一，其市场由澳大利亚和中国主导。这对产品分别占总产量和采购量的一半以上。

中东航运风险持续存在，油价反弹

周二油价上涨，从最初的跌势中恢复过来，交易员权衡了中东石油运输的持续威胁与全球供应过剩的预期。

近月布伦特原油期货上涨 0.5%，至每桶 92.90 美元，近月西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨 0.4%，至每桶 86.10 美元。

美国增加了更多电池储能，支持太阳能增长

根据太阳能工业协会和 Benchmark Mineral Intelligence 的一份报告，美国公用事业公司、家庭和企业在今年第三季度安装了 14.3 吉瓦时的新电池存储容量，以支持可再生能源发电的增长。

公用事业规模项目增加了 12.2 吉瓦时，住宅电池存储增加了 746 兆瓦时，而商业和工业用户增加了 1.3 吉瓦时，主要是根据数据中心的需求。

随着重组的继续，英国石油公司任命新董事

英国能源巨头英国石油公司任命了两名独立非执行董事，作为更广泛业务重组的一部分，该公司继续重组其领导团队。

该公司周二表示，卡特彼勒、国家电网、吉百利、百时美施贵宝和史密斯克必成的前首席财务官安德鲁·邦菲尔德(Andrew Bonfield)将于12月1日加入该公司。

石油期货因持续的运输风险而上涨——市场讨论

1027 ET - 石油期货从前一天的跌幅中回升，因为中东航运风险因全球石油盈余回归的预期而限制下降。 BOK Financial 的丹尼斯·基斯勒 (Dennis Kissler) 在一份报告中表示：“人们注意到，来自伊朗的更多威胁在早盘交易中支撑了原油期货。然而，最近他们似乎正在失去杠杆作用。”乌克兰袭击了另一家俄罗斯炼油厂，“因此地缘政治紧张局势仍然是原油价格的支撑缓冲，”他补充道。 WTI 上涨 1.1%，至每桶 86.66 美元，布伦特原油上涨 1%，至每桶 93.40 美元。 (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

乌克兰撞上关键桥梁，小麦期货上涨——市场讨论

1019 ET - 乌克兰罢工对横跨连接亚速海和黑海的刻赤大桥造成严重破坏，小麦期货引领市场走高。 StoneX 的迈克·卡斯尔 (Mike Castle) 在一份报告中表示：“显然，相对于战前的标准，运输实际上已经不存在，但这种损害可能意味着即使以某种方式达成了协议，恢复商品流通的时间也会大幅延迟。”他仍然对俄罗斯和乌克兰达成协议的可能性持怀疑态度。由于谈判的乐观情绪，投机性抛售压低了小麦价格，“但实际上我们只看到了局势升级，”他补充道。 CBOT 小麦上涨 1.9%。大豆上涨 0.6%，玉米上涨 0.3%。(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

由于大豆和原油疲软，棕榈油收低——市场讨论

格林威治标准时间 1039 - 棕榈油价格收低，受到豆油和原油价格疲软、大连植物油走软以及对马来西亚出口需求放缓的担忧的影响，吉隆坡 Iceberg X 的交易员 David Ng 表示。Ng 预计毛棕榈油期货将在每吨 4,400 林吉特左右找到支撑，并在每吨 4,600 林吉特面临阻力。他补充说，由于植物油和能源价格竞争疲软，市场情绪可能会保持谨慎。马来西亚证券交易所 2 月份交割的衍生品合约收盘下跌 113 林吉特，至每吨 4,434 林吉特。 (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahui Huang)

库存充裕、工业需求疲软打压白银前景——市场讨论

0946 GMT - 据澳新银行称，由于工业需求疲软和库存充足给市场带来压力，白银价格不太可能大幅反弹。在太阳能领域，技术进步和减少白银使用量的努力预计将导致 2026 年白银消耗量下降 19%。人工智能基础设施扩张的不确定性加剧了人们对未来需求的担忧。与此同时，充足的库存使市场能够很好地吸收需求的突然增长，从而限制了价格挤压的可能性。澳新银行分析师表示，持续复苏将需要更强劲的投资需求，而这反过来又取决于金价恢复上涨趋势。 （giulia.petroni@wsj.com）

随着焦点转向市场过剩，油价下跌——市场讨论

0926 GMT - 尽管对中东持续袭击的担忧持续存在，但由于对明年供应过剩扩大的预期不断增强，油价下跌。布伦特原油下跌 0.5%，至每桶 91.93 美元，WTI 原油下跌 0.5%，至每桶 85.29 美元。本月基准分别下跌约 16% 和 14%。然而，“从长远来看，供应流是不可持续的”，澳新银行分析师表示。 “物流面临压力，而供应、库存、炼油和有效闲置​​产能都很脆弱。”根据 Kpler 的最新数据，截至 11 月 15 日当周，中东石油流量（包括通过霍尔木兹和该地区其他路线的运输）平均每天超过 1570 万桶，低于战前 2330 万桶的水平。 （giulia.petroni@wsj.com）

美国天然气期货延续回调——市场讨论

0923 ET - 随着周末寒潮的缓解，美国天然气期货从上周高点延续回调。传统能源公司的加里·坎宁安（Gary Cunningham）在一份报告中表示：“今天的基本面好坏参半，有报道称产量下降也被总体需求下降所抵消。”他补充道：“天气模型仍然存在分歧，这为中午预报的修正敞开了大门，这可能会给我们带来一些可交易的东西。” Nymex 天然气价格下跌 2%，至 3.06 美元/mmBtu，连续第三个交易日下跌。 (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

黄金仍然受到美联储加息押注的压力——市场讨论

0906 GMT - 受美联储下个月加息预期的压力，金价维持在每金衡盎司 3,900 美元以下。盛宝银行分析师表示，“随着美联储加息预期的上升和美元走强超过了能源价格下跌的支撑，市场情绪仍然脆弱。” “这种分歧凸显了人们对通胀压力变得更广泛、更棘手、更难以扭转的担忧。”投资者现在等待美联储公布10月会议纪要，以获取有关货币政策前景的更多线索。欧洲早盘，黄金期货上涨 0.4%，至每盎司 3,869 美元。与此同时，白银上涨 1.2%，至每盎司 47.45 美元，铂金上涨 0.6%，至每盎司 1,457.30 美元。 （giulia.petroni@wsj.com）

长期来看，黄金价格在 4,000 美元左右，但双方都面临风险——市场讨论

格林尼治标准时间 0859 - 根据 BMI 的数据，未来几年金价预计将保持远高于新冠疫情爆发前的水平，徘徊在每金衡盎司 4,000 美元左右。然而，前景受到双向风险的影响，地缘政治的发展和美国货币政策的转变可能会影响金属的走势。结束美伊冲突的初步协议可能会缓解油价和通胀压力，为美联储早些时候降息铺平道路。该公司分析师表示，美元走软将提供进一步支撑，有可能将价格推升至每盎司 4,500 美元以上。但如果美联储恢复加息，冲突再次升级，或者美元和债券收益率大幅上涨，可能会削弱需求。 BMI表示，较高的收益率将降低无息黄金的吸引力，从而可能引发抛售，将金价推回3,000至3,500美元的区间。 （giulia.petroni@wsj.com）

中国信号减弱，铜价跌至四个月低点——市场讨论

title: Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying
title_en: Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying

inline_images.caption: Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying

author: Alexandra Alper and David Shepardson
article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The Trump administration plans to press ahead with efforts to block imports of Chinese data center equipment despite pushback from Amazon, Google, Meta and other US technology companies, people briefed on the matter said.

Reuters reported in August that the Federal Communications Commission was seeking to ban US imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within data centers, over national security concerns.

But the measure has faced more opposition than was previously known, with Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave and Cisco joining Microsoft in a meeting with White House officials earlier this year previously reported by Reuters. US firms could need up to a decade to comply with any such mandate, the executives told the officials, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The lobbying had raised doubts over whether the measure would go ahead. But it is moving forward, three additional people familiar with the matter said, emphasizing that it could still get shelved if sentiment within the administration changes.

Shares of US optical transceiver makers rose after the news, with Coherent up 2.2% and Lumentum up 1.5%.

The momentum is thanks in part to revelations about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which have fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats.

The FCC, Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave and Cisco did not respond to requests for comment. Microsoft declined to comment. A White House official declined to comment on the lobbying or the measure's progress but said recent FCC actions barring Chinese technology and other foreign equipment have resulted in billions in investments into US manufacturing, and thousands of new American jobs.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington said Beijing "firmly opposes the US overstretching the concept of national security" and urges the Trump administration to "stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions."

"China will continue to do what is necessary to firmly defend the legitimate and lawful rights and interests of Chinese companies," it added.

China hawks in Washington are concerned Chinese transceivers could be used by Beijing to steal data, install malware or disrupt service at US data centers.

China boasts two-thirds of the global market for optical transceivers, according to Counterpoint Research. Chinese firms like Eoptolink and Zhongji Innolight, which was added to the Pentagon's list of Chinese military-backed companies, dominate global supply, counting top American hyperscalers among their customers.

US-based Coherent and Lumentum produce technology that competes with them but lack the scale to replace Chinese vendors, according to a report by the Foundation for American Innovation.

One of the people said the US firms raised the prospect of retaliation from China, in the form of a ban on the export of indium phosphide, a critical mineral needed for US firms to produce their own optical transceivers.

Trump has taken a more dovish approach to China in his second term, as he faces down Beijing's export controls on rare-earth minerals, which underpin tech manufacturing everywhere.

But the FCC has been a notable exception, successfully barring imports of new models of Chinese drones, robots, power inverters and routers over the last year.

The Huang revelations have added to the pressure on the administration by turning a spotlight on cases of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unaddressed by the Commerce Department.

article_content_zh:
路透华盛顿11月17日 - 据知情人士透露，特朗普政府计划继续努力阻止进口中国数据中心设备，尽管遭到亚马逊、谷歌、Meta和其他美国科技公司的抵制。

路透社8月份报道称，出于国家安全考虑，美国联邦通信委员会正寻求禁止美国进口新型中国光收发器，这些光收发器允许数据在数据中心内以光速通过光纤电缆传输。

但该措施面临的反对比之前所知的要多，据路透社报道，今年早些时候，亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、CoreWeave 和思科与微软一起与白宫官员举行了会议。据两位知情人士透露，高管们告诉官员，美国公司可能需要长达十年的时间才能遵守此类指令。

游说活动引发了人们对该措施是否会继续实施的怀疑。但另外三名知情人士表示，该计划正在向前推进，并强调如果政府内部情绪发生变化，该计划仍可能被搁置。

消息传出后，美国光收发器制造商股价上涨，Coherent 上涨 2.2%，Lumentum 上涨 1.5%。

这一势头在一定程度上要归功于英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情被曝光，这促使华盛顿再次呼吁对中国技术威胁采取更强硬的立场。

FCC、亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、CoreWeave 和思科均未回应置评请求。微软拒绝置评。一位白宫官员拒绝就游说或该措施的进展发表评论，但表示，联邦通信委员会最近禁止中国技术和其他外国设备的行动已为美国制造业带来了数十亿美元的投资，并为美国创造了数千个新就业机会。

中国驻华盛顿大使馆表示，北京“坚决反对美国过度延伸国家安全概念”，并敦促特朗普政府“停止抹黑中国企业并以制裁相威胁”。

中方将继续采取必要措施，坚决捍卫中国企业的正当合法权益。

华盛顿的对华鹰派担心中国的收发器可能被北京用来窃取数据、安装恶意软件或破坏美国数据中心的服务。

据 Counterpoint Research 称，中国拥有全球光收发器市场的三分之二。新易盛（Eoptolink）和中际旭创（Zhongji Innolight）等中国公司已被列入五角大楼的中国军方支持公司名单，它们在全球供应中占据主导地位，其客户中也包括美国顶级超大规模企业。

美国创新基金会的一份报告称，美国相干公司和 Lumentum 生产的技术可与他们竞争，但缺乏取代中国供应商的规模。

其中一位知情人士表示，美国公司提出了中国可能采取报复措施的可能性，即禁止出口磷化铟，这是美国公司生产自己的光收发器所需的一种重要矿物。

特朗普在他的第二个任期内对中国采取了更温和的态度，因为他面对北京对稀土矿物的出口管制，稀土是世界各地科技制造业的基础。

但美国联邦通信委员会是一个值得注意的例外，去年成功禁止进口新型号的中国无人机、机器人、逆变器和路由器。

黄仁勋的爆料让英伟达人工智能芯片走私到中国的案件成为人们关注的焦点，而商务部却没有解决这一问题，这增加了政府的压力。

title: Sequoia, Greenoaks Lead Isomorphic Labs $5 Billion Funding Round
title_en: Sequoia, Greenoaks Lead Isomorphic Labs $5 Billion Funding Round
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Isomorphic Labs, started by AI pioneer Demis Hassabis, has secured a massive $5 billion funding boost to speed up its work using artificial intelligence for finding new medicines. The announcement comes three-and-a-half months after Hassabis stepped back as CEO of DeepMind, Google's AI lab he co-founded that's known for pushing boundaries in tech and science.

Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital lead round. This funding round was led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with support from heavyweights like Andreessen Horowitz and Alphabet (Google's parent company). Isomorphic Labs spun out from DeepMind in 2021 with a mission to use AI for modeling biology at the molecular level.

Their big win is part of a huge wave: AI drug discovery startups have pulled in a record $23.2 billion this year alone, showing just how much faith investors have in tech transforming health care.
content_snippet: Alphabet Inc.'s Isomorphic Labs, which is working to design new drugs with artificial intelligence, has raised $5 billion …
summary_en: Alphabet's AI-driven drug discovery unit, Isomorphic Labs, has secured $5 billion in Series C funding. The round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz and continued backing from Alphabet. The proceeds will scale AI-powered drug design capabilities and expand global infrastructure for pharmaceutical discovery.

title: Can A.I. Take the Edge Off One of Hollywood’s Worst Jobs?
title_en: Can A.I. Take the Edge Off One of Hollywood’s Worst Jobs?

inline_images.caption: Rotoscoping requires tracing objects frame by frame, sometimes for thousands of frames. “It’s the worst,” one visual effects artists lamented. (Foundry)
inline_images.alt: Rotoscoping requires tracing objects frame by frame, sometimes for thousands of frames. “It’s the worst,” one visual effects artists lamented.

inline_images.caption: Timothée Chalamet in “Dune: Part Two,” in which visual effects artists used a machine learning tool to turn the actors’ eyes blue. In “Dune: Part One,” the work had to be done manually. (Warner Bros.)
inline_images.alt: Timothée Chalamet in “Dune: Part Two,” in which visual effects artists used a machine learning tool to turn the actors’ eyes blue. In “Dune: Part One,” the work had to be done manually.

author: Matt Stevens
article_content:
Tedious. Mind-numbing. Soul-destroying.

Ask visual-effects artists in Hollywood and most will agree: The task known as rotoscoping, while essential, is no fun.

Perhaps that is why an industry that has at times had its pitchforks out for everything artificial intelligence seems open to the idea that the technology can alleviate this particular burden.

Rotoscoping — even the name is insipid — involves methodically tracing around an object or a person, frame by frame and often for hours so that it can be isolated from the rest of the shot. A hologram of Princess Leia does not plead for help from Obi-Wan Kenobi in the original “Star Wars” (1977) without rotoscoping. Nor do the light sabers glow.

But can A.I. ease the drudgery? And can it do so with the same expert precision that human hands have provided for decades? What happens to those workers if their jobs get replaced?

More than a dozen people who work in visual effects in Hollywood acknowledged in interviews that some of the A.I.-powered rotoscoping tools they have begun to tinker with may be saving time and reducing tedium. But they stressed that the tools were far from perfect. Almost more important, they added, rotoscoping is a slice of moviemaking that offers valuable insight into how A.I. has begun to influence the industry.

“A.I. is not a simple conversation,” said Sang-Jin Bae, the director of the Martin Scorsese Virtual Production Center at New York University. But rotoscoping, he added, “is actually the perfect case study.”

Few viewers think about rotoscoping when watching a movie, but, as a foundational part of visual effects, it is indispensable.

Ever cut out a person from an image using Photoshop? “Roto,” as some call it, is like that but way more complicated and time-consuming. As characters and objects move through the frames of a film, each frame must be rotoed again to match the movements.

In many cases, rotoing requires breaking an object into sections and drawing shapes for each section. All those shapes must be repositioned to track the object’s progression across each frame.

“If you have an actor with long blond hair, and they’re flipping in the air fighting a robot, you need to roto every single hair,” said Jason Gottlieb, a longtime visual effects artist. “It’s the worst.”

Perhaps that is why rotoscoping often falls to entry-level employees. Marti Romances, a founder and the creative director of Territory Studio, recalled doing it 20 years ago.

“I wish back then, that instead of spending the first two years of my career doing these tedious things, I could have done other things that would teach me more about creativity,” he said.

Because all shots are different, experts hesitate to generalize about the costs and time involved in rotoscoping.

By some estimates, a person might spend a week rotoscoping a complicated five-second shot. Roto for an intricate one-minute scene could cost as much as $75,000.

Varying forms of machine learning have, in fact, been assisting with the most painstaking parts of moviemaking for several years, before so many advancements were grouped under the umbrella term of A.I.

In “Dune: Part Two” (2024), a machine-learning tool was used to locate all the eyeballs of the Fremen people and color them a radiant blue. When “Dune: Part One” was made a few years earlier, that work was accomplished only through countless hours of manual rotoscoping.

Just this year, companies including Adobe and Foundry have released tools that can, with just a click from a human being, find objects and trace around them. They can also ensure that an object and its shapes move in synchronicity across frames.

The results are seldom perfect. But with only a few human-guided tweaks, they often can be. Foundry, a creative software developer based in London, estimates that its SmartRoto tool can accelerate the roto process by a factor of four.

Any filmmaker with a smaller budget than the “Dune” franchise can turn to generative A.I. tools, which tend to be cheaper and more accessible. Need to roto distracting power lines out of a scene? Generative A.I. can do that. But the results often appear a little fuzzy, like your body against a video call’s virtual background. And a little fuzzy, visual artists say, looks a lot fuzzy on a big screen.

“Everyone asks for a magic button,” said Juan Salazar, Foundry’s creative director. “That button doesn’t exist.”

The other catch to employing A.I. to solve the riddle of rotoing, one that has been stoking fears in many industries beyond Hollywood, is what happens to the workers?

As it turns out, because rotoing has been expensive and labor-intensive for so long, an overwhelming majority of those jobs have already been moved to India, where costs are lower than in the United States.

Some artists who remain stateside hope that the increased efficiency brought on by A.I. won’t simply put them out of a job, but free them up to engage with more fulfilling filmmaking tasks.

Hope also exists in that the companies experimenting with A.I. still need trained artists to clean up the substandard content most models typically produce. Fuzzy outlines don’t win Oscars.

Still, many people who work in the industry are distressed, even enraged, by what seems to be A.I.’s ineluctable march toward control. Others are more ambivalent, noting that new technologies are often overhyped.

“A.I. is a tool, but that’s all it is,” said Maggie Kraisamutr, a longtime visual effects artist. “It’s not a replacement for human beings who are creating art.”

How long that remains true is the question everyone is asking.

article_content_zh:
乏味。令人心麻木。毁灭灵魂。

询问好莱坞的视觉效果艺术家，大多数人都会同意：动态观察的任务虽然很重要，但并不有趣。

或许这就是为什么这个时常热衷于人工智能的行业似乎对这项技术可以减轻这种特殊负担的想法持开放态度。

动态观察——即使这个名字很平淡——需要有条不紊地围绕一个物体或一个人，一帧一帧地进行追踪，通常需要几个小时，以便将其与镜头的其余部分隔离开来。在原版《星球大战》（1977 年）中，莱娅公主的全息图并未向欧比旺·克诺比求助，无需转描。光剑也不发光。

但人工智能可以吗？减轻苦差事？它能否以与人类双手几十年来所提供的同样的专业精度来做到这一点？如果这些工人的工作被取代，他们会怎样？

十多名在好莱坞从事视觉效果工作的人在采访中承认，他们已经开始修补的一些人工智能驱动的动态描画工具可能会节省时间并减少乏味。但他们强调，这些工具远非完美。他们补充说，更重要的是，动态观察是电影制作的一部分，它为了解人工智能如何工作提供了宝贵的见解。已开始对行业产生影响。

“人工智能不是一场简单的对话，”纽约大学马丁·斯科塞斯虚拟制作中心主任裴尚金 (Sang-Jin Bae) 说。但他补充说，动态观察“实际上是一个完美的案例研究。”

很少有观众在观看电影时会想到动态观察，但作为视觉效果的基础部分，它是不可或缺的。

您曾经使用 Photoshop 从图像中剪出人物吗？有些人称之为“Roto”，与此类似，但更复杂且耗时。当角色和物体在电影的帧中移动时，每个帧都必须再次旋转以匹配运动。

在许多情况下，旋转需要将对象分成多个部分并为每个部分绘制形状。所有这些形状都必须重新定位，以跟踪对象在每一帧中的进展。

“如果你有一个长着金色长发的演员，他们在空中翻转与机器人战斗，你需要旋转每根头发，”长期视觉效果艺术家 Jason Gottlieb 说。 “这是最糟糕的。”

也许这就是为什么动态观察经常落在初级员工身上的原因。 Territory Studio 的创始人兼创意总监 Marti Romances 回忆起 20 年前的经历。

“我当时希望，我可以做其他事情来教会我更多关于创造力的事情，而不是在职业生涯的前两年做这些乏味的事情，”他说。

由于所有镜头都不同，专家们不愿对动态描画所涉及的成本和时间进行概括。

据估计，一个人可能会花一周的时间来动态观察一个复杂的五秒镜头。复杂的一分钟场景的 Roto 成本可能高达 75,000 美元。

事实上，在如此多的进步被归入人工智能这一总称之前，多年来，各种形式的机器学习一直在协助电影制作中最艰苦的部分。

在《沙丘：第二部分》（2024 年）中，机器学习工具被用来定位弗雷曼人的所有眼球，并将它们涂成光芒四射的蓝色。几年前制作《沙丘：第一部分》时，这项工作是通过无数个小时的手动动态描画完成的。

就在今年，包括 Adob​​e 和 Foundry 在内的公司发布了工具，只需人类点击一下，就可以找到物体并跟踪它们周围的情况。他们还可以确保对象及其形状在帧之间同步移动。

结果很少是完美的。但只需进行一些人工指导的调整，它们通常就可以实现。总部位于伦敦的创意软件开发商 Foundry 估计，其 SmartRoto 工具可以将 roto 流程加快四倍。

任何预算比《沙丘》系列电影更少的电影制片人都可以求助于生成式人工智能。工具，往往更便宜且更容易获得。需要将分散注意力的电线移出场景吗？生成式人工智能可以做到这一点。但结果往往显得有点模糊，就像视频通话虚拟背景下的身体一样。视觉艺术家说，有点模糊，在大屏幕上看起来很模糊。

“每个人都想要一个神奇的按钮，”Foundry 的创意总监胡安·萨拉查 (Juan Salazar) 说。 “那个按钮不存在。”

使用人工智能的另一个问题是旋转之谜一直在好莱坞以外的许多行业引起担忧，为了解决这个谜题，工人会发生什么？

事实证明，由于长期以来旋转加工成本高昂且属于劳动密集型，因此绝大多数工作岗位已经转移到成本低于美国的印度。

一些留在美国的艺术家希望人工智能带来的效率提高。不会简单地让他们失业，而是让他们有时间从事更有意义的电影制作任务。

希望还存在于那些尝试人工智能的公司。仍然需要训练有素的艺术家来清理大多数模型通常产生的不合格内容。模糊的轮廓不会赢得奥斯卡奖。

尽管如此，许多在该行业工作的人仍然对人工智能似乎不可避免地走向控制权感到苦恼，甚至愤怒。其他人的态度则更为矛盾，他们指出新技术常常被夸大。

“人工智能是一种工具，但仅此而已，”长期视觉效果艺术家 Maggie Kraisamutr 说。 “它并不能取代正在创造艺术的人类。”

每个人都在问这个问题，这种情况还能持续多久。

article_content_zh:
政府和国家网络机构保护人民、公共服务和经济所依赖的系统。通过 Daybreak，我们将先进的人工智能交给值得信赖的防御者来执行授权的安全工作，从审查软件和调查可疑活动到验证漏洞以及开发和测试修复程序。

OpenAI 与北约通信和信息局 (NCIA) 合作，为北约核心机构提供先进的网络安全模型，帮助保护盟军网络。作为这项工作的一部分，北约每月使用多达 3000 亿个原始输入和输出代币。

北约对 OpenAI 工具的早期使用表明，有能力的网络防御者如何将前沿模型付诸实践，支持北约维护其成员国自由和安全的使命。它还有助于加强负责全天候保护盟军网络的跨国团队的网络专业知识，并创造有益于整个欧洲和更广泛联盟的防御者的经验教训。

OpenAI 还支持（在新窗口中打开）2026 年交叉剑演习。该演习由北约合作网络防御卓越中心 (CCDCOE) 组织，包括一个新的培训流程，参与者在技术环境中使用 OpenAI Daybreak 构建、部署和评估用于网络作战的人工智能代理。培训将参与者与人工智能代理一起作为操作员，重点是维持人类监督。

OpenAI 仍然完全致力于北约负责任地采用人工智能的原则，并提供安全可靠的解决方案。

除了北约之外，我们已经向欧洲的防御者提供了对我们网络模型的访问，包括欧盟的 ENISA 以及法国 (ANSSI)、德国和波兰的国家网络机构。

乌克兰数字化转型部正在使用 OpenAI 的 Daybreak 工具来加强民用基础设施的网络防御。该计划旨在帮助乌克兰团队更快地识别软件漏洞并开发和测试修复程序，从而支持防御者在持续的网络攻击中保护基本服务。

欧盟网络机构 ENISA 使用我们的模型识别了欧盟机构使用的软件中的四个漏洞，并针对所有四个漏洞发布了修复程序（1（在新窗口中打开）、（在新窗口中打开）2（在新窗口中打开）、（在新窗口中打开）3（在新窗口中打开）、（在新窗口中打开）4（在新窗口中打开））。 ENISA 和 CERT-EU（在新窗口中打开）11 月（在新窗口中打开）的联合报告还描述了对使用前沿模型（包括通过 Daybreak 访问的 OpenAI 模型）和 Codex 安全插件等工具的 27 个软件项目的审查。在测试的模型中，软件维护人员评估的 88 个潜在问题中有 95% 被确认为真实问题，这证明了人工智能与人类专业知识相结合的价值。

CERT Polska 使用 OpenAI 模型帮助识别 MikroTik RouterOS（在新窗口中打开）中的六个漏洞，并与供应商协调披露。研究人员指导了这项工作，在真实系统上测试了结果并验证了其影响，人工智能加速了分析和潜在漏洞的探索。 MikroTik 发布了修复程序，CERT Polska 确认修复程序阻止了其观察到的攻击，为网络运营商提供了保护受影响设备的具体方法。

我们将继续与政府、国家网络机构和国际合作伙伴合作，将前沿人工智能能力转变为更强大、更安全、更有弹性的系统，帮助防御者发现弱点，更快地修复它们，并保护人们每天依赖的服务。
article_content:
Governments and national cyber agencies protect the systems that people, public services and economies depend on. Through Daybreak, we’re putting advanced AI into the hands of trusted defenders for authorized security work, from reviewing software and investigating suspicious activity to validating vulnerabilities, and developing and testing fixes.

OpenAI works with NATO’s Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) to provide NATO’s core institutions with access to advanced cybersecurity models, helping protect Allied networks. NATO has used up to 300 billion raw input and output tokens per month as part of this work.

NATO’s early use of OpenAI tools shows how capable cyber defenders can put frontier models to work, supporting NATO’s mission of safeguarding the freedom and security of its member states. It also helps strengthen cyber expertise across multinational teams responsible for protecting Allied networks around the clock, and creates lessons that can benefit defenders across Europe and the broader Alliance.

OpenAI also supported (opens in a new window) the 2026 Crossed Swords exercise. Organized by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE), the exercise included a new training stream in which participants built, deployed, and evaluated AI agents for cyber operations, using OpenAI Daybreak in the technical environment. The training put participants alongside AI agents as operators, with an emphasis on maintaining human oversight.

OpenAI remains fully committed to NATO’s principles for responsible AI adoption and to delivering solutions that are safe and secure.

Beyond NATO, we have already provided access to our cyber models to defenders in Europe, including the EU’s ENISA and national cyber agencies in France (ANSSI), Germany and Poland.

The Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine is using OpenAI’s Daybreak tool to strengthen the cyber defence of civilian infrastructure. The initiative is designed to help Ukrainian teams identify software vulnerabilities and develop and test fixes more quickly, supporting defenders who protect essential services amid persistent cyber attacks.

The EU’s cyber agency, ENISA, used our models to identify four vulnerabilities in software used across EU institutions, with fixes published for all four (1 (opens in a new window), (opens in a new window)2 (opens in a new window), (opens in a new window)3 (opens in a new window), (opens in a new window)4 (opens in a new window)). A November (opens in a new window)joint report from ENISA and CERT-EU (opens in a new window) also describes a review of 27 software projects using frontier models including OpenAI models accessed through Daybreak, and tools including the Codex security plug-in. Across the models tested, 95% of the 88 potential issues assessed by software maintainers were confirmed as genuine, demonstrating the value of combining AI with human expertise.

CERT Polska used OpenAI models to help identify six vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS (opens in a new window) and coordinated their disclosure with the vendor. Researchers directed the work, tested findings on real systems and verified their impact, with AI accelerating analysis and the exploration of potential vulnerabilities. MikroTik released fixes, which CERT Polska confirmed prevented the attacks it had observed, giving network operators a concrete way to protect affected devices.

We will continue working with governments, national cyber agencies and international partners to turn frontier AI capability into stronger, safer, more resilient systems, helping defenders find weaknesses, fix them faster and protect the services people rely on every day.

article_content:
Model ML landed $250 million in a Series B round at a $1.5 billion valuation.

It designs AI agents that handle routine tasks for bankers, consultants, and investors.

The new funding will go into research, engineering, and larger customer deployments.

Go to any junior banker and ask him or her where the week went, and you’ll hear the same answer. Pitch decks and diligence memos. Time spent in font work and double-checking numbers. It’s clever people doing things that should be done by a machine.

Model ML raises $250 million at a $1.5 billion valuation to solve this problem. The startup develops AI agents for bankers, consultants, and investors, reducing the time spent on spreadsheets, slide decks, and late-night email threads.

General Atlantic and QED Investors co-led the round, the company said in a statement on Tuesday. Other investors included Evolution Equity Partners, Airtree, Forestay Capital, Y Combinator, Latitude, Inception Fund, and 13Books Capital.

Model ML’s Series B at $250M is more than 3x larger than its $75M Series A just a year ago. Nigel Morris of QED summed it up in a single statement, noting that he hadn’t seen a team grow quicker. To say that at such an early age in the company’s history is quite a statement.

Model ML works like a virtual partner for all bankers. The firm designs personal AI agents that get to know its users’ clients, deals, processes, and output. The more you use them, the better they will get.

They are also at work behind the scenes. The agents operate within the system already existing in the business and monitor for pertinent news. They then decide what is important and draft completed reports, such as an analysis of a company that a banker writes about.

The company claims it can reduce a task from days to minutes. Banks are extremely conscious about security and they are correct. It can be deployed on any infrastructure, keeping the data on the same servers the companies use.

Model ML states that customer information is not used for AI model training. Chaz and Arnie Englander are the brothers behind this startup. Chaz is the CEO. The two founded a small family office after selling previous startups, they said.

Pitches were still coming in, but they wanted to do a better job of filtering out founders and reducing each business to a one-pager, so they created software to do just that. So they decided that they were better builders than investors.

In the third quarter, the company reported annual recurring revenue had increased by 12x and daily active users increased by 26x from last year. These are company numbers, not audited. Nonetheless, they suggest actual demand.

The massive demand suggests that investors are hoping that AI agents will be able to perform tedious and mundane tasks, rather than just answering questions. Banking is a natural test! The work is repetitive, voluminous, and costly.

The new cash will support London and New York research and engineering teams, more product development and bigger customer deployments. This year Model ML has also set up offices in Paris, Madrid, Tokyo, Singapore and Dubai.

If you’re in the finance, consulting, or investing business, Model ML wants to take away the mundane stuff first. Think about what you would delegate if you had to do so tomorrow. Then see if large companies employ agents for the second stage of the work.

content_snippet: Nearly 1 in 3 of more than 350 products Amazon advertised as deals during recent Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales provided no savings at all.
summary_en: An analysis of over 350 Amazon holiday deals by Groundwork Collaborative found that 29.1% were priced higher or unchanged compared to the previous 30 days, while nearly 60% showed no savings compared to the prior 90-day period. ai_analysis.insight_zh: 电商促销季的“伪折扣”已成为平台定价算法追求利润最大化的标配手段。这一趋势反映了电商生态已进入基于动态数据博弈的零和博弈期，消费者不仅难以通过促销获得真实实惠，反而正成为平台算法诱导消费的核心对象。

title: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State
title_en: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State

inline_images.caption: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State

author: Lingling Wei
article_content:
China's push to strengthen its AI capabilities involved two separate efforts allegedly linked to Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation. While Kang expanded a network of data centres backed by the Chinese government, Alice reportedly built a close, romantic relationship with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang. The report claims she also helped create a channel for accessing Nvidia's advanced computing chips, several of which Washington has sought to prevent from reaching China. Together, their activities allegedly supported China's ambition to gain an edge over the US in artificial intelligence.

Kang Wei's business interests in China grew into a major data-centre operation, with projects worth more than $9 billion proposed between 2021 and 2024, a review of Chinese public records by the Wall Street Journal found. These ventures had financial backing from government-linked investors and were promoted as part of China's plan to build more computing infrastructure. The findings offer a closer look at Kang's previously unreported involvement in China's AI expansion, at a time when the US is trying to limit China's access to advanced computing technology.

Kang's entry into the sector began in 2021 through Century Longteng, a Shanghai-based company backed by both private investors and a local government body. He later joined its leadership and helped steer its expansion into data centres. One of its early major partnerships was with Huawei in 2022, covering cloud computing, energy systems and data-centre infrastructure. The company then announced plans for a massive computing park in Wuhu, with an estimated investment of $4.5 billion. The development was designed to include eight buildings and space for roughly 24,000 server racks. A separate project worth around $5 billion was announced in Sichuan in 2024.

As Kang pursued data-centre projects in China, his wife Alice Huang was working on a separate business front involving Nvidia chips. Her company, Megaspeed, reportedly told Nvidia in November 2023 that Alibaba would be a major customer. It subsequently received cloud partner status, which offered it priority access to Nvidia processors. The WSJ has reported that some of the chips obtained by Megaspeed were later sent to China. However, there is no public evidence establishing that the Chinese government directed these purchases or that the processors were used in Kang's data centres. Alice was also reportedly in a romantic relationship with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang, whom Kang had known since their time in the video game industry.

The couple's business activities have since come under scrutiny. Singapore began investigating Megaspeed and several individuals in February 2025 over suspected false declarations related to server purchases. While authorities said there was not enough evidence to establish domestic criminal offences, Alice received a formal warning and was barred from entering Singapore. The investigation involving Megaspeed and six other people is still ongoing. Separately, Kang was detained in Shanghai earlier this year in connection with a stock-market manipulation inquiry, according to the WSJ, but has since been released. Megaspeed has defended its operations as legitimate and lawful and said Alice no longer works with the company.

article_content_zh:
康在中国政府的支持下扩大了数据中心网络，而爱丽丝则与英伟达时任首席执行官黄仁勋建立了密切的浪漫关系。该报告称，她还帮助创建了一个获取英伟达先进计算芯片的渠道，华盛顿一直试图阻止其中一些芯片进入中国。据称，他们的活动共同支持了中国在人工智能领域超越美国的雄心。

《华尔街日报》对中国公共记录的审查发现，康伟在中国的商业利益已发展成为一项重要的数据中心业务，在 2021 年至 2024 年间提出的项目价值超过 90 亿美元。这些企业得到了与政府相关的投资者的财政支持，并作为中国建设更多计算基础设施计划的一部分得到推广。在美国试图限制中国获得先进计算技术之际，这些调查结果让我们更仔细地了解了康此前未报道的参与中国人工智能扩张的情况。

Alice Huang 的丈夫在中国政府的支持下建立了价值 90 亿美元的数据中心帝国 虽然 Alice Huang 获得了 Nvidia 先进人工智能芯片的使用权，但她的丈夫正在中国各地建立一个由政府支持的计算基础设施组成的庞大网络。 《华尔街日报》由 Lingling Wei 进行的一项新调查揭示了 Nvidia 与 Megaspeed 争议的另一个方面：Alice Huang 的丈夫 Kang Wei 建立的广泛商业网络及其与中国国家支持的人工智能雄心的联系。根据《华尔街日报》查阅的中国证券备案文件和政府公告，在中国政府实体的支持下，2021 年至 2024 年间与康的数据中心网络相关的拟议投资超过 90 亿美元。该网络的核心是世纪龙腾，据报道，该公司的股权结构包括上海一家政府实体持有 10% 的股份，康氏投资网络持有 27% 的股份，深圳上市公司世纪华通持有 63% 的股份。 2022年，世纪龙腾与受美国出口限制的中国科技巨头华为签署合作协议，涵盖云数据中心、能源基础设施、计算能力等领域。康的网络随后开展了几个大型项目： 安徽芜湖：拟议耗资 45 亿美元的开发项目，包括八座数据中心大楼和约 24,000 个服务器机架，并得到当地政府对电力和基础设施的支持。四川凉山：另一个拟议的数据中心开发项目价值约 50 亿美元，将于 2024 年启动。深圳：公司备案中记录了更多数据中心参与情况。这些项目与北京国家“东数据、西计算”倡议相一致，旨在扩大和重新分配中国各地的计算能力。与此同时，Alice Huang 的新加坡公司 Megaspeed 于 2023 年成为 Nvidia 云合作伙伴，获得了先进人工智能芯片的优先使用权。阿里巴巴被认定为主要客户。 《华尔街日报》此前报道称，Megaspeed 收购的至少部分 Nvidia 芯片被运往中国。更令人担忧的是，据报道，康和爱丽丝向潜在投资者推销上海和东南亚的数据中心项目，同时声称他们可以将英伟达芯片引入中国。这提出了一个比黄仁勋与黄爱丽丝的个人关系更大的问题。美国最先进的人工智能硬件如何与中国政府支持的价值数十亿美元的计算基础设施网络相结合？重要的是，《华尔街日报》承认，现有的公共记录并不能证明北京指导了 Megaspeed 的芯片采购，也不能证明这些芯片最终到达了康的数据中心。这些联系尚未得到证实，需要进一步调查。但更广泛的国家安全影响不容忽视。当华盛顿试图限制中国获得先进的人工智能计算能力时，一对夫妇在技术鸿沟的两边进行操作：其中一方拥有进入英伟达芯片生态系统的特权采购渠道，并与其时任首席执行官有私人关系。另一个是在中国政府的支持下开发价值数十亿美元的计算基础设施。这种安排是如何发展的，谁知道这一点，以及采取了哪些保障措施来防止美国技术加强中国的军事和战略人工智能能力？这不再只是一个关于首席执行官的浪漫丑闻的故事。这是一个关于出口管制、企业责任以及美国技术领先地位与中国国家支持的人工智能雄心的潜在交集的故事。它需要答案。

康于 2021 年通过世纪龙腾进入该行业，这是一家总部位于上海的公司，得到了私人投资者和地方政府机构的支持。后来他加入了该公司的领导层，并帮助引导该公司向数据中心扩张。其早期的主要合作伙伴之一是 2022 年与华为建立的合作伙伴关系，涵盖云计算、能源系统和数据中心基础设施。该公司随后宣布计划在芜湖建设一个大型计算园区，预计投资 45 亿美元。该开发项目包括八栋建筑和可容纳约 24,000 个服务器机架的空间。 2024 年，四川宣布了一个价值约 50 亿美元的单独项目。

当康在中国开展数据中心项目时，他的妻子爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 正在从事涉及 Nvidia 芯片的独立业务。据报道，她的公司 Megaspeed 在 2023 年 11 月告诉 Nvidia，阿里巴巴将成为其主要客户。随后它获得了云合作伙伴地位，这使其能够优先使用 Nvidia 处理器。据《华尔街日报》报道，Megaspeed 获得的部分芯片后来被运往中国。然而，没有公开证据证明中国政府指导了这些采购，或者这些处理器被用于康的数据中心。据报道，爱丽丝还与英伟达时任首席执行官黄仁勋保持着恋爱关系，康从电子游戏行业就认识了黄仁勋。

此后，这对夫妇的商业活动受到密切关注。新加坡于 2025 年 2 月开始调查 Megaspeed 和数名个人涉嫌与服务器购买相关的虚假声明。虽然当局表示没有足够的证据证明她犯有国内刑事犯罪，但爱丽丝还是收到了正式警告，并被禁止进入新加坡。涉及 Megaspeed 和其他六人的调查仍在进行中。据《华尔街日报》报道，康今年早些时候因涉嫌股市操纵调查而在上海被拘留，但后来被释放。 Megaspeed 捍卫其运营合法合法，并表示 Alice 不再与该公司合作。

title: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward
title_en: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Electronics Mobile Phone Phone and Iphone
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Electronics Mobile Phone Phone and Iphone

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Electronics Mobile Phone and Phone
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Electronics Mobile Phone and Phone

author: Julian Chokkattu
article_content:
My wife and I were driving back from a date night. She was talking about a friend's very expensive utility bill, but I had missed the beginning of what she said (I was driving, after all).

Then I remembered: Wait, I can ask Siri to remind me! At a traffic light, I double-tapped the digital crown on the Apple Watch, and Siri's new Live Rewind feature spun back the clock 15 seconds and showed me a transcript of what my wife said.

I sheepishly interrupted her to show her the transcript. “Look!” Her reply? “Why wouldn't you just ask me to repeat myself?” She shrugged at this new Apple Watch capability and continued talking.

A few days later, I was chatting with my brother on my stoop. Once again, I lost focus for a few seconds and remembered to ask Siri to help me recall what my brother said moments ago. But this time, before I excitedly showed my brother the Apple Watch screen, I preemptively said, “Yeah, I know I could just ask you to repeat yourself.” I got a perplexed look back.

Live Rewind, one of Apple's new Audio Intelligence features on its latest Apple Watches, is designed to give you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. It's in public beta in watchOS 27.3, but is expected to launch officially before the year's end.

Coming alongside it is another new capability called Siri Recap: Give the assistant permission to listen to your environment—you can set schedules or have it trigger when you reach the office—and you'll see a “Recap” in the Siri app at the end of the day. It’ll show you summaries of conversations and list out important details that people said. It's very similar to AI notetakers, many of which run on dedicated hardware devices.

The power here is that it all happens on your Apple Watch, the same device you wear everywhere to track your fitness, monitor health, and check notifications. That ubiquity is exactly what makes privacy advocates uneasy—they say features like these normalize ambient surveillance, much like smart glasses, undermining the privacy of bystanders who don't consent to being recorded.

“One of the concerns that we have with things like the Apple Watch is we don't know what the watch is picking up on,” Reem Suleiman, senior campaign director at the nonprofit digital rights advocacy group Fight for the Future, tells WIRED. “Just because the device wearer is the one opting in to use the feature, you're not getting consent from everybody who you walk around.”

Apple has spent a great deal of effort explaining how the system works and how the company plans to maintain the privacy of its users and the people around them. First, these features are opt-in, and they are limited to the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4. They also require an iPhone 16 or newer with iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence. These features are not available for users under 18, and they currently work only in English.

For Live Rewind, the audio is processed on-device and cannot be accessed. When you activate it, a small chime plays from the Apple Watch that serves as a warning for folks nearby. Text disappears unless you choose to save it to Siri. For Recaps, Siri keeps them factual, doesn't identify speakers, and also omits content the system deems sensitive. If you don't save a Recap, it'll self-delete in seven days. Apple uses its Private Cloud Compute processing system for the data, which is never stored or logged on its servers. Data stored in the Siri app is end-to-end encrypted when syncing with iCloud.

Siri Recaps are stored in the Siri app and will self-delete in seven days if you do not save them.

Even if you're happy with Apple's privacy focus, I haven't found these capabilities tremendously useful over the past week. Live Rewind works well in moderately quiet environments, but the transcript can quickly turn into inaccurate gibberish when there's a lot of background noise.

Activating it in front of the person you're chatting with feels awkward. It comes across like pulling out your smartphone when someone's trying to talk to you—a little rude and distracting. Instead of keeping screens out of sight—a big digital detox trend—you're introducing one in the middle of a human conversation. I brought the topic up with my wife again, and she echoed some of those feelings, saying it felt like a feature that would stunt a person's social skills. Instead of asking someone to repeat themself, they're bringing an Apple Watch into the mix to fill in the gaps.

I am not saying it can't be helpful. When it works, it feels like a superpower. Maybe there are certain situations where you don't want to interrupt a group conversation and ask someone to repeat themself. Right now, though, there's the problem of remembering that this feature exists and remembering to use it. I have also found the 15-second rule a little too short, and it resulted in me missing parts of the conversation.

Recap has been a little more helpful. For testing purposes, I've set Siri to capture recaps all day, every day, but I like that you can create a custom schedule or have it trigger when you arrive at a specific location, like the office. You can manually turn Siri Recap on or off in the Apple Watch's Control Center. Most impressive is that, despite having Recap enabled constantly, I haven't seen a meaningful dip in battery life. I've continued charging the Apple Watch Series 12 after a day and a half.

Siri Recap logs summaries of ambient conversations.

One of the more perplexing things was opening the Siri app to look at my recaps and finding a bunch of conversations I had no recollection of having. Turns out, Siri was recording media I was watching, like on YouTube or Instagram. This is a problem I encountered with AI notetakers, like the Amazon-owned Bee AI wearable, which claimed to be working on “liveness detection” to solve it. Its latest hardware shipped with a feature where it doesn't record a conversation if it doesn't detect the wearer's voice within a set period. Hopefully, Apple can figure out a solution. For now, you can edit or delete these recaps.

One day, I forgot to record an interview (though I took notes), and I knew the person said something that I hadn't written down. I headed over to Siri and found exactly what I was looking for—paraphrased, but there. That said, the Recaps aren't designed to be detailed summaries and action plans from your meetings or conversations, unlike dedicated AI notetakers. They're meant to jog your memory. At times, I wish Siri were more detailed, but if that's what you're after, you'll have to invest in a third-party device.

Recap can be helpful for work meetings, but I haven't personally found it all that compelling in my personal life. Looking back at what it has picked up over conversations with friends and family, the only thing I feel is: Yep, those conversations happened. A friend was talking about their woodworking hobby—they can't use oil-based polyurethane as a finish in the winter months as it stays tacky. Siri logged this in such a matter-of-fact way, but when I revisited the conversation in the recap, I didn't find it helpful, useful, or interesting. (No offense, friend!) It's just nuggets of life.

Apple has pulled off impressive feats with these features, capturing these moments in a way that feels a little more privacy-preserving than competitors, without tanking the already limited battery life of its smartwatches. But socially, we're still figuring out what it means to walk around with always-on passive recorders. For now, I'm happy to stick with my wife's advice and ask: “Come again?”
